question: Does Leona Zealot's -8 might effect apply as a constant aura or as a one-time snapshot? If a stunned unit at 1 might (after Leona's effect) receives +2 might, does it go to 3 might or stay at 1?
answer:
Ruling: Leona Zealot's -8 might effect is a passive aura that continuously applies. If you buff a unit after Leona's effect reduces it to minimum 1 might, the buff will increase the might above 1.

Sequence:

Leona's passive effect reduces stunned enemy might by -8 to a minimum of 1

This continues to apply as long as the conditions are met

Any subsequent buffs are added on top of this ongoing effect

A 2 might unit reduced to 1, then given +2 might, would be at 3 might

Nuances:

If the effect said "when you stun an enemy here, give it -8m to a minimum of 1m" it would snapshot like Smoke Screen instead of being continuous

The current wording makes it an aura-type effect rather than a one-time modification

question: Can you play Stupefy in response to Void Seeker during a Dreaming Tree conquest showdown, draw cards from Stupefy's resolution, and then play Defy from those drawn cards to counter the Void Seeker?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Stupefy in response to Void Seeker, and after Stupefy resolves and you draw cards, you gain priority again before Void Seeker resolves, allowing you to play Defy if you drew it.

Sequence:

Dreaming Tree trigger resolves

Opponent plays Void Seeker

You react with Stupefy, then pass

Opponent passes and chain begins resolving

Stupefy resolves (unit gets -1, you draw cards)

Opponent (who owns the next item, Void Seeker) gets priority and passes

You can now play Defy to counter Void Seeker

Nuances:

Each time an item on the chain resolves, there's a priority window again, starting with the player who owns the next item on the chain

The Dreaming Tree trigger resolves before Stupefy in this sequence

question: Does Sett the Boss's protection effect prevent lethal spell damage (like from Void Seeker), or does it only work against combat damage?
answer:
Ruling: Sett's protection effect prevents lethal damage from spells like Void Seeker, not just combat damage.

Nuances:

The asker initially thought Sett only protected against combat damage, but this was incorrect

question: When Leona Legend's ability triggers during a showdown after a chain resolves, does it create a new chain, is it still a showdown, and can players respond with action cards or only reactions?
answer:
Ruling: Leona Legend's triggered ability creates a new chain that can be responded to with reactions. Showdowns do not end when a chain resolves - both players must pass focus in sequence before a showdown ends.

Sequence:

Rune Prison resolves on the initial showdown chain, stunning the attacker

The chain ends

Leona Legend triggers and creates a new chain

Players can respond to this new chain with reactions

Both players must pass focus in sequence for the showdown to end

Nuances:

Players are limited to reactions when responding to the new chain during the showdown, not action cards like Hextech Ray

question: Does Ravenbloom get +1 for each instance when you repeat it, and what happens if you repeat and complete the effect twice but the opponent defies it on the 3rd attempt?
answer:
Ruling: Repeat adds additional effects to a spell rather than playing a whole new one, so it's only one instance on the chain. You can only repeat once.

Nuances:

The complete rules for repeat interactions are not yet available in the current ruleset, so some edge cases remain unclear until updated rules are released.

question: In a showdown, if my opponent casts Hexray (deal 3 damage) and then reacts to their own spell with Smokescreen (reduce might by 4), how does priority work?
answer:
Ruling: The player who cast Hexray retains priority after casting it and can immediately react with Smokescreen on the same chain. Then both players pass priority, Smokescreen resolves first, then Hexray resolves.

Sequence:

Player A plays Hexray

Player A retains priority and plays Smokescreen (reacting to Hexray)

Player A passes

Player B passes

Smokescreen resolves

Player A passes

Player B passes

Hexray resolves

Nuances:

It would also work if they played Smokescreen after Hexray resolved as a separate chain, though this would allow the opponent to play an action in between

When a chain fully resolves, focus and priority automatically pass to the player who did NOT play the last action

question: Does a unit with 0 Might die, or does it need damage marked on it to be killed?
answer:
Ruling: A unit can have 0 Might and survive on the board. It needs damage marked on it equal to or exceeding its Might to be killed.

Nuances:

A unit's Might cannot go below 0; if it would, it is treated as 0 for all purposes

In Set 2, many Might reduction effects no longer have the minimum limit of 1

The limit of 1 Might in earlier versions was mainly to avoid corner cases at the start

question: Can you activate a gear ability that buffs an exhausted unit during a showdown after playing a unit that becomes exhausted from moving to an occupied battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot use gear abilities during a showdown unless they have the "action" or "reaction" keywords.

Sequence:

Activated abilities on gears, units, and legends can only be used outside of a showdown during your turn by default

Abilities with the "action" keyword can be used during a showdown when there's no chain

Abilities with the "reaction" keyword can be used whenever a reaction spell can be used

Nuances:

The same rules apply to spells as well as gear abilities

question: If a unit is removed from the battlefield in response to Hidden Blade targeting it, does Hidden Blade still resolve and does its controller draw 2 cards?
answer:
Ruling: When Hidden Blade resolves, it checks if the target is still legal (still at a battlefield). If the unit has been removed from the battlefield, Hidden Blade does not kill the unit and its controller does not draw 2 cards.

Nuances:

The draw 2 effect is not dependent on the unit dying, but it is dependent on the target being legal on resolution

If the unit is saved by a replacement effect but remains at the battlefield, you would still draw 2 because the unit is still at a battlefield

question: Does Master Yi's legendary defender +2 ability apply when Yasuo uses his ability against a defender?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Master Yi's +2 applies when he is the defender and is alone. The +2 is a passive ability that is active at all times when the unit has defender designation.

Sequence:

Master Yi must be designated as a defender

Master Yi must be alone

The +2 is then active during Yasuo's ability resolution

Nuances:

The +2 only applies if Master Yi is alone

question: When Ravenbloom Student (which gains +1 Might when you play a spell) is targeted by Falling Star, does the Student get the +1 Might before taking damage?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ravenbloom Student gets +1 Might before taking damage from Falling Star.

Sequence:

Falling Star is played, triggering Student's ability to gain +1 Might

Falling Star resolves by adding two damage effects to the chain (using a reflexive trigger)

Student gains the +1 Might

The two damage effects resolve

Nuances:

The two damage effects created by Falling Star's reflexive trigger do not count as spells themselves

However, the damage from these effects still counts as being dealt by a spell (a specific exception for damage)

question: When defending with Master Yi's +2 might bonus and playing a Challenge Action spell during a showdown, does Challenge count only the unit's base might or does it include the defending bonuses?
answer:
Ruling: The might increase from defending bonuses counts. The unit has the increased might while the showdown is ongoing, so Challenge uses that total might.

Nuances:

The +2 from Master Yi is technically not a "buff" in game terminology, though it functions as a might increase during defense

question: Can you decline to pay deflect costs on mandatory triggered abilities, and does this allow you to skip the ability entirely?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can decline to pay deflect costs even on mandatory triggered abilities. When you decline to pay in step 4, the entire ability fails to enter the chain, effectively skipping it.

Sequence:

Choose targets for the mandatory triggered ability (including units with deflect)

In step 4, decline to pay the deflect cost

The entire ability fails to enter the chain

Continue playing the card as if the trigger never happened

Nuances:

This works even when other legal targets without deflect are available - you can choose the deflect target and then decline

No reaction window occurs during this process

If an ability has multiple parts (like damage + another effect), declining deflect causes the entire ability to fail, not just the deflect portion

question: Can Mistfall be used on an opponent's turn if Stand United is used as a reaction on the opponent's turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Mistfall can be used on an opponent's turn. Mistfall is a triggered ability that activates any time a friendly unit is buffed, regardless of whose turn it is.

Nuances:

Mistfall does not need to say "reaction" to be used on an opponent's turn; it triggers automatically whenever its condition (buffing a friendly unit) is met

Stand United can buff during an opponent's turn as a reaction, which would trigger Mistfall

question: Can Defy counter Yasuo, Remorseful's triggered ability?
answer:
Ruling: No, Defy cannot counter Yasuo's triggered ability. Defy can only counter spells, and Yasuo's trigger is an ability, not a spell.

Nuances:

Defy specifically says "counter a spell" and not "counter a spell or ability"

Cards like Not So Fast have different text that would allow them to counter abilities

question: If a buffed unit is reduced to 1 might by Smoke Screen, then an opponent tries to use Call to Glory by removing the buff as payment (which would temporarily make the unit 0 might), does the unit die before Call to Glory resolves?
answer:
Ruling: The unit does not die from having 0 might alone. Units only die if they have damage equal to or greater than their might.

Nuances:

Smoke Screen and other might reducers snapshot their effect once and are not continuous

You can have 0 might units in the game

Under current rules, cleanups don't happen before a spell resolves, so the opponent would need to add something else to the chain (like exhausting a rune) to trigger a cleanup that would kill a damaged unit at 0 might

Under updated rules, cleanups will happen more frequently and would resolve this situation differently

question: Can Yasuo with two Masks of Foresight move to an unattended battlefield for +2, use his Legend ability to return to base, then use Ride the Wind to move to another contested battlefield for another +2 (total might 8), then cast Last Breath to deal 8 damage before using Fight or Flight to save himself, and can the opponent use Reaver's Row defense ability to dodge the Last Breath damage?
answer:
Ruling: The initial movement sequence works as described, but at Reaver's Row, Yasuo is not an attacker during an open showdown, so Mask of Foresight bonuses don't apply. The opponent's defense trigger will go on the chain first, allowing them to potentially retreat before Yasuo's ability resolves.

Nuances:

Mask of Foresight only grants +1 might when you are an attacker, which doesn't apply in open showdowns

Defense abilities trigger and go on the chain before the attacking unit's abilities resolve, allowing the defender to potentially escape

question: Are there any overtime rules for official Riftbound events?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, when round time is called, players complete 5 more turns, and at the end of the 5th turn after time was called, the higher score wins (draw if tied).

Sequence:

Round time is called

Players complete 5 additional turns

At the end of the 5th turn, compare scores

Higher score wins; draw if scores are tied

question: When using Dazzling Aurora with Snapvine, does the opponent heal from Snapvine before or after Dazzling Aurora's damage resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Dazzling Aurora's damage resolves first, then healing from Snapvine happens after all ending abilities are complete.

Sequence:

Dazzling Aurora triggers and resolves at the start of end of turn

Once all ending abilities are fully resolved, healing occurs

The opponent heals after taking the damage from Dazzling Aurora

question: If you have enough points when you play Draven, does he count as Mighty for ramp triggers, or does he only become Mighty after he's in play?
answer:
Ruling: Draven counts as Mighty when played if you have enough points at that time, so he will trigger ramp effects.

Nuances:

The Mighty status is checked when Draven is played, not only after he enters play

question: When a showdown is triggered during the resolution of Promising Future (by playing Dragon's Rage and moving an enemy unit to an occupied battlefield), does the showdown happen immediately or after both players have played their cards from Promising Future?
answer:
Ruling: The showdown does not happen immediately. It becomes pending and will start once the chain is empty (after Promising Future is fully resolved and both players have played their chosen cards).

Sequence:

Both players choose cards from Promising Future

Both players play their chosen cards

Promising Future fully resolves

The chain becomes empty

The pending showdown then starts

question: If I use Icathian Rain to destroy a monster, can I summon 2 Phoenix with their effects from trash while Icathian Rain is resolving?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can summon Phoenix cards from trash while Icathian Rain is resolving. When any of Icathian Rain's damage triggers kills a unit, your Phoenixes will trigger and you can pay the cost to play them.

Sequence:

Icathian Rain resolves and puts 6 triggers on the chain, each dealing 2 damage to a unit

You choose all targets before the triggers resolve

Players have a window to react before each trigger resolves

When any trigger kills a unit, Phoenix effects trigger and you can pay the cost to play them

question: If I have two recruits and the opponent attacks with a single unit, will Imperial Decree trigger once or twice (does each recruit dealing damage count as a different event)?
answer:
Ruling: Imperial Decree will trigger only once. Damage is pooled together and then distributed, so all units take damage in a single event regardless of how many sources are dealing damage.

Nuances:

If you deal enough damage to kill a unit through Imperial Decree, you can kill it even through Zhonya's. Zhonya's would trigger and resolve first (exhausting, recalling, and healing the unit), but then Imperial Decree would still kill it afterward.

Having multiple recruits does not create multiple damage events for Imperial Decree purposes.

question: If a Recruit at Trifarian Warcamp is targeted by Stupefy, does its power return to 2 after Stupefy resolves due to Warcamp's passive ability?
answer:
Ruling: No, the unit remains a 1 power unit after Stupefy resolves.

Nuances:

Both Warcamp and Stupefy apply passively

This same principle applies to other buff scenarios

question: When multiple non-combat showdowns are triggered in sequence (e.g., Player A moves to Battlefield 1 triggering a showdown, then during that showdown Player B uses Ride the Wind to move to Battlefield 2), in what order do the showdowns resolve?
answer:
Ruling: The current showdown always resolves first before any newly triggered showdowns begin.

Sequence:

First showdown begins when Player A moves to Battlefield 1

During first showdown, Player B uses Ride the Wind to move to Battlefield 2

Second showdown is marked as pending

First showdown completes

Second showdown then begins and resolves

Nuances:

A showdown begins when control of a battlefield is contested and the turn is in a neutral open state

The rules may need clarification regarding pending non-combat showdowns for this circumstance

question: Does Udyr's effect trigger when his buff is spent by another card's effect (like Wildclaw Shaman)?
answer:
Ruling: No. Udyr's effect is an activated ability with the template "cost: effect" where spending his buff is the cost. You must directly activate his effect and spend the buff on him as a cost to get one of his four effects.

Nuances:

Effects that trigger whenever you spend a buff are phrased as "when you spend a buff" - Udyr does not have this wording

You cannot spend the same buff as the cost for multiple effects (e.g., spending Udyr's buff for both his effect and another card's effect like Monastery of Hirana)

Conquering a battlefield with a buffed Udyr does not automatically trigger his effect

question: When playing Promising Future while Brynhir's effect prevents the opponent from playing cards, what happens to the card chosen by Promising Future?
answer:
Ruling: This follows the "Do As Much As You Can" principle. The opponent chooses a card from Promising Future and it remains banished, since they cannot play it due to Brynhir's effect.

Sequence:

Resolve Promising Future normally

Opponent chooses a card to banish

The card remains banished (the step where opponent would play the card is skipped)

The card does not go to trash

Nuances:

Brynhir does not override Promising Future; both effects apply

All steps of Promising Future resolve except the opponent playing the banished card

question: Do triggered abilities like Riptide Rex provide a window to use Reactions on the targeted unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, all triggered abilities create a chain, allowing all relevant players to react.

Sequence:

Triggered ability goes on the chain

Players can respond with reactions before the triggered ability resolves

question: When a spell deals damage equal to a unit's might (e.g., 3 damage to a 3 might unit), can you use a reaction to boost the unit's might and prevent it from dying?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can respond with a reaction (like Discipline) to boost a unit's might and prevent it from dying when damage is assigned to it.

Nuances:

Units have only Might, not separate attack and health stats

A unit dies if it is assigned damage equal to or greater than its Might

"Buff" is a specific game object that gives +1 Might and stays until removed by a card effect

"Boost" refers to Might increases from non-Buff sources (like spells or abilities)

Most spell-based Might increases last until end of turn

Some abilities give conditional Might increases (e.g., while a unit is at a battlefield)

A unit can only hold one Buff at a time; attempting to Buff an already Buffed unit does nothing

question: For Convergent Mutation, if you copy stats from a creature with temporary buffs to another creature, does the copied creature keep those buffed stats after the original buff expires?
answer:
Ruling: No, the copied creature does not keep the buffed stats permanently. The card has a printing error and should read "until end of turn" according to the errata.

Nuances:

For competitive play, the errata always takes precedent over what is printed on the card

question: If a unit gains might from a spell for the turn, then dies and gets recalled, does it still have the added might after being recalled to base?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the unit retains the might buff after being recalled to base.

Nuances:

When a unit is recalled, it doesn't die or leave the field

Recall is not considered a move action

question: Can you flip Tideturner on Battlefield B to switch it with something on Battlefield A when someone is attacking Battlefield A?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can flip Tideturner on Battlefield B and switch it with something on Battlefield A, even when someone is attacking Battlefield A.

Nuances:

Tideturner's ability can be activated across different battlefields

Similarly, Zhonyas can be activated on Battlefield A to save a card on Battlefield B (when flipped, Zhonyas is recalled to your base)

question: How many actions and reactions can be played in a chain, and how does priority/focus work during showdowns?
answer:
Ruling: You can play multiple actions during a showdown by alternating focus - after a chain resolves, if your opponent passes focus and does nothing, you can play another action. You can play multiple reactions in succession by holding priority, but you cannot respond to an action with another action.

Sequence:

Player plays an action (starts a chain)

Opponent gets priority to react

If opponent passes, chain resolves

Focus returns to original player

Player can start a new chain with another action

Showdown only ends when both players pass on an empty chain

For reactions:

You can hold priority after playing a reaction to play additional reactions

Priority to play reactions only passes manually

You can react to your own cards to retain priority

Nuances:

You can never react to a chain with an action - the whole chain must resolve first

You can only play actions when you have focus or on your turn

Focus automatically passes to the opponent when a chain ends

question: Can you use Teemo Legend's ability to return a hidden Teemo card from the board?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot use Teemo Legend to return a hidden Teemo from the board. A hidden card is not identified as "Teemo" while it is facedown - it is simply a hidden card unless you play it first.

Nuances:

Hidden cards lose their card name identity while facedown

The card would need to be played/revealed first before it could be targeted as "Teemo"

question: Does the Possession card awaken (ready) an exhausted unit, or does it stay exhausted when moved to the enemy base?
answer:
Ruling: Possession does not ready the unit you're gaining control of. If it was already readied, it stays readied. If it was exhausted, it stays exhausted.

Nuances:

Some units have abilities that ready them (e.g., Darius readies when you cast a second spell), but that's not related to Possession itself

An exhausted unit's only restrictions are: you cannot exhaust it for costs/effects and you cannot move it with a Standard Move Action

If you use a spell or effect (like Ride the Wind, Yasuo Unforgiven, or Zenith Blade) to move an exhausted unit into a battlefield, it can still conquer

question: Can multiple ready units move simultaneously from base to an occupied battlefield and trigger a single showdown with combined might, or must they move one at a time with separate showdowns?
answer:
Ruling: Multiple units can move simultaneously to the same battlefield destination, and this triggers only a single showdown (not separate showdowns for each unit).

Sequence:

Multiple standard moves happen simultaneously if they share the same destination

All units arrive together

A single showdown occurs with the combined might of all units moved

question: If you play Mystic Reversal to steal an opponent's spell, does that spell count as played for Legion purposes?
answer:
Ruling: The player who played Mystic Reversal is considered to have played the stolen spell, not the original caster. Therefore, the opponent does not activate Legion effects from the stolen spell.

Sequence:

When a spell is put on the chain, it checks for cast triggers at that time

If control of the spell changes via Mystic Reversal before resolution, the player who controls it at resolution is the one who played it

A card is only considered "played" when it has finished resolving in its entirety

Since the Mystic Reversal player controls the spell when it resolves, they are the one who played it

Nuances:

This is different from countering a spell with Defy or similar effects, where the countered spell is not considered played at all

The original caster does not get Legion credit for a spell stolen by Mystic Reversal

question: Can you use Defy to counter Shen when played at reaction speed?
answer:
Ruling: No, Defy cannot target Shen. Shen is a unit, not a spell, and Defy can only target spells.

Nuances:

Even though Shen is played at reaction speed, it is still a unit card and therefore not a valid target for Defy

question: Do spells that reduce might (like Stupefy) bypass buffs, or do they take the buffed might value into account?
answer:
Ruling: Spells that reduce might take into account the current might of the unit from all sources, including buffs. A unit with 1 base might and a buff (giving +1 might for 2 total) that gets hit by Stupefy (-1 might to minimum 1) would end up at 1 might.

Nuances:

Buffs directly modify the might of the unit like any other might-modifying effect

All might modifications get bundled together when calculating the final value

The "minimum of 1 might" clause applies to the final result after all modifications are considered

question: If you use Deathgrip to kill an Immortal Phoenix, does the Phoenix see itself being killed and trigger its ability? Can you play the Phoenix from trash outside of normal timing (e.g., during a showdown)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Immortal Phoenix sees itself being killed by Deathgrip and triggers its ability. You can play the Phoenix from the trash outside of normal base speed timing.

Sequence:

When Deathgrip kills a unit (including Phoenix itself), the unit is sent to the trash immediately as part of the active kill action, not during cleanup

Phoenix's trigger condition is met (a spell killed a unit) while Phoenix is in the trash

You can pay the cost for Phoenix's trigger and replay it from the trash even during a showdown

Nuances:

This works similarly to Darius Trifarian seeing itself as the second spell played in a turn

Active kill actions (like Deathgrip) send units to trash immediately, unlike passive kill actions from damage which happen during cleanup

Example scenario: If defending with Phoenix + another unit, you can Deathgrip the Phoenix to boost the second unit, then replay Phoenix from trash to the same battlefield

question: For a card that says 'Target a gear. Its controller may kill it' then 'Draw 1' - do you need to kill the gear to draw, and can you play it without controlling a gear yourself?
answer:
Ruling: You can play the card as long as any player controls a gear (including your opponent's). You draw 1 card regardless of whether the gear is killed or not.

Sequence:

Target any gear (yours or opponent's) when playing the spell

The gear's controller chooses whether to kill it during resolution

Draw 1 card regardless of the choice made

Nuances:

You cannot play the card if no gears are on the battlefield at all

The draw effect is independent from the kill effect (separated by a full stop/period)

You can target your own gear and choose not to kill it, still drawing the card

question: Can Retreat target an opponent's unit, or does 'friendly unit' only mean the caster's own units?
answer:
Ruling: 'Friendly unit' refers only to your units or a teammate's units, not opponent units.

Nuances:

If you cast Retreat on an ally's unit, it returns to their hand and they channel 1

question: Are there any rules or changes to implement for playing Riftbound with 5 players to make it more balanced?
answer: No answer was provided in this thread. The original poster asked for suggestions but received no responses.

question: In 1v1 Riftbound, does the player going first skip their draw on the first turn?
answer:
Ruling: In 1v1 formats, all players draw a card during the draw phase of their turn, including the first turn. Only in multiplayer formats does the first player skip their first draw phase.

Nuances:

The multiplayer rule (first player skips first draw) does not apply to 1v1 formats

This is a format-specific rule difference between 1v1 and multiplayer

question: If a unit with 4 Might and a buff (making it 5 Might) is moved to a battlefield, the opponent reacts with Smokescreen (giving -4 Might), and then Sett's champion ability is used to spend the buff and recall the unit, will the unit survive as a 0 Might unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the unit will survive. A unit only dies when it has damage marked on it equal to or greater than its Might. Having 0 Might does not cause death if there is no damage marked on it.

Sequence:

Unit with 4 Might and a buff (5 Might total) moves to battlefield

Opponent uses Smokescreen, giving -4 Might (unit becomes 1 Might)

Sett's ability spends the buff and recalls the unit to base, healing it

Unit is now 0 Might (4 base Might - 4 from Smokescreen) with no damage marked

Unit survives because it has no damage marked on it

Nuances:

Smokescreen's -Might effect lasts until end of turn and is not removed by healing

Healing only removes damage, not -Might effects

Lethal damage requires a non-zero amount of damage marked on a unit

Future sets will have -Might cards without the minimum 1 Might limit, making this interaction more common

If a unit has damage marked equal to its Might, spending a buff that was increasing its Might would cause it to die

question: Do units defending Trifarian Warcamp get the might bonus outside of showdown and combat, such as for the purposes of cards like Gust or triggering Fiora's mighty abilities?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, units defending Trifarian Warcamp receive the might bonus at all times, not just during showdown and combat. This means the bonus applies for effects like Gust (which checks might to determine if a unit can be moved) and for triggering mighty-dependent abilities like Fiora's.

Nuances:

A 3 might unit on Trifarian Warcamp becomes 4 might and cannot be moved by Gust

Fiora on Trifarian Warcamp reaches 5 might, becomes mighty, and gains her additional deflect, flanking, and shield abilities

question: If Fading Memories targets a unit and Sett saves it with Sett's legend ability, does the unit keep the Temporary keyword and die again next turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the unit keeps the Temporary keyword even after being saved by Sett's legend ability.

Nuances:

The unit will die again at the end of the next turn due to retaining Temporary

question: If a player has only 4 cards in their main deck when resolving an effect that tells them to look at the top 5 cards (like Promising Future), does this trigger a burnout?
answer:
Ruling: No burnout is triggered. You only look at/reveal as many cards as are available in your deck (4 cards in this example). A burnout only occurs if the deck is completely empty when attempting to look/reveal cards.

Nuances:

When looking at or revealing cards, those cards remain in the deck (they don't move to another zone like drawing does)

Since the cards stay in the deck while being looked at, the deck is not considered empty during the look/reveal action

This means you cannot trigger a burnout mid-reveal unless your deck was already empty before starting the reveal

question: During a showdown, after a reaction is played to buff a unit, can an action card (like Hidden Blade) be played to kill the buffed unit, or must combat resolve first?
answer:
Ruling: Actions can only be played to start a new chain when a player has focus, not during an ongoing chain. During a showdown, focus passes back and forth between attacker and defender after each chain resolves, allowing either player to start a new chain with an action card until both players pass consecutively.

Sequence:

Attacker declares attack and gets focus first

If attacker passes, focus goes to defender

Defender plays a reaction (e.g., +2 might buff), starting a chain

Chain resolves completely

Focus returns to attacker, who can now play an action card (like Hidden Blade) to start a new chain

This continues until both players pass focus consecutively, then combat resolves

Nuances:

Actions cannot be played while a chain is ongoing (closed state)

Reactions are the exception and can be played during a chain

Hidden cards at the battlefield can be played at reaction speed as part of the Hidden mechanic

question: Does rule 352.14.b mean targets are chosen after finalization is complete, or during the finalization process?
answer:
Ruling: Targets are chosen during the finalization process, not after it is complete. The phrase "when the spell or ability is finalized" means "during the process of finalization."

Nuances:

The wording "when the spell is finalized" uses "when" synonymously with "while" or "during," not "after"

Interpreting it as "after" would break the order in weird ways because it would occur after the legality check

The wording could be clearer, especially for non-native English speakers, by using phrasing like "when the spell is being finalized" or "during the process of finalization"

question: After playing Hidden Blade on an enemy unit with Deathknell, who gets priority first after the Deathknell trigger finalizes?
answer:
Ruling: The player controlling the Deathknell effect gains priority, as they control the newest item on the chain after the trigger is finalized during cleanup.

Sequence:

Player A plays Hidden Blade and starts a chain

Chain finalizes and executes, both players pass

Chain resolves and Hidden Blade effect executes

Cleanup takes place upon removal of last item on the chain

Deathknell triggers on cleanup and is added to the chain

Deathknell is finalized within cleanup

Chain goes to step 1 and finalizes

Player controlling the Deathknell effect (newest in chain) gains priority

Nuances:

Finalizing does not modify priority in general, but when a new effect is added to the chain during cleanup, the controller of that newest effect gains priority

question: Does the deck language requirement apply to runes and battlefields, or only to the main deck?
answer:
Ruling: There is no explicit "same language" rule. The actual rule is that cards in a deck cannot be told apart without looking at them (e.g., by thickness or feel). This applies to cards within the same deck zone.

Nuances:

Chinese and English cards have differences in thickness and feel, so mixing them in the same deck zone would violate the rule

It's unclear whether runes need to match the main deck language, but as long as runes are all the same language as each other (and thus indistinguishable from one another), they would likely be acceptable even if different from the main deck language

No official ruling exists yet on cross-zone language mixing

question: Can showdowns start after a unit moves into a battlefield, including an empty one, and are there any other circumstances that would start a showdown?
answer:
Ruling: A showdown can be triggered by moving into a battlefield controlled by your opponent or by moving into an empty battlefield. Specifically, a showdown opens when a move causes a battlefield to become contested while it has no units present from any player other than those that just moved.

Sequences: N/A

Nuances:

The showdown occurs without combat when triggered by movement

The battlefield must become contested as a result of the move

Only applies when no other units are present besides those that just moved

question: Can Last Breath be used to ready a unit when the opponent doesn't have a unit to target for damage?
answer:
Ruling: No, Last Breath cannot be activated without both a friendly unit to ready and an enemy unit at a battlefield to deal damage to. Both targets must be legal at activation for the spell to enter the chain.

Nuances:

If Last Breath is successfully activated with both valid targets, but one target becomes invalid before resolution, the spell resolves doing as much as it can with the remaining valid target ("do as much as you can" only applies during resolution, not activation)

The distinction between activation requirements and resolution is key: all targets must be legal when activating the spell, but targets can become invalid during resolution

This differs from cards like Dragon's Rage which use "Then" to indicate sequential timing, where the second target is chosen during resolution rather than activation

question: Can Wind Wall target itself as the spell to be countered, and if so, would Ravenbloom Student get +1 Might from the resolution?
answer:
Ruling: Wind Wall can target itself because it moves onto the Chain before targets are declared, making it a valid target for itself. However, Ravenbloom Student would not get +1 Might because a card that is Countered is not considered to have been played.

Sequence:

Wind Wall is put onto the Chain

Targets are declared (Wind Wall can target itself as it's now a spell on the Chain)

Wind Wall resolves and counters itself

Ravenbloom Student does not trigger because countered cards are not considered played

Nuances:

This interaction is mostly irrelevant in practice but could be used to put a spell in your trash

The rule preventing deterministically illegal choices does not apply here because the targeting is not deterministically illegal

Magic has a separate rule prohibiting self-targeting, but Riftbound does not have an analogous rule

question: If a unit with 3 printed might at Trifarian War Camp gets Smoke Screened, does it have 1 or 2 might?
answer:
Ruling: The unit has 1 might. Smoke Screen snapshots the unit's might at 4 (3 base + 1 from War Camp), then reduces it by 3, resulting in 1 might (3 + 1 - 3 = 1).

Sequence:

War Camp's passive ability applies first, giving the unit +1 might (total 4 might)

Smoke Screen sees the unit at 4 might and snapshots a -3 reduction

Final calculation: 3 base + 1 (War Camp) - 3 (Smoke Screen) = 1 might

The unit keeps +1 from War Camp as long as it remains there and -3 from Smoke Screen until end of turn

Nuances:

If the unit moves off War Camp afterward, it will have 0 might (3 base - 3 from Smoke Screen)

Both War Camp and Smoke Screen are in the arithmetic layer, with increases applied before decreases in layering rules

The layering order doesn't change the final result because Smoke Screen snapshots the modified value

question: Can a player play reactions to save units after combat damage has been assigned?
answer: Ruling: No, once you get to assigning damage, the window for playing reactions is over.

question: How does Mask of Foresight work in 2v2 games, specifically whether the buff applies to teammate units?
answer:
Ruling: Mask of Foresight's "friendly" designation applies to teammate units as well in 2v2 games. Both you and your teammate's units receive the buff based on how many Masks of Foresight you have.

Nuances:

When your units attack/defend alone, they get +X based on how many Masks of Foresight you have

When your teammate's units attack/defend on their turn, they receive the same buff

question: When an opponent casts Possession on a unit that has equipment attached, does the opponent also take control of the equipped gears?
answer:
Ruling: No, the opponent does not gain control of the equipped gears. The gears remain attached to the unit and their effects continue to apply, but the original owner retains control of the equipment.

Sequence:

When Possession resolves on a unit with equipped gears, only the unit (top-most card) changes control

The equipped gears remain attached to the unit until detached by a card effect or game effect

The gear's effect text remains active on the possessed unit as long as it stays attached

If the gear detaches (such as when the unit dies, is banished, or otherwise leaves the board), it is recalled to the original owner's base during cleanup

Nuances:

The opponent cannot use effects like Jax or Weaponmaster to move the gear away from the unit because they don't control the gear

The opponent does benefit from the gear's effect text while it remains attached to the possessed unit

Control of the gear never changes, only the unit's control changes

question: Does Tryndamere's ability count only combat damage?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Tryndamere's ability counts only combat damage.

Nuances:

Spell damage can factor into the math by reducing a unit's remaining health, meaning Tryndamere would need to deal less combat damage to reach the threshold for triggering while conquering

question: If you retreat a blue Viktor (Inquisitive) on your opponent's turn, does he make a recruit token?
answer:
Ruling: No, Viktor does not make a recruit token when retreated. Play effects occur after the triggering spell finishes the complete process of being played, which in the case of retreat will be after Viktor is put back in hand.

Sequence:

Retreat is played targeting Viktor

Viktor is returned to hand as part of retreat resolving

Play effects would trigger after retreat fully resolves

Since Viktor is no longer on the battlefield, his play effect does not trigger

question: Can a player use Hidden Blade from hand to kill their own unit before Temporary destroys it at the start of their beginning phase?
answer:
Ruling: Hidden Blade from hand cannot be used to react to the Temporary trigger because it is not a reaction. However, if Hidden Blade were already hidden at the same battlefield, it could be used at reaction speed to kill the temporary unit before the Temporary effect resolves.

Nuances:

Hidden cards can be played at reaction speed to anything on the chain

Hidden cards have additional targeting restrictions that must be followed

You may use reactions to triggers caused by phase changes (like the Temporary trigger being put onto the chain), but cannot take actions before "the start of your beginning phase" otherwise

question: If a player conquers Zaun Warrens and uses its 'when you conquer' effect to discard Mega Death Rocket, can they retrieve Mega Death Rocket from trash with its own 'when you conquer' ability?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot retrieve Mega Death Rocket with its own 'when you conquer' ability in this scenario.

Sequence:

You conquer the battlefield and gain the point

The 'when you conquer' trigger window opens

At this point, Mega Death Rocket is not yet in the trash (it will be discarded as part of resolving Zaun Warrens' effect)

Since Mega Death Rocket is not in the trash when the 'when you conquer' trigger window is active, it cannot be retrieved

Nuances:

The conquer point is gained before the discard effect resolves

Cards must already be in the trash when the 'when you conquer' trigger window opens to be eligible for retrieval effects

question: If a Sprite with 5 power has 3 marked damage on it from Hextech, will it still deal full combat damage and kill both blocking units?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the Sprite will still deal its full 5 damage in the combat damage step and can kill both blocking units. Marked damage does not reduce the amount of damage a unit deals in combat.

Sequence:

Hextech resolves, leaving 3 marked damage on the Sprite

Combat damage step occurs

Sprite distributes its full 5 damage to blocking units

Blocking units distribute 4 damage to the Sprite (only needs 2 more to kill it)

Once all damage is assigned, units with damage equal to or above their power are killed

Nuances:

A unit deals its full combat damage regardless of how much marked damage it has on it

The Sprite only needs 2 more damage to be killed (since it has 5 power and already has 3 marked damage), but it still deals all 5 of its damage

question: If you have two green Ahris on one battlefield, do you score three points on that field when you hold it?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you would score 3 points when you hold a battlefield with two green Ahris on it.

Nuances:

Ahri is considered an exception as a unit, so there is no limitation preventing multiple copies from contributing their scoring effects

This scoring can be further amplified with cards like Power Nexus or Svellsongur

question: If a player scores 1 point on offense (capping one battlefield) but cannot win that way, then the opponent burns out due to triggered abilities, does the attacking player win by reaching 8 points total (7 + 1 from cap + 1 from opponent's burnout)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the attacking player wins the game. The point gained from the opponent burning out counts as the 8th point and can win the game immediately.

Sequence:

Attacking player caps one battlefield, gaining 1 point (going from 7 to 8 points)

Since they cannot win by single capping on offense, they would normally draw a card instead

However, their unit movement triggers the opponent's Volibears, causing the opponent to burn out

The burnout gives the attacking player another point

This point can be the 8th point that wins the game

question: Does damage get removed after non-combat showdowns?
answer:
Ruling: No, damage is only removed after combat and at end of turn.

Nuances:

Non-combat showdowns do not trigger damage removal

question: If Traveling Merchant moves to an open battlefield and you discard Flame Chompers, can you play Flame Chompers directly to the battlefield Traveling Merchant is moving to?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play Flame Chompers to the battlefield Traveling Merchant is moving to because you do not control that battlefield yet when the discard effect resolves.

Nuances:

Control of the new battlefield is not established until Traveling Merchant's movement fully resolves

question: Can Ezreal Prodigy's static effect be used to ignore Nocturne's special cost when Nocturne is revealed off a stacked deck?
answer: Ruling: No, Ezreal Prodigy's effect does not work with Nocturne's special cost. While Nocturne says "may", it must also say "as an additional cost" for Ezreal's effect to apply.

question: Can you play Call To Glory with 0 energy if you choose to spend a buff instead of paying the 3 resource cost?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Call To Glory without having 3 energy available if you choose to spend a buff instead.

Sequence:

Calculate the cost first before paying

If you opt to consume a buff, the cost becomes only spending a buff with no energy required

Pay the calculated cost

Nuances:

Energy and Power work with a Mana Pool system, so you don't need to pay immediately when playing the spell

The buff spending is an additional cost option that replaces the energy requirement

question: Does Wielder of Water get +2 might when moving into an empty battlefield, and can it be targeted by Gust?
answer:
Ruling: Wielder of Water does not get +2 might when moving into an empty battlefield because it is a showdown, not a combat, so there are no attacker/defender designations. Therefore, it can be targeted by Gust.

Nuances:

Wielder of Water's ability is a passive "while I'm defending alone" effect, not a "when I defend" trigger, so you cannot react to it with Gust during combat

If player 2 moves units to a battlefield where Wielder of Water is already present, combat starts when the battlefield becomes contested, attacker and defender are assigned, and Wielder of Water has 4 might before there's any opportunity to use Gust (unless player 2's movement opened a chain from a move-triggered ability)

question: Does Svellsongur copy only a unit's original printed text, or does it copy all text including modifications from other equipment?
answer:
Ruling: Svellsongur copies only the original printed text of a unit, not text added by other equipment or modifications.

Nuances:

This ruling is not explicitly stated in the written rules (RAW would suggest it copies all text)

The limitation is based on developer comments and design intent (RAI)

This limitation appears to be specific to Svellsongur; other equipment are intended to interact with each other

A Chinese FAQ (communicated with Riot) clarified that the copy action only affects printed text, though this FAQ is not official

question: When do you score points for controlling a battlefield/zone in Riftbound?
answer:
Ruling: You score a point if you control a battlefield at the START of your turn, not at the end of your turn.

Nuances:

This timing distinction is critical for determining win conditions and whether a player can recover from a losing position

question: Why does Kaisa's legend ability have reaction speed if activated abilities can only be used during your turn when the chain is empty?
answer:
Ruling: Activated abilities with reaction speed can be used in any reaction speed window, not just during your turn when the chain is empty. The reaction speed designation specifically allows the ability to be used at times beyond the default restriction.

Nuances:

The default rule for activated abilities is that they can only be used during your turn when the chain is empty

When an activated ability has reaction speed specified, it overrides this default restriction and allows use in any reaction speed window

question: Is the second effect 'Then, if I am at a battlefield, buff all other friendly units there' a passive or a one-time active effect?
answer:
Ruling: It's a single-use trigger when the unit is played, not a passive effect.

Sequence:

The first part of the effect resolves first

Then the second part resolves only if legal (if the unit is at a battlefield)

Nuances:

This is a standard WYPM (When You Play Me) trigger that resolves as normal

question: Is the starting leader card (Chosen Champion Unit) considered to be on the field, and does it enter ready when played?
answer:
Ruling: The Chosen Champion Unit in the Champion Zone is not considered in play and cannot trigger abilities. When played from the Champion Zone, it enters exhausted like any other unit unless otherwise stated.

Nuances:

While in the Champion Zone, the card functions more like a face-up card in your hand than a card on the field

The Chosen Champion Unit has the same restrictions as any other unit in the Main Deck

question: If a unit is targeted by Darius's spell (Noxian Guillotine) before combat, does it only need 1 damage assigned to it during combat to die?
answer:
Ruling: No, you must still assign damage equal to the unit's might during combat, even if it was targeted by Noxian Guillotine earlier. The Guillotine effect does not reduce the lethal damage requirement for combat damage assignment.

Sequence:

Noxian Guillotine resolves during showdown before combat damage

During combat, you must still assign lethal damage (damage equal to or exceeding might) to units before assigning damage elsewhere

After combat damage is dealt, the unit targeted by Guillotine will die from the combined damage

Nuances:

If you have enough total damage to split between multiple units, you can assign lethal damage to one unit and less-than-lethal damage to a Guillotine-targeted unit, and both will die (e.g., 4 might attacking two 3-might units where one was Guillotined: assign 3 to one, 1 to the Guillotined unit)

This ruling applies even to units with Tank - you must still assign damage equal to their might before damaging other units

Lethal damage is defined as nonzero damage equal to or exceeding a unit's might

question: Can units from base and ganking units be used together in the same showdown?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you can use both units from base and ganking units in the same showdown.

question: Can Sprite Call be used as a Reaction when it would be sent to Trash due to losing control of a Battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Sprite Call cannot be used as a Reaction in this situation. The card goes to Trash as a result of cleanup, which doesn't use the chain, so you cannot react to it.

Nuances:

You need to trigger Sprite Call before your other unit gets removed

You can't conquer a Battlefield that you already scored that turn (including scoring for holding)

You can lose and gain control of a Battlefield, but that doesn't result in a conquer

question: When Volibear attacks and deals 5 damage split however you want, can you use actions before or after the ability resolves to buff/save units, and can you overkill units with the damage?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot play action spells during Volibear's ability because it starts a chain where only reaction spells can be played. By the time you can play actions again, the damage has already been dealt, cleanup has been performed, and units have died.

Sequence:

Volibear's ability starts a chain

Only reaction spells can be played during the chain

Targets are chosen when the ability is played

During resolution, damage is divided among targets

Each target must be assigned damage greater than 0

Cleanup is performed and units die

Only after this can actions be played again

Nuances:

You can use reaction spells (like Viktor's signature spell) to respond to the ability before it resolves

If a reaction buffs units, damage is still divided during resolution, but each target must receive at least 1 damage

question: If Mountain Drake is affected by Smoke Screen (reducing it to 6 Might), then targeted by Void Seeker, and saved with Zhonya's, does it stay at 6 Might or return to 10 Might?
answer:
Ruling: The Mountain Drake stays at 6 Might because it was not defeated, only recalled by Zhonya's.

Nuances:

Zhonya's recalls the unit rather than having it be defeated, so ongoing effects like Smoke Screen's Might reduction persist

question: Where in the rules is "Board Zone" defined, and does it include the banish zone?
answer:
Ruling: Board zones are defined in the rules (rule 106), and the banish zone is included as a board zone.

Nuances:

This ruling has implications for cards like Portal Rescue that interact with board zones

question: When playing a unit with Accelerate (like Kai'sa) via Baited Hook, can you pay the Accelerate cost to have it enter ready, and is the Accelerate cost still required?
answer:
Ruling: When playing a unit via Baited Hook, you can pay optional additional costs like Accelerate, and you must pay mandatory additional costs. Baited Hook only sets the base cost to zero.

Sequence:

Baited Hook allows you to play the unit with base cost set to zero

You then have the opportunity to pay additional costs (like Accelerate's 1 energy and 1 power)

If additional costs are mandatory (like Cruel Patron's requirement to kill a unit), you must still pay them

Nuances:

Only the base cost is set to zero by Baited Hook; all additional costs function normally

Optional additional costs (like Accelerate) remain optional

Mandatory additional costs must still be paid

question: Can a player hold priority after playing one reaction to play another reaction before passing priority to the next player?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can hold priority after playing a reaction to play another reaction before passing priority to the next player.

Nuances:

You need to hold priority if you want to ensure you can play multiple reactions, because if you pass priority and your opponent also passes, the topmost chain item will resolve.

question: If I use Tideturner with only one unit on a battlefield that has a hidden card, does the hidden card die during the swap or does it stay?
answer:
Ruling: The hidden card will stay. You don't lose control of the battlefield during the Tideturner swap.

Sequence:

The unit movement from Tideturner is treated as simultaneous

There is no window where you don't have units at that battlefield

Cleanup happens after Tideturner resolves

At cleanup, you still control a unit at that battlefield, so you maintain control and keep the hidden card

Nuances:

Think of the move as simultaneous for all intents and purposes, preventing any loss of battlefield control during the swap

question: Does damage heal after combat include spell damage, or only combat damage?
answer: Ruling: All damage on all units in play heals after combat, regardless of how they were damaged (including spell damage).

question: Can you resolve missed triggers (like Forgetting Battlefield/Holding Units effects) in the same turn at casual/low OPL events?
answer:
Ruling: At high OPL events, missed triggers cannot be resolved in the same turn. At casual events like Nexus Nights, you can typically resolve them in the same turn if you missed the trigger, but this is not guaranteed.

Nuances:

At low OPL events, there is a "spirit of the format" clause, but tournament rules still apply

If your opponent objects to resolving a missed trigger, you must call a judge who has final say

The enforcement depends on the specific event, judge, and local culture

Most judges at low OPL will be lenient since these events are for learning, but some locals are more competitive

question: Can I spend the buff from Kraken Hunter's ability towards accelerating the card?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you can spend the buff towards accelerating the card.

question: Can Imperial Decree be used to chain token attacks, sending in 1-Might tokens one at a time to kill high-Might enemy units by dealing 1 damage each (which becomes lethal under the spell's effect)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can send tokens in one at a time to trigger separate combats under Imperial Decree. Each token that deals any damage will trigger the spell's effect to kill the damaged unit, regardless of the unit's Might value. This works on offense when sending units in sequentially.

Sequence:

Cast Imperial Decree, which creates a delayed trigger effect for the turn

Send in a 1-Might token to initiate combat at a battlefield

The token deals 1 damage to an enemy unit during the showdown

Imperial Decree's trigger activates and kills the damaged unit

Resolve the combat fully

Send in the next token and repeat

Nuances:

Imperial Decree applies to any unit that takes damage during the turn, even units that enter play after the spell resolves (the delayed trigger exists independently, not tied to specific units)

This strategy does NOT work well on defense because damage assignment rules require you to assign all damage to one unit until it has damage equal to its Might before assigning to another unit

You cannot move in multiple tokens simultaneously and spread 1 damage to multiple units - damage must be fully assigned to one unit first

The spell does not retroactively kill units that were damaged before it was cast (the trigger is "when [they] take damage")

If a unit receives lethal combat damage, the Imperial Decree trigger still goes on the chain even though the unit dies during cleanup, opening a reaction window

Units that already have damage marked before Imperial Decree is cast are not affected unless they take additional damage after the spell resolves

question: Can Kaisa's ability (which gives power for spells) be used to pay for non-spell costs through recycling, or to pay the energy cost of spells like Retreat?
answer:
Ruling: Kaisa's ability only provides power that can be used to pay for spells, not energy. This power cannot be used to pay for units or to pay the energy cost of any card, including spells.

Nuances:

Kaisa provides power (like recycling a rune), not energy (like exhausting a rune)

The power Kaisa generates can only be used for spell costs, regardless of when or how it was generated

Kaisa can be tapped at any time during the turn and the power gets stored in the pool

Kaisa does not give you a rune or energy; she gives power with a restriction that it can only pay for spells

question: Can you play Cull the Weak if you own no units anywhere, and if so, does your opponent still have to kill a unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Cull the Weak even if you own no units. Your opponent must kill one of their units, but you do not have to kill any of your own units.

Nuances:

Killing your own unit is not a cost or a target, so the card is legal to play without having units

The "do as much as you can" rule applies - you resolve as much of the effect as possible

question: Does Shield stack in Riftbound?
answer: Ruling: Shield stacks. Assault also stacks.

question: Where are the rules for Ravenbloom Student's trigger in the new Comprehensive Rules?
answer: The user found the answer themselves but did not share the specific location or ruling in the thread.

question: What is the correct setup order for Riftbound games, particularly regarding when battlefields are revealed and when turn order is determined?
answer:
Ruling: The setup order for every game is: Legend > CC > Battlefields (revealed based on mode of play) > Turn order > Draw/Mulligan. Battlefields are always revealed before turn order is determined.

Sequence:

Reveal legends

Choose CC (Command Center)

Pick and reveal battlefields simultaneously (in 1v1 Bo3)

Determine turn order (losing player from previous game decides in games 2 and 3)

Draw cards and resolve mulligans

Nuances:

In games 2 and 3 of a Bo3, players know who lost and who will pick turn order, but not what they'll pick until after battlefields are revealed

Players can and do plan around this information

This sequence applies to every game, every time

question: How does Caitlyn's card work? Does she deal and receive damage at the end of combat, or only one? Does moving her to a battlefield and tapping trigger her ability?
answer:
Ruling: Caitlyn has two abilities. The first is a passive that makes Caitlyn always the last of your units to die when assigning combat damage. The second is an activated ability that requires paying a cost to use.

Nuances:

Moving Caitlyn to a battlefield and exhausting her does not trigger her effect because it is an activated ability, not a triggered ability

You must pay the cost to activate the second ability

question: Does Pirate's Haven apply to multiple units, or just one unit?
answer:
Ruling: Pirate's Haven applies to each unit, not just one unit.

Nuances:

The wording may seem ambiguous (similar to Ahri's effect), but it applies to all applicable units, not just the first one

question: Can you move units from another battlefield to the current combat to affect might summing?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot use the standard move action to move units mid-combat. However, you can move units mid-combat if a card or ability specifically instructs you to do so.

Nuances:

Standard movement actions are not allowed during combat

Card effects or abilities that cause movement (like Zenith Blade) can be used during combat

question: Does moving a unit with an effect like Fight or Flight exhaust the unit?
answer:
Ruling: No, moving a unit with a card effect does not exhaust it.

Nuances:

Exhausting a unit is the cost to make a standard move

When card effects move a unit, they simply move it without requiring exhaustion

question: Can Recruit the Vanguard be played to deploy units to the battlefield where a showdown combat is about to occur?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if you are the defender in the showdown, you can play units to that battlefield because you control it.

Nuances:

This only works when you are the defending player

The defender controls the battlefield where the showdown is taking place

question: Does Purple Miss Fortune affect my partner's units in a 2v2?
answer: Ruling: Yes, Purple Miss Fortune affects your partner's units in a 2v2.

question: When Karthus and Kog'maw die at the same time, does Kog'maw's Deathknell trigger twice due to Karthus's passive ability?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, when Karthus and Kog'maw die at the same time, Kog'maw's Deathknell triggers twice. Karthus's ability is a passive (not a triggered ability), so it applies even when Karthus dies simultaneously with other units.

Nuances:

This differs from Viktor Leader's triggered ability, which cannot trigger when Viktor dies at the same time as another unit (due to the rule that a game object cannot evaluate its trigger condition if it leaves the zone at the same time the trigger is satisfied)

Karthus works because it's a passive ability that "occurs" rather than a triggered ability with a trigger condition

question: Does playing 2 Spirit's Refuge give a buffed card Deflect 2?
answer:
Ruling: No, multiple Spirit's Refuge do not stack to give Deflect 2. The card text specifies that friendly buffed units have deflect "if they didn't already," which prevents stacking.

Nuances:

The card's text explicitly prevents granting additional deflect to units that already have it from another Spirit's Refuge

question: In a 2v2 match, can Yasuo's effect target a friendly unit from a teammate's base and move it to your base to use as your unit?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot use Yasuo's legend ability on your partner's units in a 2v2 match.

Nuances:

The restriction is not about whether the units are "friendly" (they are), but rather that you cannot move your partner's units "to and from your base"

question: When attacking with Lecturing Yordle against Ahri (Inquisitive) and Ahri Legend, should Cleave be played before or after the showdown starts to maximize Might?
answer:
Ruling: Playing Cleave after the showdown starts results in higher Might (4) compared to playing it before entering the battlefield (2), because the timing of when Ahri's Might reduction effects apply differs.

Sequence:

If Cleave is played before Yordle enters: Yordle starts at 2 Might + 3 from Cleave - 1 from Ahri Legend - 2 from Ahri Champion = 2 Might total

If Cleave is played after entering (during showdown): Yordle starts at 2 Might - 1 from Ahri Legend - 0 from Ahri Champion (doesn't apply yet) + 3 from Cleave = 4 Might total

Nuances:

Cleave activates in both timing scenarios (before or after entering battlefield)

The key difference is when Ahri Champion's Might reduction applies relative to when Cleave's bonus is added

question: When passing priority during a Showdown in combat with an empty chain, does the non-turn player need to pass twice in a row after the turn player passes, or does passing work differently?
answer:
Ruling: When you have focus and priority and the chain is empty, passing means you pass both focus and priority together (not just priority). If both players pass consecutively with nothing on the chain, the showdown ends.

Sequence:

Contesting player (usually turn player) gains focus and priority at showdown start

If contesting player passes with empty chain, they pass both focus and priority to opponent

If opponent then passes with empty chain, both players have passed consecutively and the showdown closes

Combat continues to damage step

Nuances:

Focus passes back and forth until both players pass consecutively - it's not about each player getting one turn

One player could play 5 actions while the other plays 0 if they keep passing focus back

The player who contests the battlefield gains focus (usually turn player, but not always)

Passing is contextual: passing with something on the chain only passes priority, passing with empty chain passes both focus and priority

question: If I have two Gem Crafters on the battlefield, does the ability trigger twice when a new unit enters?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if you have two Gem Crafters on the battlefield, the ability triggers twice when a new unit enters. Multiple instances of Vision trigger separately.

Sequence:

When a new unit enters, the first Gem Crafter's Vision triggers

Look at 1 card and decide whether to put it into your memory

Then the second Gem Crafter's Vision triggers

Look at 1 card and decide whether to put it into your memory

Nuances:

When you play the second Gem Crafter, it will also trigger both existing Gem Crafters' abilities

You resolve each Vision trigger separately (look at 1, decide, then look at the next 1, decide) - not look at 2 cards and decide for both at once

question: Can I activate a Hidden spell from a different battlefield than where the triggering effect is happening?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can activate a Hidden spell from any battlefield at reaction speed for 0 cost (as long as it isn't the turn you hid it).

Nuances:

The Hidden spell cannot target things outside the battlefield it's hidden on

You can still play it in response to spells targeting other battlefields

question: If Icathian Rain's first two triggers target Viktor, Leader of the Glorious Evolution and the remaining triggers kill 3 other non-token units, can Viktor spawn tokens with his effect?
answer:
Ruling: Viktor can spawn tokens if the first two triggers (which resolve last due to stack order) target him, because he will still be alive when the other units die. If the last two triggers target Viktor, he will die before seeing the other units die and will not spawn tokens.

Sequence:

Icathian Rain triggers are placed on the stack in order (c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c6)

Stack resolves in reverse order (last in, first out)

If c1 and c2 target Viktor, they resolve last, so c3-c6 resolve first, killing other units while Viktor is alive to see them die

If c5 and c6 target Viktor, they resolve first, killing Viktor before other units die, so he doesn't see them die

Nuances:

The key factor is whether Viktor is alive at the moment the other units die, which depends on stack resolution order

question: If you're defending, can you use Arcane Shift to banish and replay Blue Ahri from/onto the same battlefield to trigger her 'When I Defend' ability a second time in the same combat?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can trigger the 'When I Defend' ability a second time. When a unit is banished and replayed, it becomes a new game object that never saw the first trigger happen, so it can trigger again even in the same combat.

Nuances:

While units normally only trigger their 'When I attack/defend' abilities the first time they gain the attacker/defender designation in a combat, banishing creates a new game object that is treated as never having triggered before

This interaction is a core combo for cards like Watcher when defending

question: If a player pays Repeat for a spell and the opponent responds with Defy, does Defy stop the entire spell or does the Defy also get negated?
answer:
Ruling: Defy stops the entire spell, including the Repeat effect.

Nuances:

Repeat does not create a second chain item; it remains part of the same spell on the chain

Repeat must be declared as an additional cost when playing the card, not after resolving any part of the spell's effect

question: If an opponent plays Hextech Ray targeting a card on field, can they change the target if the defending player responds by playing a unit from hidden (like Teemo in trap) before Hextech Ray resolves?
answer:
Ruling: No, they cannot change targets. The target is chosen and locked in when Hextech Ray is finalized to the chain, before the opponent has a chance to respond.

Sequence:

Player plays Hextech Ray and chooses target when finalizing it to the chain

Target is now locked in

Opponent can now respond (e.g., by playing a unit from hidden)

Hextech Ray resolves with original target

Nuances:

The unit being played from hidden must not have been hidden on the same turn (summoning sickness applies)

question: If I cast Gust targeting my own Ravenbloom Student that is already at 3 Might, does the Student get +1 Might (becoming 4 Might) before Gust resolves, or does Gust resolve first and return the Student to hand?
answer:
Ruling: Gust resolves first and returns the Student to hand. A card is not considered played until it fully resolves, so the Gust would resolve before the +1 Might increase could trigger.

Sequence:

Gust is cast targeting the 3 Might Ravenbloom Student

Gust resolves, returning the Student to hand

The Student never reaches 4 Might because it is returned to hand before the +1 Might trigger can occur

question: If Uncheck Power is countered by Wind Wall, are units exhausted?
answer:
Ruling: Uncheck Power exhausts friendly units as part of spell resolution, not as a cost. If the spell is countered by Wind Wall, your units are not exhausted and remain in their previous state.

Sequence:

Uncheck Power is played and put on the stack

If countered by Wind Wall, the spell does not resolve

Units are not exhausted because exhausting happens at resolution, not when playing the spell

Nuances:

The exhausting effect is part of resolution, not an additional cost paid when playing the spell

question: Can a player hold priority after playing an Action card during a showdown to play a Reaction speed spell as a 'buffer' before the opponent responds?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can hold priority and play a Reaction speed spell like Stupify on top of the chain. However, this doesn't effectively 'buffer' against counters like Wind Wall because counters target 'a spell' on the chain, not specifically the previous spell, so your opponent can choose to counter whichever spell they want.

Nuances:

Counter spells like Wind Wall can target any spell on the chain, not just the most recent one

Simply adding more spells to the chain doesn't protect earlier spells from being countered

question: Does the Shield keyword stack when multiple units or effects grant Shield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, each instance of Shield stacks. Multiple sources of Shield add together to create a cumulative Shield value.

Sequence:

Each unit with Shield grants its Shield value

Shield granted by other units' abilities adds to the total

Shield granted by combat tricks (like Block) also adds to the total

All Shield values sum together for the final Shield amount

Nuances:

In the example with 2 Tarics and a Sunlit Guardian: one Taric would have Shield 5 (1 from itself, 1 from the other Taric, 3 from Block), the other Taric would have Shield 2, and the Guardian would have Shield 3

The resulting might values would be: one Taric with 9M, one Taric with 6M, and Sunlit Guardian with 6M

question: When a unit is saved by Zhonya's or Guardian Angel (replacing its death), do equipment cards detach from the unit?
answer:
Ruling: When a unit is saved by Zhonya's or Guardian Angel (the death is replaced and prevented), the unit doesn't die, so equipment remains attached.

Nuances:

When multiple replacement effects (like both Zhonya's and GA) would prevent the same death, you choose which applies first; the second replacement effect won't trigger since the death has already been prevented by the first one.

question: If a unit with Assault (like Jinx) attacks and gets hit by Smokescreen, then plays Fists of Fury to survive, what is their Might after combat? Does it go to 0 or stay at 1?
answer:
Ruling: When a unit's Might is reduced by Smokescreen during combat and then modified by other effects, the Might can go to 0 or even negative values. The minimum of 1 restriction on Smokescreen was not changed by the new ruling.

Sequence:

Smokescreen snapshots the target's Might value when its effect happens

It applies a continuous reduction equal to that snapshotted value minus 1 for the turn

Other modifiers are then applied to the base Might

The final Might can be 0 or negative

Nuances:

For Jinx (5 base Might): After Smokescreen reduces her to 2 Might, if she plays Fists of Fury (+3 Might), her out-of-combat Might would be 0 (5 base - 4 from Smokescreen + 3 from FoF = 4, but she's at 2 in combat, so 2 - 2 = 0)

For Chemtech Enforcer (2 base, becomes 4): Smokescreen would snapshot at 4 and apply -3, resulting in -1 Might (2 base - 3 from Smokescreen = -1)

Smokescreen's reduction is snapshotted when the effect happens and applies continuously for the turn

question: In a 4-player FFA game, do you need to conquer all 3 battlefields to score the last point?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not need to conquer all 3 battlefields to score the last point. You only need to have scored on all point values previously.

Sequence:

If you already hold 2 battlefields and then conquer the third, you score the final point

Alternatively, you can hold just one battlefield to get the final point

You can also get the final point via other means like Yasuo

Nuances:

The restriction on needing to have scored all previous points only applies to getting points from conquering battlefields

Other methods of scoring (like Yasuo) can grant the final point without this restriction

Opponents have a chance to remove your hold during their turn before you score

question: When a temporary token (Sprite) is on a battlefield with a hidden unit (Teemo), and the temporary trigger happens at the start of turn, can you reveal the hidden unit before the token is removed to maintain control and score for holding?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can reveal the hidden unit before the temporary token is removed. The temporary trigger can be responded to, allowing you to reveal Teemo first, which then resolves before the Sprite token is discarded.

Sequence:

Temporary trigger goes on the chain during beginning phase

You have priority first and can respond by revealing Teemo

Teemo (as permanent) goes on chain and resolves

Teemo's WYPM trigger goes on chain

After all pass, Sprite temporary trigger resolves and token goes to trash

Teemo remains on battlefield and you score for holding

Nuances:

If you had removed the token before revealing Teemo, you would lose control and Teemo would be discarded

Teemo will not be readied during activation phase because temporary happens during beginning phase (after awake phase)

question: How does The Zero Drive card work, specifically the 'banish this' mechanic and what it's used for?
answer:
Ruling: When a unit equipped with The Zero Drive dies, you banish that unit. You can then pay the cost and banish The Zero Drive equipment itself to return all units that were banished by The Zero Drive's "When an equipped unit dies, banish it" effect.

Sequence:

Unit equipped with The Zero Drive dies

That unit gets banished (instead of going to discard)

Pay the cost and banish The Zero Drive equipment

All units banished by The Zero Drive's effect return

Nuances:

Banished units go to a separate zone called the banished zone, not the trash/discard pile

question: Can Jinx: Rebel's ready ability trigger multiple times?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Jinx: Rebel's ability will trigger each time you discard.

Nuances:

The ability can trigger on your opponent's turn as well

question: Can Crackshot Corsair and Warwick combo so that Warwick will kill the unit that Crackshot deals damage to?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Crackshot Corsair and Warwick can combo together. The triggers happen simultaneously, so you can order them so that Crackshot Corsair's trigger happens first and then Warwick will kill all units at the battlefield with damage on them.

Sequence:

Crackshot Corsair's trigger resolves first, dealing damage to a unit

Warwick's trigger resolves second, killing all units at the battlefield with damage on them

question: Can you move a unit from battlefield to battlefield using Ride the Wind without the standard movement restriction (ganking)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can move units from battlefield to battlefield using Ride the Wind. The battlefield-to-battlefield restriction only applies to standard movement, not to movement from spells or abilities.

Nuances:

When moving units with spells or abilities, you don't exhaust the units unless the effect specifically says to do so.

question: When Tideturner is played from hidden, does it trigger 'When I Defend' abilities on units that are moved into combat?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, units that become defenders after combat starts should still trigger their "When I Defend" abilities when moved into combat by Tideturner played from hidden.

Nuances:

This does not work with "When I Attack" triggers when playing from hidden, because if you control a hidden card, you control the battlefield and would never be assigned as the attacker

The current wording on Tideturner will receive an errata (likely to clarify it can target any unit when revealed from hidden, not just units at the current location)

This ruling is based on developer clarification rather than explicit rules text

question: In what order do you perform setup steps, specifically when are battlefields revealed - immediately when chosen or after mulligans?
answer:
