Ruling: Battlefields are chosen and revealed before determining who goes first, and therefore before mulligans. When you place a battlefield into the battlefield zone, it is visible to all players immediately.

Sequence:

Reveal legend

Reveal champion

Choose and reveal battlefields

Determine who goes first

Resolve mulligans

question: Can you play Ride the Wind targeting a unit at Vilemaw's Lair to move it to base (even though Vilemaw's Lair prevents the movement), just to ready the unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Ride the Wind targeting a unit at Vilemaw's Lair with base as the destination. The unit will be readied but will stay at Vilemaw's Lair since the Lair prevents the movement.

Sequence:

Target a unit at Vilemaw's Lair with Ride the Wind

Choose base as the move destination

When Ride the Wind resolves, do as much as you can: the unit is readied but does not move (prevented by Vilemaw's Lair)

Nuances:

Base is still a valid destination for targeting purposes because Vilemaw's Lair doesn't make destinations invalid; it simply prevents the movement effect from occurring

The spell resolves legally even though the movement doesn't happen

question: For 'Forge of the Future' with text 'Kill This', can the card be trashed at any point or does it require another card's effect to destroy it?
answer:
Ruling: 'Kill This' is an activated ability where killing the card is the cost to activate the ability, as indicated by the colon (':') in the card text.

Sequence:

Pay the cost by killing/trashing the card

The ability activates

Nuances:

This is an activated ability, not a passive effect that can be used at any time without structure

question: Can a card affect an enemy base if it doesn't specify it only affects units at a Battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, cards can affect enemy bases unless they specifically state they only affect units at a Battlefield.

Nuances:

The default rule is that cards can affect units anywhere unless restricted by the card text

Only cards that explicitly specify "units at a Battlefield" are limited in their targeting

question: Can Flash and Fight or Flight both trigger Kayn - Unleashed's ability even though they both move to the same location (base)?
answer:
Ruling: No, using Flash and Fight or Flight together will not trigger Kayn's ability twice because he won't physically move the second time since he's already at base. A unit must physically move to a new location for it to count as a 'move'.

Sequence:

First movement spell moves Kayn from battlefield to base (counts as one move)

Second movement spell targeting base does nothing since Kayn is already at base (does not count as a move)

Nuances:

The two moves must occur in the same turn, but not necessarily in the same chain

Actions can be played during a Showdown, allowing windows to play movement spells at different points

To trigger Kayn's ability with reaction-speed spells (like responding to Falling Star), you need two reaction-speed movement spells that move to different locations, such as Tideturner plus Flash or Fight or Flight

question: Does choosing a unit/gear in the opponent's hand with Mindsplitter count as progress towards Ezreal's Prodigal Explorer ability (which requires targeting 2 gears/units in the same turn)?
answer:
Ruling: No, Mindsplitter does not count towards Prodigal Explorer's requirement. Mindsplitter only targets a player, not units or gear. The card chosen from hand is selected during resolution and is not a target.

Nuances:

Effects that use "choose" during resolution are distinct from "targeting" effects

Cards in hand are not considered proper units; they are only units when on the board (they are "unit cards" in hand)

question: How do you pay for Baited Hook's activation cost that shows a 1 symbol, a yellow symbol, and tap?
answer:
Ruling: You need to exhaust 1 rune of any color (generating 1 energy) and recycle 1 yellow rune (generating 1 yellow power). These can be the same rune done in sequence: exhaust a yellow rune to float 1 energy, then recycle that same rune to generate 1 yellow power.

Sequence:

Exhaust 1 rune of any color to generate 1 energy

Recycle 1 rune that produces yellow power (can be the same rune)

Tap the card

Nuances:

Number in circle symbols mean energy (which has no domain type)

Colored symbols always mean power

Energy and power are different resources

The rainbow symbol is the generic version of colored power symbols (can pay or be paid for with any color) but still requires recycling

question: When are checks done to see if something dies, and does this happen during a showdown before it ends?
answer:
Ruling: Currently, cleanup (when death is checked) happens anytime something resolves, a unit moves, the turn ends, and showdown ends. This means in the Yasuo/Volibear example, Volibear would die during the showdown after Last Breath resolves, before Yasuo would die.

Sequence:

Yasuo deals 6 damage to 9 might Volibear during showdown

Last Breath is played, dealing another 6 damage to Volibear

Cleanup happens when Last Breath resolves

Volibear dies (12 total damage)

Yasuo survives

Nuances:

This rule is changing in the new Comprehensive Rules, where cleanup will happen any time the game state changes

Healing happens at the end of Combat and end of Turn, not during cleanup

All combats are showdowns

question: Does the second player have untapped runes during the first player's first turn?
answer: Ruling: No. During the first player's first turn, only the first player has runes. The second player only gets their runes in the channel step of their first turn.

question: If I use Flash when they cast Hidden Blade in combat, do they have to kill their own unit instead?
answer:
Ruling: No. Once targets are chosen when finalizing a spell, they cannot be changed. When Flash moves the targeted unit to another zone, it becomes an illegal target for Hidden Blade, so the spell cannot execute any of its instructions (can't kill the unit and its controller can't draw 2).

Nuances:

This differs from Falling Star and Icathian Rain because those spells create reflexive triggers that target when they resolve, giving a priority window to respond before targeting happens

Only spells/abilities that say "do this:" or "do this X times:" create a window where you can react before targeting happens

Hidden Blade's "its controller draws 2" requires checking information about the target, which cannot be done if the target is illegal

If the unit is saved by a replacement effect (like Zhonya's Hourglass or Sett's legend ability), the controller still draws 2 because the target was legal when Hidden Blade resolved

For information to be referenced, the unit needs to either be on the board or have been moved to another zone by the effect that references its information

question: When combat starts, is there a window to play cards before Attack/Defend abilities trigger, and does Teemo, Strategist's errata prevent him from triggering his Defend ability when played from hidden during combat?
answer:
Ruling: There is no window to play cards between starting combat and when Attack/Defend abilities trigger, unless a triggered ability occurs during movement that creates a priority window. Teemo, Strategist still works when played from hidden at reaction speed during combat because "When I Defend" triggers when a card gains the defending designation, not only at the start of combat.

Sequence:

Combat starts and Attack/Defend abilities trigger immediately

Players get priority to respond after these triggers are on the chain

If Teemo is played from hidden at reaction speed during the showdown, he becomes a defending card

When he gains the defending card designation, his "When I Defend" ability triggers

Nuances:

The only exception for a window before Attack/Defend triggers would be if a triggered ability occurred during movement (such as a merchant move trigger)

Teemo's errata was specifically implemented because of changes to defender triggers, to ensure he doesn't trigger twice

question: If an opponent's token has 3 might on battlefield, and I use Hextech Ray (which deals 3 damage) and they respond with Discipline (which gives +2 might), does the token end up with 2 might or 5 might?
answer:
Ruling: The token has 5 might with 3 damage marked on it. Damage does not reduce might/strength in Riftbound.

Sequence:

Token starts with 3 might

Discipline adds +2 might (now 5 might total)

Hextech Ray deals 3 damage (marked on the token)

Token has 5 might with 3 damage marked

Nuances:

There is no HP in Riftbound; units track damage separately from might

A unit dies when damage marked on it equals or exceeds its might

Damage does not reduce a unit's might value

question: When you move an enemy unit into your occupied battlefield (e.g., with Charm), does that enemy become the attacker or defender?
answer:
Ruling: The enemy unit becomes the attacker. Even though your spell moved the unit, it is their unit that applies the contested status to the battlefield.

Sequence:

You use a spell/ability to move an enemy unit into your occupied battlefield

The enemy unit applies contested status to the battlefield

The enemy unit is treated as the attacker

question: When does a player decide to go first or second in relation to battlefield selection and reveal?
answer:
Ruling: The decision to go first or second is made after the battlefields are selected and revealed.

Sequence:

Set aside and select battlefields

Reveal battlefields

Decide first or second

Mulligan

Nuances:

There is currently some ambiguity in the rules about when to choose and reveal battlefields during the "Set Aside BF" step, which is being addressed in an updated Comprehensive Rules release

question: When two Akshans are played to steal gear from each other and then both die, who controls the gear?
answer:
Ruling: Controller is decided in the first layer using dependencies and timestamps. When control-change effects stop applying due to their sources leaving play, the gear returns to its original controller if no other control effects remain active.

Sequence:

Player A plays Akshan, creating a "change controller to Player A" effect on Player B's gear

Player B plays Akshan, creating a "change controller to Player B" effect that depends on and overrides Player A's effect due to timestamp order

If Player A's Akshan dies first, their control effect stops applying, but Player B's effect continues, so Player B controls the gear

If Player B's Akshan then dies, their control effect stops applying

With no control-change effects remaining, the gear returns to its original controller (Player B)

Nuances:

Control-change effects don't "take back" gear when they stop; they simply stop applying

When multiple control effects apply to the same object, they are applied in timestamp order, with later effects overriding earlier ones

The gear doesn't "bounce" between controllers when effects end; it simply resolves to whoever controls it after recalculating remaining effects

Layers are recalculated when an Akshan dies

question: When Zhonya's or Sett's abilities recall a unit to base exhausted instead of it dying, what happens to damage that was dealt to the unit from a spell?
answer:
Ruling: Both Zhonya's and Sett's abilities have received errata to now also heal the units they save when recalling them to base exhausted.

Nuances:

The original templating did not work as intended without this errata

question: When using Dragon's Rage, do you pay Deflect costs for both the unit being moved and the unit being chosen at the destination?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you pay Deflect costs for both the unit being moved and the unit chosen at the destination, since both are being chosen/targeted by Dragon's Rage.

Nuances:

If Dragon's Rage gets countered, you won't need to pay the Deflect cost because the "then do this" part only happens after Dragon's Rage resolves.

question: Can you exhaust a rune for energy and then recycle that same rune for power in the same turn, using both resources to pay for different costs?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, a single rune can provide both 1 energy (by exhausting) and 1 power (by recycling) in the same turn. These resources go into your resource pool and can be used to pay for different costs.

Sequence:

Exhaust the rune to generate 1 energy (goes into your resource pool)

Recycle that same exhausted rune to generate 1 power (also goes into your resource pool)

Both resources remain available in your pool until end of turn

Pay costs from your resource pool as needed

Nuances:

Energy and power are completely distinct resource types and are not interchangeable

Resources in your pool don't have to be spent immediately when generated - they can be "floated" and used later in the turn

You must exhaust the rune BEFORE recycling it to get both resources; if you recycle first, you only get the power

Players should verbally announce when they are exhausting a rune for energy before recycling it for clarity

The rune itself is gone once recycled, but the energy it generated remains in your pool

question: If you play Feral Strength with Repeat on Irelia and use her Legend ability to ready her, does she get +7 Might total?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Irelia gets +7 Might total. Feral Strength with Repeat gives +2 twice (targeting Irelia both times), her Vanguard effect triggers twice when chosen (+1 each time), her Legend ability readies her (+1), and her Vanguard effect triggers again when readied (+1), for a total of +2+2+1+1+1 = +7.

Sequence:

Feral Strength with Repeat is played, creating one chain item with doubled text (two instances of "Give a unit +2 this turn")

Target Irelia with both +2 effects

Irelia's Vanguard effect triggers twice (once for each time she's chosen as a target), granting +1 each time

Irelia's Legend ability triggers (since an ally unit was chosen), allowing you to pay 1 Power to ready her

When Irelia is readied, her Vanguard effect triggers again, granting +1

Total: +2 +2 +1 +1 +1 = +7 Might

Nuances:

Repeat does not create a separate chain item; it doubles the effect text on one chain item

You may choose different targets for each instance of the repeated effect

If Feral Strength is countered, Irelia still gets +3 from being chosen twice and readied (the Vanguard triggers still resolve)

question: How do layers and dependency work in Riftbound, particularly regarding the order of applying effects?
answer:
Ruling: Layers are applied in order from top to bottom as listed in the rules. Within a layer, if one effect depends on another (applying one effect alters the outcome of the other), the independent effect applies first, then the dependent effect. If no dependency exists, effects are applied in timestamp order (the order the cards creating those effects were played).

Sequence:

Apply layers in order (type/supertype, then keywords, then numeric modifications)

Within each layer, check for dependencies between effects

If dependency exists, apply the independent effect first, then the dependent effect

If no dependency exists, apply effects in timestamp order (oldest card first)

For numeric modifications (might, energy, power), all modifications are applied arithmetically (following BODMAS/PEMDAS)

Nuances:

Timestamp is based on when the card was played, not when the effect becomes relevant or active

The rules document currently has gaps: it doesn't explicitly state what order to apply dependent effects, how to resolve dependency loops, or how to handle simultaneous timestamps

Dependencies for might-altering effects are unlikely to occur with current cards

Passive effects exist as soon as the card is played, even if they don't do anything until certain conditions are met

question: Is Vi's Champion Unit effect an activated ability that can be used multiple times per turn at base speed, and does it grant Might each time it's activated?
answer:
Ruling: Vi's effect is an activated ability that can only be used at base speed (during your turn, outside of showdowns). It does not specify "once per turn," so it can be activated multiple times as long as you can recycle cards from your trash.

Sequence:

Activate Vi's ability during your turn at base speed

Choose a card from your trash to put at the bottom of your deck

Vi gains 1 Might

Repeat as many times as desired (if you have cards in trash)

Nuances:

The ability does not exhaust Vi, so there's no limit beyond having cards in your trash to recycle

Gaining Might is not the same as getting a "Buff" - Vi can gain Might multiple times without restriction

This ability cannot be used on your opponent's turn or during showdowns

If you have 2 Vi units out, only the one that activated the ability gets the Might boost

question: What is the penalty when a player has forgotten to list battlefields on their decklist at a high-level tournament?
answer:
Ruling: At high-level tournaments (high OPL), a player who has forgotten to list battlefields on their decklist should receive a game loss and be required to fix their deck list registration.

Sequences:

Issue the game loss penalty

Have the player fix their deck list registration for the next round

Verify their deckbox contains only 3 battlefields to ensure no additional cards were present

Nuances:

The timing of when the issue is discovered matters (typically deck checks happen at the start of a round)

Some people incorrectly suggest treating non-presented battlefields as blank, but there is no rule support for this approach

question: Are official Riftbound sleeves with holographic patterns allowed in OPL tournaments, and what does OPL stand for?
answer:
Ruling: OPL stands for Organized Play Level. While the rules technically prohibit holographic sleeves in OPL tournaments, in practice players have been using official holographic sleeves (like worlds sleeves) without issue, though you should check with the Head Judge to be safe.

Nuances:

Rules as written and rules as actually enforced are somewhat different for sleeve rules

As long as sleeves aren't distractingly holographic, Head Judges typically approve them

It's recommended to bring matte backup sleeves to structured events in case a judge enforces the rule more strictly

Checking your deck in with the Head Judge at structured events is a good practice

question: What is the correct procedure to start a game in Riftbound?
answer:
Ruling: The correct game start procedure is: place hidden champion and legend, reveal both, choose one BF from 3 and place it hidden, reveal BF, determine turn order randomly, then draw and mulligan (with player 1 mulliganing first, then player 2).

Sequence:

Players place hidden champion and hidden legend

Both players reveal champion and legend

Players choose one BF from 3 and place it hidden

Both players reveal their chosen BF

Turn order is chosen by one random method

Players draw cards

Player 1 mulligans first

Player 2 mulligans second

Turn 1 begins

Nuances:

The second player mulligans after the first player, which provides a small informational advantage (seeing opponent's mulligan decisions can inform your own mulligan choices)

BF selection happens before turn order determination, as this can affect mulligan decisions

question: What happens if a new showdown is triggered while another showdown is already in progress?
answer:
Ruling: When a new showdown would start during another showdown, it enters a "Staged" state and waits until the first showdown ends before starting.

Sequence:

First showdown proceeds normally

New showdown enters Staged state

After first showdown ends, the Staged showdown begins

If multiple showdowns are Staged simultaneously, the active player chooses which starts first

Nuances:

This situation is very unlikely in 1v1 games

More likely to occur in 3+ player games where there are multiple battlefields

question: While you are contesting a battlefield, do you also control it?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not control the battlefield if you are the one contesting it.

Nuances:

You cannot cast cards that require controlling a battlefield (like Recruit the Vanguard) while contesting

You can only score each battlefield once per turn, either through conquer or hold

Moving a new unit into a previously scored battlefield does not trigger conquer effects again

question: What does rule 626.1.d say?
answer: Unable to determine - the thread only contains a reference to rule number 626.1.d without any discussion of its content, interpretation, or application.

question: How should a judge handle informing players about a wrong ruling that was made in a previous game?
answer:
Ruling: Inform the players of the correct ruling and apologize, but do not interrupt their current game to do so.

Sequence:

Wait until the players' current match is completed

Before the next round starts, inform them of the correct ruling

Apologize for the error

Move on without attempting to rewind or change past game results

question: Can a player use multiple reaction spells in sequence if they draw cards between them (e.g., using Stupefy, drawing a card, then using Retreat in response to the same spell)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, a player can use multiple reaction spells in sequence in response to the same spell on the chain, even if they draw cards between casting them.

Sequence:

Opponent casts a spell (e.g., Icathian Rain)

Player uses first reaction spell (e.g., Stupefy) which draws a card

Player can then use the newly drawn reaction spell (e.g., Retreat) in response to the same original spell

Nuances:

You cannot play spells while another spell is actively resolving - you must respond while the spell is on the chain, before it resolves

For Sabotage specifically, you must play Retreat in reaction to Sabotage being on the chain; once Sabotage resolves and they look at your hand, it's too late

question: Can you play a Legend in a different language than your deck?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, a player's Legend can be in a different language than their Main Deck or Rune Deck.

Nuances:

This rule exists to allow usage of overnumbered cards

question: Does Gemcraft Seer's ability work for tokens?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Gemcraft Seer's ability works for tokens because tokens are units.

Nuances:

Tokens count as units for the purposes of abilities that affect units

question: If Teemo (Strategist) reveals Nocturne on his defend ability, can Nocturne be summoned to the Teemo battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Nocturne can be summoned to the Teemo battlefield when revealed by Teemo's defend ability.

Nuances:

This assumes the Teemo player controls that battlefield, which is almost always true when the defend trigger happens

A corner case exists where Strategist wouldn't control the battlefield: active defense where you use an effect like Ride the Wind to move Teemo into an open showdown

question: When playing Falling Star, when must both targets be chosen - can the player choose one target, let it resolve, then choose the second target, or must both targets be chosen at once when the card resolves?
answer:
Ruling: When Falling Star resolves, both reflexive triggers are put on the chain and both targets must be chosen at that time, before either trigger resolves. Once targets are chosen and the triggers are on the chain, they cannot be changed.

Sequence:

Play Falling Star (no targets chosen yet)

Falling Star resolves → both triggers are put on the chain and targets are chosen now for both triggers

First trigger resolves

Second trigger resolves

Opponents can react between each step

Nuances:

If a unit is removed before Falling Star resolves (e.g., via Retreat), the triggers can only target remaining legal units when they are put on the chain, potentially forcing the caster to target their own units

This differs from spells like Singularity, which require targets to be chosen when casting the spell, not when it resolves

The reflexive triggers are not optional - if there are legal targets, they must be chosen

Deflect costs are paid after targets are chosen for the reflexive triggers, and the caster can choose not to pay these costs, which removes the trigger from the chain

question: Does blue Viktor get two Recruits after using Portal Rescue to target a friendly non-recruit unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Viktor gets two Recruits when Portal Rescue targets a friendly non-recruit unit - one for playing Portal Rescue and one for playing the unit that was banished and played back to base.

Nuances:

If you target Viktor himself with Portal Rescue on an opponent's turn, you only get 1 Recruit (not 0) because Viktor can see himself being played as a card on an enemy's turn, but Portal Rescue itself does not give a Recruit since Viktor is pending at Portal's resolution.

Viktor's effect only triggers when a card fully resolves, not while cards are pending.

question: Do reactions take priority over actions and unit abilities in resolution order?
answer:
Ruling: Base speed, action, and reaction only determine when you can play something, not the order anything resolves. The order things resolve is Last In First Out (LIFO) off the chain - the last thing to go onto the chain will be the first thing to resolve.

Sequence:

When combat starts, the chain is initially populated with "when I attack" triggers

Then "when I defend" triggers are added

Then both players can play reactions

Once everyone passes, the chain starts resolving with the latest played item first

Nuances:

You cannot play an action after an ability has already gone on the chain

If multiple cards are discarded simultaneously, you choose the order their effects go on the chain

question: Can you pay one cost to hide Teemo directly from the champion zone, and what is the cost if Teemo is on the board?
answer:
Ruling: You can hide Teemo for 1 cost from hand or from champion zone. If Teemo is on the board, it costs 2 total (you must use Teemo Legend to return the unit to hand for 1 cost, then hide it for 1 cost).

Sequence:

If Teemo is on the board: Use Teemo Legend to return the unit to hand (1 cost)

Then hide Teemo from hand (1 cost)

Total: 2 cost

Nuances:

Hiding directly from champion zone costs only 1

Hiding from the board requires the two-step process above

question: If Viktor, Leader is in base and two units die simultaneously at a battlefield during combat, how many Recruit tokens are created?
answer:
Ruling: You create one Recruit token for each non-Recruit unit that died. If two non-Recruit units die simultaneously, you create two Recruit tokens.

Nuances:

If Viktor himself dies in the combat, you create 0 Recruits

The simultaneous deaths are treated as separate instances for Viktor's ability, similar to how Wraith of Echoes can choose which death triggers its "first time" ability when multiple units die simultaneously

This differs from abilities like Leona Radiant Dawn that specifically say "one or more" which would only trigger once for multiple simultaneous events

question: What happens when an opponent uses Challenge and then you Rebuke the targeted card? Do actions resolve simultaneously, and would the unit still take damage?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot use Rebuke in response to Challenge because Rebuke is an action and cannot be used when something else is on the chain.

Nuances:

You could use Gust (a reaction) instead if the unit is small enough

When using Gust, it would resolve first (most recently-added thing resolves first), and Challenge would do nothing since the challenged unit no longer exists

question: Can you hide a card from your hand to a battlefield you control when you are not conquering?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can hide a card to a battlefield you control even when not conquering. Hiding is a Discretionary Action that requires you control the battlefield, the card is in your hand, it's your turn, and there's no active chain or showdown.

Sequence:

Must be during your turn

No chain or showdown can be active

Card must be in your hand

Must hide to a battlefield you control

Nuances:

You can only have 1 hidden card at a battlefield at a time unless a battlefield effect allows additional hidden cards

You cannot activate a hidden card the same turn you hide it

Hiding does not create a chain

Hiding is different from playing a card

question: Can you buff a unit that already has a buff, and does it replace the existing buff?
answer:
Ruling: A unit cannot have multiple buffs unless specifically stated (like "any number of buffs"). You cannot replace an existing buff by buffing the unit again.

Nuances:

You can still choose to target a buffed unit with another buff effect, but on resolution nothing happens and the unit is not considered to have been buffed again.

question: Does Ravenborn Tome buff all of the reflexive triggers from Icathian Rain, or does it not buff them because they're not considered spells?
answer:
Ruling: Ravenborn Tome buffs all instances of damage from Icathian Rain's reflexive triggers. The spell itself is the source of the damage dealt by its reflexive triggers, so the Tome's bonus applies to all of them.

Sequence:

Play Icathian Rain (the spell itself deals no damage initially)

Each reflexive trigger causes Icathian Rain to deal damage

Each instance of damage gets the +1 bonus from Tome because Icathian Rain is the source

Nuances:

The key rule is that when an ability is the source of damage, it is in addition to the spell that created that ability - meaning the spell itself is still considered the source

This would also apply to lingering effects: if a spell dealt damage over multiple turns, it would get the bonus each time

The spell playing itself may deal no damage, but the reflexive triggers it creates still count as the spell dealing damage

question: Does Karma Channeler's ability trigger when you pay recycling costs for runes?
answer:
Ruling: No, Karma Channeler does not trigger when you pay recycling costs for runes. Runes are not cards and Karma received errata clarifying she only cares about Main Deck cards, which runes are not part of.

Nuances:

Karma Channeler will trigger off her own Vision if you recycle the card itself

Recycling runes never triggered Karma, but the errata made this more clear

question: If Rell contests an occupied Reavers Row with one enemy unit, and the defender moves back with Reavers Row's trigger, will Rell still get her on attack trigger to play and attach an equipment?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Rell will still get her on attack trigger even if the defender moves back. Once a showdown starts, it finishes even if all units leave the battlefield.

Sequence:

Rell's on attack trigger goes on the chain first

Reavers Row trigger goes on the chain second (resolves first as topmost item)

Defender moves back

Rell's trigger resolves, allowing her to play and attach equipment

Nuances:

If Rell attaches Recurve Bow during this sequence, the bow's on attack trigger does NOT activate because Rell has already been given the attacker designation before the attachment happens

The bow attachment resolves after the defending unit has already retreated in this scenario

question: Can Sett's ability save a unit that has the Temporary keyword from Fading Memories?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Sett's ability can save a unit with Temporary from being sacrificed.

Nuances:

The unit will still have the Temporary keyword after being saved, so it will need to be saved again at the start of your next beginning phase.

question: Can an opponent use reactions (like Gust) during your turn if you only played units with no triggers and are passing turn?
answer:
Ruling: No, the opponent cannot use reactions during your turn if you only played units and passed turn without any triggers occurring. Reactions can only be played when a player has priority, which requires either a chain/stack of abilities or a showdown.

Sequence:

You play units during your turn

If those units have no "when I'm played" triggers, no stack is created

You pass turn with no end-of-turn triggers

No priority window exists for the opponent to react

Turn passes to opponent

Nuances:

Reactions can be played "at any time" on a player's own turn, but "any time" is defined as "when you have priority"

Priority requires either triggered abilities going on the stack or a showdown

Phase changes, placing units, moving, and adds cannot be reacted to unless accompanied by a triggered ability or showdown

If units like Annie or Sona with end-of-turn triggers were played, that would create a priority window

question: Can a spell that targets something be played if there are no valid targets?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play a spell that targets if there are no legal targets available. You must have legal targets to put a spell on the chain and finalize it.

Nuances:

Spells that say "up to ___ targets" or "any number of targets" can choose to target zero units

Falling Star is a special case because the spell itself doesn't target (the reflexive triggers it generates do target), so you can play it without a legal target and it just won't generate its triggers

question: Do all units everywhere heal after a combat concludes?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, all units heal after a combat concludes and at the end of turn.

Nuances:

Units heal even if they were not involved in the combat

You can heal damaged units by invoking a combat with other units

question: Do abilities stack per activated gear in Riftbound?
answer: Ruling: Yes, abilities stack per activated gear. The trigger will occur each time its conditions are met.

question: When playing a green Repeat spell that targets purple Irelia (who reduces the cost of spells that choose her by 1), does the cost reduce by 1 or 2?
answer:
Ruling: The cost is reduced by 1 energy total. Repeat creates an additional cost to choose the same target twice, but it's still one spell, so Irelia's cost reduction applies only once.

Nuances:

If a Repeat spell targets two different Irelias, you get double discount (one reduction from each Irelia)

The final cost to play a Repeat spell targeting one Irelia is 3 energy

question: Does Cull the Weak trigger Dreaming Tree's card draw ability when you choose a friendly unit at that battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Cull the Weak does not trigger Dreaming Tree. Dreaming Tree only triggers when you target a friendly unit with a spell, and Cull the Weak does not target (the choices are made on resolution by each player, not when the spell is put on the chain).

Nuances:

Dreaming Tree uses the word "choose" in its card text, but according to designer intent communicated to judges, this specifically means "target" despite the plain English reading suggesting otherwise

The core rules define two types of choices for spells: targeting choices (made when putting the spell on the chain) and non-targeting choices (made on resolution), but only targeting choices trigger Dreaming Tree

Rule 352.10.e specifies that choices made by other players (like in Cull the Weak) are not targets

This ruling contradicts a strict reading of the card text and rules as written, but reflects the intended design and how it has been judged at official Riot events

There is an official request for clarification in feedback channels to resolve the discrepancy between the plain text reading and the intended ruling

question: When an opponent plays Falling Star targeting multiple units, how should they communicate the order of triggers, and how can I get them to specify the order without revealing I have a Hidden Zhonya's?
answer:
Ruling: When Falling Star resolves, the player must declare which units the triggers are targeting and communicate what order the triggers will happen in (either which goes on the chain last or which resolves first).

Sequence:

Player casts Falling Star

Player must specify targets and order (e.g., "3 to X then 3 to Y")

Triggers go on chain in declared order

Opponent can respond with cards like Zhonya's

Nuances:

Players should be declaring this order by default when casting Falling Star

If order is unclear or not communicated, you should ask for clarification to avoid miscommunication

To avoid revealing information, ask for clear trigger ordering every time they cast Falling Star (not just when you have a response), so they learn to play correctly and you don't telegraph when you have relevant cards

If a player deliberately avoids providing clear representation of their triggers, you can call a judge

If they say "targeting X and Y" without specifying order, you can make an assumption based on the order stated, but this risks miscommunication

question: Does hiding a card (putting it facedown on the battlefield) start a chain?
answer: Ruling: No, hiding a card does not open a chain.

question: When a unit with Deathknell dies while possessed, who controls the trigger?
answer: Ruling: The owner of the unit controls the Deathknell trigger, not the player who possessed it. The trigger is created from the trash.

question: If Warwick Hunter Champion (with 'kill all damaged enemy units here' ability) is killed by Hidden Blade in response to his attack declaration, does his ability still kill a damaged Caitlyn on the battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Warwick dies and Caitlyn lives. When Hidden Blade (a reaction spell) resolves first and kills Warwick, his ability still triggers but fails to resolve because it cannot find the "here" information it needs after Warwick has left the battlefield.

Sequence:

Warwick declares attack, triggering his ability

Opponent plays Hidden Blade (reaction spell) in response

Hidden Blade resolves first, killing Warwick

Warwick's ability attempts to resolve but fails because Warwick is no longer on the battlefield and the ability cannot find "here"

Caitlyn survives

Nuances:

Unlike Magic: The Gathering, Riftbound has no "Last Known Information" rule - if an object leaves the zone it was expected to be in, effects that reference it fail to find the needed information

The ability does go on the stack/chain, but it fails to resolve properly rather than being removed from the stack

question: Can you play Nocturne (found via Stacked Deck during a showdown) to a contested battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot play a unit to a battlefield you do not control. As an attacker, you never control the contested battlefield, so you cannot play Nocturne to it mid-showdown. As a defender, the battlefield is contested but still under your control, so you can play units to it during the showdown.

Sequence:

Attacker goes to a contested battlefield

Showdown occurs

If attacker plays Stacked Deck and finds Nocturne, they cannot play it to the contested battlefield (no control)

If defender plays Stacked Deck and finds Nocturne, they can play it to the contested battlefield (still have control despite it being contested)

Nuances:

A battlefield can be both contested AND controlled by the defender simultaneously

Control, not contested status, determines whether you can play units to a battlefield

question: What are tokens in Riftbound, what represents them, and what do they do?
answer:
Ruling: Token units are units created by effects that do not count as cards. They can be represented by anything players agree on (official token cards, dice, etc.), exist outside the game when not in use, and are kept off to the side (not in your deck).

Sequence:

Tokens are created by effects as specified

They enter the board with stats (might, etc.) as specified by the creating effect

When tokens leave the board for any reason (killed, sent to hand, etc.), they are destroyed and vanish back to ether rather than going to trash

Nuances:

Different token types exist (sprites have 3 might, recruits have 1 might)

The effect creating the token specifies its might

Tournament rules require tokens to be able to represent card state (exhausted, might, etc.)

question: In a best-of-3 match with decklists, do you have to designate a specific battlefield for game 1, or can you choose from your registered battlefields after seeing the opponent's champion?
answer:
Ruling: You do not have to designate a specific battlefield for game 1. Battlefields are registered as a group, and you select which one to use after legends and command centers are revealed, allowing you to counter-pick even in game 1.

Sequence:

Legends and command centers are revealed

Battlefield is selected from your registered group

Nuances:

A chosen champion is an element of deck construction and cannot be swapped in game 1, even when decklists are not in use

question: Can Ava play a hidden card to a battlefield you don't control?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ava can play a hidden card to a battlefield you don't control. You play the hidden card on the battlefield where Ava attacks, not where she hides.

Nuances:

You could pay 1 mind, play Hidden Blade from hand, and target a unit at a different battlefield than where Ava is hiding

question: Can an opponent react to Forge of the Future by casting a reaction that kills a unit to bring back Immortal Phoenix from trash before the recycle resolves, and would they then get to target a new card in trash?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, opponents can react to Forge of the Future's activation before it resolves. If they kill a unit with a reaction spell, Phoenix's trigger is added to the chain immediately and will resolve before Forge can, allowing Phoenix to be played from trash. However, the cards targeted for recycling are chosen on activation and cannot be changed - if Phoenix was declared as a recycle target and gets played, you lose that recycle.

Sequence:

Forge of the Future activates and targets cards in trash for recycling

Opponent can react to the activation before it resolves

If opponent kills a unit with a reaction spell, Phoenix's trigger is added to the chain immediately

Phoenix's trigger resolves before Forge resolves

Phoenix is played from trash

Forge resolves, but if Phoenix was targeted for recycle, that recycle is lost

Nuances:

Phoenix doesn't specify enemy unit, so you can kill your own units to trigger it

You could hypothetically react to Forge with a spell on your own unit to trigger Phoenix

question: When Trifarian Warcamp is played in an Ahri Legend deck and enemy units move to the occupied battlefield, do they get +1 Might from the battlefield before Ahri's -1 Might trigger resolves, resulting in them staying at their base Might?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the passive +1 Might from Trifarian Warcamp applies immediately when units finish moving to the battlefield, before Ahri's triggered ability resolves. The effects cancel out, leaving units at their base Might (e.g., 1 Might Recruits remain 1 Might).

Sequence:

Enemy units move to the occupied Trifarian Warcamp battlefield

Trifarian Warcamp's passive +1 Might applies immediately as units finish moving

Units become the Attacker, triggering Ahri's ability

Ahri's triggered ability goes on the chain and resolves, giving each attacking unit -1 Might

Net result: units return to their original Might value

Nuances:

Trifarian Warcamp is a passive effect, not a triggered ability, so it applies immediately rather than going on the chain

Any battlefield can be played with any Legend deck; there are no restrictions

question: When Kai'Sa conquers and tries to play a spell from the trash pile that has a conditional cost reduction (e.g., 'costs 2 less if first card played'), does Kai'Sa check the printed cost or the reduced cost to determine if the spell can be played?
answer:
Ruling: Kai'Sa checks the printed energy cost on the card, not any conditional reduced cost, to determine if a spell can be played from the trash pile.

Sequence:

Kai'Sa looks for cards with printed energy cost less than your current points

Only cards meeting this printed cost requirement are valid selections

If a card is validly selected (printed cost is less than points), then cost reductions would apply when actually casting it

Nuances:

If the spell's printed cost is already less than your points, you can select it with Kai'Sa and then the cost reduction would apply when casting

The cost reduction condition is evaluated after the card is selected, not during the selection process

question: In a 1v1 duel, if both players randomly select the same battlefield, do they play with the same battlefield or must they redraw until different battlefields are selected?
answer:
Ruling: You keep the same battlefields. There is no rule preventing both players from having the same battlefield in a 1v1 duel.

Nuances:

The only restriction on battlefields is in 2v2 format, where both teammates cannot bring the same battlefield.

question: In BO1 and BO3, how is first turn and battlefield selection determined?
answer:
Ruling: In BO1, battlefields are randomly selected. In BO3, battlefields are chosen by both players (each battlefield can only be used once per match). For the first game in both formats, first turn is chosen by the winner of any agreed upon random method (like rolling dice). In BO3, after the first game, the loser of the previous game decides who goes first.

Sequence:

Game 1: Random method determines who chooses first turn

Game 2 and beyond (BO3 only): Loser of previous game decides who goes first

Nuances:

In BO3, once a battlefield is used, it cannot be used again in the same match

Most players use "high roll" (rolling dice) as the random method

The random selection for first turn only applies to the first game

question: If I scored a holding point on a battlefield this turn, then left it, and my opponent took control of it, can I score again and trigger conquer effects if I take it back this same turn?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot score a second point or trigger conquer effects on a battlefield where you already scored a holding point this turn. You can gain control of it, but not conquer it.

Sequence:

You score a holding point on a battlefield

You leave the battlefield and opponent takes control

You move back to the battlefield

You gain control but do not score or conquer

Nuances:

You can only score 1 point per battlefield per turn

Conquering is attached to scoring, so no scoring means no conquering

Gaining control and conquering are different mechanics

question: Can you play an Action card after another Action card has resolved during a showdown?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, after one chain resolves during a showdown, a player can start another chain with an Action or Reaction spell. Each player will have an opportunity to play Action cards during a showdown.

Sequence:

Showdown begins

Attacker has Priority and Focus, can start a chain with an Action or Reaction spell

Priority passes to defender who can cast Reaction spells or pass

When both players pass, the chain resolves

Focus and Priority passes to the other player who can now start a new chain with an Action or Reaction spell

This continues until both players pass Focus in a row, then combat damage resolves

Nuances:

Both players need to pass Focus in a row to move to combat damage resolution

The player with Focus can start a new chain with Action or Reaction spells after the previous chain resolves

question: If you are at 12 runes and cannot channel for your turn, do you draw one more card?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not draw a card if you cannot channel. You simply do not channel at all.

Nuances:

Some learn-to-play videos incorrectly showed this rule, but it was a mistake

Ramp spells that draw cards when you can't channel may create confusion, as they seem like reminder text for channeling, but this is not how the base channeling rule works

question: If I have 2 Zhonya's Hourglasses and 1 of my units dies, do I have to activate both?
answer:
Ruling: No, only one Zhonya's Hourglass applies when a single unit dies.

Nuances:

If 2 of your units die at the same time, each Zhonya's will save one of them

With cards like GA and Soraka, you can order replacement effects to choose not to utilize your Zhonya's (if you can)

question: When do you choose targets for Falling Star's damage, and how does this interact with En Garde?
answer:
Ruling: You choose targets for Falling Star when you play it, but damage is allocated when it resolves. This means the opponent can see which units are targeted before deciding whether to use En Garde.

Sequence:

Play Falling Star and declare targets (e.g., unit A for 3 damage and unit B for 3 damage, or unit A for both instances of 3 damage)

Opponent can react with En Garde or other responses based on the declared targets

Falling Star resolves and deals the damage to the targeted units

Nuances:

You can target the same unit with both instances of 3 damage to ensure it dies

The opponent can see your targeting choices before deciding whether to use En Garde, allowing them to avoid wasting protection on a unit that would die anyway

question: How does Party Favors work in a 1v1 setting?
answer: Ruling: In a 1v1 game, your opponent chooses either cards or runes, and both players receive the corresponding benefit.

question: For Accelerate effects that allow units to enter ready, do you only tap an additional rune or do you also recycle a rune?
answer:
Ruling: For Accelerate abilities, you must both exhaust (tap) 1 energy rune of any color AND recycle 1 rune of the specified color shown in the Accelerate cost.

Sequence:

Pay the normal unit cost (e.g., 5 runes for Miss Fortune)

Exhaust 1 additional rune of any color for the energy cost

Recycle 1 rune of the color specified in the Accelerate cost (e.g., orange for Miss Fortune)

The unit enters play ready instead of exhausted

Nuances:

The energy cost (exhaust) can be paid with any color rune

The recycle cost must match the specific color shown in the Accelerate ability

question: Does Karma's ability trigger when recycling a rune to pay for Sett legend's ability, and if so, can the buff be given to the unit being recalled?
answer:
Ruling: Karma's ability does not trigger when recycling runes to pay for Sett legend's ability because runes are not cards.

Nuances:

Karma's card text specifically states that runes are not cards

For rules purposes, "cards" always refers to main deck cards, which runes are not

question: When defending a battlefield, if a player uses Ride the Wind to move Yasuo to that battlefield during combat, does Yasou's 'When I attack' ability trigger?
answer:
Ruling: Yasou's 'When I attack' ability does not trigger when moved to a battlefield where his controller is the defender. All units controlled by the defending player are considered defenders, regardless of when they arrive at the battlefield.

Sequence:

Attacker attacks the battlefield and passes without playing Actions

Defender plays Ride the Wind to move Yasou to the battlefield

Ride the Wind chain resolves (Yasou's ability does not trigger)

Focus passes back to the attacker, who can play Actions again

Nuances:

After Ride the Wind fully resolves, the attacker regains the opportunity to play Actions and could use cards like Last Breath at that point

question: Can Ekko's Deathknell ability untap runes during a showdown in time to kill a damaged opponent's unit before damage is cleared?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot untap runes and use them to kill damaged units before damage is cleared. By the time Ekko's Deathknell triggers, the showdown has already ended.

Sequence:

Units are killed first

Damage is cleared second

There is no opportunity to play cards between these steps

Nuances:

Once you reach damage calculation, do the resolution step, and perform the cleanup, nothing else can be done about the showdown

question: Can you have more than 1 hidden unit/spell/gear on the battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot have more than 1 hidden unit/spell/gear on the same battlefield object in general.

Nuances:

There is a card (the Bandle Tree) that modifies this limit and allows exceptions

question: What should be done when a player entered a wrong match result in round 1 that was only discovered in round 5, with playoffs upcoming?
answer:
Ruling: The Head Judge has final authority to decide how to resolve scorekeeping problems. In this case, when fixing the score would compromise tournament integrity too much due to the domino effect on Swiss pairings across multiple rounds, the result should not be changed.

Sequence:

Assess whether the tournament has playoffs and whether they have started

Evaluate how much fixing the score would compromise the tournament integrity given the domino effect on subsequent Swiss pairings

Consider whether the player who made the mistake should face penalties (though this may be harsh for a single tracking mistake, especially in lower level events)

Make a decision prioritizing the lesser evil that doesn't screw over other players

Nuances:

The Swiss aspect's integrity is technically compromised either way because players may have faced stronger/weaker opponents than they should have based on incorrect standings

In low level events without playoffs, you can simply fix the score and standings

Prevention is key: have a scorekeeper or Head Judge enter scores rather than letting players self-report, and warn players to properly track scores

question: How does Convergent Mutation interact with Teemo, Scout's "When you play me" trigger when played in response to the trigger being on the chain?
answer:
Ruling: When you flip Teemo and respond to his "When you play me" trigger by playing Convergent Mutation before the trigger resolves, Convergent Mutation resolves first (setting Teemo's Might equal to the targeted unit's current Might), then Teemo's trigger resolves (adding +3 to Teemo's Might). If you let Teemo's trigger resolve first, he gets +3 Might before Convergent Mutation sets his Might equal to the target.

Sequence:

Lee Sin attacks and passes priority

Reveal Teemo, "When you play me" trigger creates a chain

React with Convergent Mutation targeting Teemo and Mundo, no responses

Convergent Mutation resolves, setting Teemo to 8 Might (Mundo's current Might)

Mundo goes to 9 Might from Convergent Mutation entering trash

Teemo's trigger resolves, giving him +3 Might up to 11 Might

Combat resolves: 20 total Might (11 Teemo + 9 Mundo) vs 18 Lee Sin

Nuances:

Convergent Mutation snapshots the target unit's Might at time of resolution; later changes to that unit's Might don't retroactively affect the boosted unit

If Teemo's trigger had resolved before playing Convergent Mutation, Teemo would end at 8 Might total (not 11) because Mutation would overwrite the previous buff

question: If a card reduces a 2 might unit's might (without stating a minimum), does the unit die at 0 might?
answer:
Ruling: A unit with 0 might does not automatically die. It only dies if it has non-zero damage marked on it equalling or exceeding its might.

Sequence:

Unit's might is reduced to 0

Unit survives unless it has at least 1 damage marked on it

If it has 1 or more damage marked, it dies (since damage equals or exceeds its 0 might)

Nuances:

Units cannot have 0 marked damage, so damage must be at least 1 to trigger death

This interaction is intentional design

question: Can you use Sett - The Boss's Legend ability to recall a unit to base if they are already at base?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can use the ability to recall any unit that meets the condition in the replacement ability, even if they are already at base. The unit will still be exhausted.

Nuances:

The ability can be used on units already at base

The exhaustion effect still applies regardless of the unit's location

question: For Icathian Rain triggers with Viktor Leader, does the order matter for preventing Recruit spawns, and how should triggers be ordered?
answer:
Ruling: The order of triggers matters. Viktor should be targeted with the last trigger to go onto the chain (which resolves first) to prevent spawning Recruits when other units die.

Sequence:

Icathian Rain creates 6 reflexive triggers that resolve one by one

Each reflexive trigger is followed by a cleanup

Target Viktor with the last trigger added to the chain (so it resolves first)

This kills Viktor before other units die, preventing Recruit spawns

Nuances:

This differs from Unchecked Power where all units die together

Players typically just state the order they want triggers to resolve rather than specifying chain order

question: Can Flame Chompers be summoned directly to Zaun Warrens when discarded to conquer it, and can Flame Chompers be summoned during a showdown if discarded via instant speed effects like Get Excited?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Flame Chompers can be summoned directly to Zaun Warrens when discarded to conquer it. During a showdown, if you use an instant speed discard effect like Get Excited, you can summon Flame Chompers to the battlefield and add to total power pre-damage step if you control the battlefield (usually as the defender).

Nuances:

You need to control the battlefield to summon Flame Chompers during a showdown, which is typically the case when you are the defender

question: If you start your turn holding 1 battlefield (reaching 7 points), then lose control of it but take the other battlefield during the same turn, do you still win?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, this is a win. You do not need to actively hold both battlefields simultaneously to score the final point via conquest.

Sequence:

Start turn holding 1 battlefield, gaining a point (reaching 7)

Lose control of that battlefield during your turn

Take control of the other battlefield during the same turn

Win condition is met

Nuances:

You only need to have scored both battlefields at some point during that turn, not hold them simultaneously

question: If you Defy a hidden card that gets revealed in combat, does Ember Monk still get his bonus +2 might?
answer:
Ruling: No, Ember Monk does not get the bonus. Cards need to resolve to count as played for effects like Ember Monk.

Sequence:

Hidden card is revealed in combat

Defy is played as a react

The card is removed before it resolves

Since the card didn't resolve, it doesn't count as "played"

Ember Monk does not get the +2 might bonus

Nuances:

This same principle applies to other "when played" effects like Ravenbloom Student, Darius, and Legion

A card only counts as "played" if it resolves

question: When Teemo Strategist flips and triggers his ability to damage an enemy unit, and the enemy uses Bullet Time in response, does Bullet Time kill Teemo before his ability resolves or after?
answer:
Ruling: Bullet Time can only be activated after the chain that includes Teemo's ability has fully resolved. Teemo's ability resolves first, then Bullet Time can be used.

Sequence:

Teemo Strategist flips and his ability triggers

Teemo's ability fully resolves (damage is dealt)

Bullet Time can then be activated

question: How does Void Gate interact with Volibear Furious's damage splitting ability?
answer:
Ruling: Void Gate increases the total pool of damage that Volibear splits among units. Instead of splitting 5 damage, Volibear splits 6 damage among the targets.

Nuances:

Volibear is currently the only effect that splits damage, which is why it receives specific treatment in the rules

The damage increase applies to the total pool before splitting, not to each instance or target

question: When Watcher targets a defending Stalwart Poro (currently 2 Might), what is the Poro's Might at different stages: after Watcher's ability resolves and then during combat when the Defender ability triggers?
answer:
Ruling: When Watcher's ability resolves, Stalwart Poro's Might goes to 1 (minimum floor applies). When Watcher enters combat with the Poro and attacker/defender are designated, the Poro becomes 2 Might with shield due to its Defender ability.

Sequence:

Stalwart Poro starts at 2 Might while defending

Watcher is played and its ability resolves, reducing Poro to 1 Might (minimum of 1 applies)

Watcher moves to combat with Poro

When attacker and defender are designated, Poro's Defender ability triggers, making it 2 Might with shield

question: Can Charm be used to move an opponent to their ally's field to make them fight each other in a 2v2 game?
answer: Ruling: No, you cannot use Charm to move an opponent to their ally's battlefield. It is an illegal choice and cannot be done.

question: When you conquer a battlefield, do you immediately control it before resolving conquer effects (e.g., can a unit revealed by Rek'sai's conquer effect be played at the newly conquered battlefield)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you immediately control a battlefield when you conquer it, before conquer effects resolve. Units revealed by conquer effects can be played at the newly conquered battlefield.

Sequence:

Conquer the battlefield

Control is established

Conquer effects happen

question: When Volibear and Kayn fight and Kayn triggers his ability to not take damage, what happens to the showdown if neither unit dies?
answer:
Ruling: At the end of combat, if units from both sides remain, the attacker's units are recalled to base.

Sequence:

Combat occurs between Volibear and Kayn

Kayn triggers his ability and does not take damage

Neither unit kills the other

At end of combat, attacker's units are recalled to base

question: Do judges receive anything to progress through tiers (e.g., points toward Level 2/3) for judging at Nexus Nights/Skirmishes, or do they get any promos?
answer:
Ruling: No information about the judge program progression, tier advancement, or judge promos has been released yet.

Nuances:

This applies to judging at Nexus Nights and Skirmishes

No details are currently available about how judges advance through levels

question: Is there a time limit for overtime turns in Riftbound, and can stores implement their own time limits?
answer:
Ruling: Overtime in Riftbound is untimed (5 turns with point total determining winner/draw). Tournament officials are encouraged to watch matches and prevent slow play, but there are no timed turns.

Nuances:

Stores can potentially implement their own timing rules for practical reasons (like store closing times), but this is not official

Players should be clearly informed when non-standard timing rules are being used

Adding time limits to turns creates complexity around what constitutes slow play versus legitimate thinking time

Magic does not have timed turns in overtime, but judges at large events will watch matches and prompt players who take too long

question: Does retaining priority when you control the next item on the chain mean you can play multiple reactions back-to-back in a showdown before passing priority?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, when you play a spell, you retain priority and can play reactions back-to-back as many as you have resources for. Once you're done, you pass to the next player who will have a chance to play reactions.

Sequence:

Player plays a spell (Action or Reaction) and retains priority

Player can play additional Reactions to the chain without passing

When ready, player passes priority to opponent

Opponent can now play Reactions

Once all players pass in succession, resolve the topmost item on the chain

Nuances:

You cannot respond to an Action card with another Action card - Actions must start the chain

A chain can only be started by one item

Focus and Priority are different: Focus allows you to start a chain during showdowns (play Actions or Reactions when chain is empty), while Priority allows you to play Reactions when there's an open chain

Focus passes automatically when a chain finishes resolving during showdowns

When you pass priority during a chain, you retain Focus

question: When Ahri Inquisitive's effect triggers on Daring Poro, am I forced to give the -3 might and forced to pay the deflect cost?
answer:
Ruling: No, you are not forced to pay the deflect cost on triggered abilities. You can decline to pay the deflect cost when the trigger finalizes, which removes it from the chain as if it never happened.

Sequence:

Ahri's trigger goes onto the chain as pending

When the trigger finalizes and costs are paid, you can choose whether to pay the deflect cost

If you decline to pay deflect, the trigger is removed from the chain as if it never happened

Nuances:

This only applies to triggered abilities, not other ability types

Even if the Poro wasn't alone, you could still target it and decline the deflect cost

question: Can a player exhaust all their runes in response to a reaction speed spell that will kill their Ekko unit, even if they don't have costs to pay at that moment?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can exhaust your runes in response to the spell. Both the exhaust and recycle abilities of runes are at Reaction speed and can be used any time a reaction can be made.

Sequence:

Opponent casts reaction speed spell that will kill Ekko

You can exhaust all your runes in response at Reaction speed

Once the spell begins resolving and kills Ekko, you don't have another moment to react

The exhausted runes recycle when Ekko dies, giving you additional energy for the rest of the turn

Nuances:

Rune abilities can also be used mid-resolution when a card asks you to pay a cost, though this is not relevant to this scenario

The benefit is gaining more total energy for the turn (e.g., with 8 runes where 3 are exhausted, exhausting the other 5 before Ekko dies gives you 13 effective energy for the rest of the turn)

question: Can Pack of Wonders target cards in the trash to return them to hand?
answer:
Ruling: Pack of Wonders can only target cards on the board (gear, units, or hidden cards), not cards in the trash.

Nuances:

The card works with Treasure Chest because Treasure Chest triggers when it leaves the board (including when returned to hand), not when it goes to trash

The "owner's hand" specification in the card text refers to which hand the targeted card returns to, not which cards can be targeted

"Friendly gear, unit or hidden card" means friendly gear, friendly unit, or friendly facedown card

question: What is the timing/sequence for battlefield reveals during game setup?
answer:
Ruling: Battlefields are revealed after Champions are chosen but before turn order is determined.

Sequence:

Legend selection

Champion selection

Battlefield reveal

Turn order determination

Draw cards

Mulligan

question: Can you attack the same battlefield multiple times in one turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can attack the same battlefield multiple times in one turn. There is no limit to the number of combats per turn, and attacking a battlefield repeatedly to pick off defenders is a valid strategy.

Nuances:

The restriction that you can only score each battlefield once per turn does not limit how many times you can attack it

question: When activating Unlicensed Armory (which requires discarding as a cost) with Jinx, Rebel in play, what is the correct stack order?
answer:
Ruling: Unlicensed Armory goes on the chain first, then Jinx, Rebel's trigger goes on top of it.

Sequence:

Activate Unlicensed Armory (it goes on chain)

Pay costs including discarding a card

Jinx, Rebel's trigger goes on the chain on top of Armory

Nuances:

The discard being a cost does not change the sequencing - triggers do not interpose between paying costs and putting the ability on chain

Armory is an activated ability that can only be used at base speed

The ability goes on chain before costs are finalized and paid

question: How does Divine Judgement interact with hidden cards? Does it ignore them or do they get recycled as part of 'the rest'?
answer:
Ruling: Divine Judgement ignores hidden cards entirely. They are not selected and they are not recycled.

Nuances:

Hidden cards are not considered spells, units, or gear

Hidden cards are not units, gear, runes, or cards in hand, so they don't fall under the categories that get recycled by "recycle the rest"

question: Can Zhonya's be used to react at any time during damage assignment and control which unit survives?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot use Zhonya's to react during damage assignment or when damage is dealt. You must flip Zhonya's before combat damage (during the showdown while you still have priority). If multiple units die simultaneously to combat damage, the controller chooses which one to save.

Sequence:

Flip Zhonya's during the showdown before combat damage is assigned (while you have priority)

Combat damage is assigned in entirety

Combat damage is dealt simultaneously to all units

If multiple units die at once, the controller of those units chooses which one to save with Zhonya's

Nuances:

You cannot react to damage being assigned or dealt because those processes do not pass priority

The showdown must have ended before damage assignment, so there is nothing to react to at that point

To play a reaction outside of your turn, you need priority, which requires a chain

Priority is passed when you explicitly pass it or when a chain item resolves

question: If you refuse to play Deflect, does the entire card/ability resolve still? Specifically: Can you refuse Deflect on Stupefy and still draw a card, or refuse Deflect on First Mate targeting Qiyana and still get a 3/3 unit?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot refuse Deflect for spells or activated abilities (where payment and targeting happen simultaneously). You can refuse Deflect for triggered abilities, but the ability will still be countered if you do refuse.

Sequence:

If targeting happens at the same time as payment (like Stupefy), you cannot refuse Deflect

If the target comes later (like triggered abilities such as First Mate), you can refuse Deflect but the ability will fizzle

Nuances:

For First Mate specifically: Playing the unit and its triggered ability are completely separate things. You can play units without their triggers working correctly, so you would still get the 3/3 unit even if the triggered ability is countered by refusing Deflect

question: If a unit is damaged but not killed, and then their might is reduced to less than the damage on the unit, does the unit die?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if a unit's might is reduced below the amount of damage on it, the unit dies.

Nuances:

This interaction is noted as a reason why Kai'sa is particularly strong

question: Does Wraith of Echoes' ability trigger for token units?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Wraith of Echoes triggers for token units. Recruit tokens are not cards, but they are units, so they trigger Wraith of Echoes.

Nuances:

Recruit tokens are units but not cards

The card text specifically refers to "token unit" which confirms tokens trigger the ability

question: In a 3+ player game, how does chain priority work during a showdown between two non-adjacent players?
answer:
Ruling: Priority always passes in turn order following whoever got priority first. In a showdown between players 1 and 3, player 2 receives priority after player 1 (before player 3) because they are the next player in turn order.

Sequence:

Player 1 initiates showdown with player 3

Player 1 gets priority first

Player 2 receives Focus next as the next turn player

Priority continues in turn order

question: Can Forge of the Fluft's ability be used to attach an already attached equipment to a new unit?
answer: Ruling: Yes, Forge of the Fluft's ability can be applied to attach an already attached equipment to a new unit.

question: Can you use a basic rune ability reaction in response to an opponent tapping runes to gain mana before they play a spell?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot react to an opponent tapping runes for mana. Reactions that add mana cannot be responded to.

Nuances:

Tapping runes to generate mana is not an action that can be responded to with reactions

question: If Ezreal moves in as an attacker, kills the only defender with his effect, then the opponent uses Ride the Wind to bring in a new defender with lower might than Ezreal, who gets pushed back?
answer:
Ruling: Ezreal gets pushed back. He is the attacker.

Nuances:

Even though Ezreal has higher might than the new defender, the attacker is always the one who gets pushed back when a new defender enters after the original defender is removed

question: In a showdown, does the attacker or defender get priority first?
answer: Ruling: The attacker gets priority first in a showdown.

question: For Ezreal - Prodigy, what is considered an extra cost that his effect can reduce?
answer:
Ruling: Optional additional costs are ones that use the words "may" and "as an additional cost" (or "may" and "as a cost to play"). Repeat and accelerate are the two most common examples.

Nuances:

Equip is not an optional additional cost; it's the cost of an activated ability

Hidden is not an optional additional cost; hiding a card is a game action with a cost, not an additional cost to play a card or effect

Hard Bargain's "unless its controller pays 2" is not an optional additional cost; it's paying to get a separate effect (not countering your spell)

Deflect is not reduced by Ezreal because it's not optional

To be an optional additional cost, it must be both optional AND additional (not just the regular cost of playing the card)

question: When a player accidentally sees an extra card while drawing, what is the remedy? Should recycled cards be separated before shuffling the extra card back?
answer:
Ruling: The player receives a warning and shuffles the extra card back into the random portion of the deck (not including recycled or mulligan cards). If this is the third warning of the same type, it escalates to a Game Loss.

Sequence:

Separate any recycled and mulligan cards from the deck

Shuffle the extra card into the random portion of the deck

Issue a warning (or Game Loss if it's the third offense)

Nuances:

If a player doesn't remember how much they've recycled, attempt to determine it based on the current game state

question: If Fiora gains Mighty during combat (after being declared as a defender), does she get the +1 from Shield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Fiora gets the +1 from Shield when she gains Mighty during combat, even after being declared as a defender.

Nuances:

Shield and Assault are passive "while" effects, not triggered "when" abilities

They do not use the chain and are always active when their conditions are met

If Fiora gains Mighty from Shield itself (like from Fortified Position), she gets both bonuses at once

question: Does attaching an equipment count as selecting/choosing the unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, equipping does choose a unit.

Nuances:

The previous Comprehensive Rules explicitly stated that attaching cards to others does not count as selecting

This was expected to change in the updated Spirit Forged CR (version 1.2)

The rule reference is 744.1.c.2 in the new CR

question: What cards can be played to trigger 'when you play a spell' effects without affecting the board state?
answer:
Ruling: You can play Bullet Time to deal 0 damage (even with units on the battlefield), and you can play Icathian Rain/Falling Star with no units on the board. These will trigger 'when you play a spell' effects.

Nuances:

Bullet Time can deal 0 damage even if the battlefield isn't empty

If you control a unit and play Falling Star/Icathian Rain, the triggered abilities they create must target legal targets if any exist, and your own units are legal targets

For Ravenbloom Student and similar effects, only the initial spell (Rain/Falling Star) counts as +1 spell played; the triggered reflex abilities do not count as additional spells played

question: If Warwick's ability triggers when killing a unit, does that unit still deal combat damage or is it taken out of play?
answer:
Ruling: Warwick's ability triggers and resolves during the Initial chain when Warwick is made an attacker, killing the targeted unit before the combat damage step occurs. The killed unit does not deal combat damage.

Sequence:

Warwick is made an attacker

Warwick's attack trigger goes on the chain during the Initial chain

The ability resolves, killing the target unit

Combat damage step occurs (but the killed unit is already gone)

Nuances:

Bullet Time can be used to move Warwick into a battlefield controlled by an opponent, killing all enemies before combat damage

Flurry of Blades allows you to deal damage while Warwick's ability is still on the chain

Warwick's ability cannot trigger across multiple battlefields in the same turn because once combat finishes at one battlefield, all units (including those at other battlefields) heal all damage

question: When an opponent attempts to conquer an uncontrolled battlefield and you Zenith Blade your own unit there during the showdown: (1) Can you play Shen on that battlefield during the showdown? (2) If your opponent stuns your unit during the showdown, who retreats when it resolves?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot play Shen on the battlefield during the showdown because no one controls it yet. If your opponent stuns your unit during the showdown, only the opponent's unit retreats (as the attacker), while your stunned unit can still take the spot and establish control at the end of the showdown.

Sequence:

Opponent initiates showdown to conquer uncontrolled battlefield (becoming the attacker)

You play Zenith Blade to move your unit to the battlefield

During showdown, you cannot play Shen because you don't control the battlefield yet

If opponent stuns your unit, showdown resolves with opponent's unit retreating as the attacker

Your stunned unit remains and establishes control over the battlefield

Nuances:

A stunned unit can still take a battlefield spot and establish control at the end of a showdown

The opponent is designated as the attacker because they contested the uncontrolled battlefield on their turn, which is why their unit retreats when combat ends

question: Does Symbol of the Solari's tie effect recall units from all battlefields or just the battlefield where the tied combat occurred?
answer:
Ruling: Symbol of the Solari only recalls units from the battlefield where the tied combat occurred, not from all battlefields.

Nuances:

The card text could be read as affecting all battlefields because it says "recall ALL units", but this has been clarified via errata

A tie occurs when both sides still have units remaining after combat damage is dealt

Ties commonly happen when units are stunned or have low might

question: If an opponent plays Falling Comet targeting a unit at a battlefield, and you react with Flash to move the unit to base, does Falling Comet still resolve and destroy the unit?
answer:
Ruling: If you move your unit back to base with Flash, Falling Comet will not have a valid target on resolution and will not deal damage to the unit.

Nuances:

Falling Comet specifies "at a battlefield" as part of its targeting requirement

When the target is no longer at a battlefield upon resolution, the spell loses its valid target

question: Are players allowed to freely communicate with each other during Free for All mode in Riftbound?
answer: Ruling: Yes, players can freely communicate with any other player during Free for All mode. The social aspect is a core component of that game mode.

question: How do reactions and actions interact with Falling Star, specifically when can someone react and when do you choose targets?
answer:
Ruling: You choose all targets for Falling Star's reflexive triggers at the same time, before either trigger resolves. Players can react at three different points during Falling Star's resolution.

Sequence:

Players can react before Falling Star resolves

After Falling Star resolves, the reflexive triggers go on the chain and you choose all targets at once

Players can react before either reflexive trigger has resolved

The first trigger resolves and deals 3 damage (if able)
