Choose and reveal Battlefields (method depends on type of play)

Determine turn order and first player

Draw 4 cards and mulligan in turn order

Nuances:

Legend, Champion, and Battlefield zones are open information (not facedown zones)

For best-of-one matches, battlefields are randomly selected

For best-of-three matches, players choose one battlefield each game but cannot use the same battlefield twice

question: If Aurora triggers during my end step and I play Deadbloom to conquer Targon's Peak, do I get to ready two runes before my opponent's turn?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not get to ready two runes. The end of turn triggering window has already passed when Aurora triggers during your end step.

Nuances:

You would still score from conquering Targon's Peak, as scoring is not an end of turn effect

End turn triggers happen only once; once all current end turn effects have triggered, no new end of turn effects will trigger

question: When a unit dies during a chain resolution, does cleanup happen immediately and does deathknell trigger before the rest of the chain resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Cleanup happens every time an item on the chain resolves. If cleanup causes a deathknell trigger, that trigger is added as the most recent item on the chain.

Sequence:

An item on the chain resolves

Cleanup happens immediately

If a unit died, its deathknell trigger is added to the chain as the most recent item

The chain continues resolving with the deathknell now on top

question: Can you use Unchecked Power to kill all units at a battlefield, then respond to the Deathknell trigger by flipping a Hidden unit to maintain control of the battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot do this. When Unchecked Power resolves, there is a cleanup that kills the Deathknell unit and removes the Hidden card before the Deathknell effect triggers, because you have already lost control of the battlefield.

Sequence:

Unchecked Power resolves

Cleanup occurs

Deathknell unit dies and Hidden card is sent to trash (due to loss of battlefield control)

Deathknell effect triggers (but Hidden card is already in trash)

Nuances:

This is a known issue that also occurs with Conquer triggers after losing control of a battlefield

Hidden is planned to be reworked to address this type of interaction

question: Should players exchange deck lists with their opponents at the beginning of a match in Summoner's Skirmish Competitive OPL tournaments?
answer:
Ruling: Deck lists are for organizers and judges to perform deck checks and ensure deck legality, and should not be given to opponents.

Nuances:

The tournament rules make no mention of letting opponents see lists

Tournament organizers could theoretically decide to implement open deck lists, though this would be non-standard

Open lists can help smaller judge teams catch pre-siding violations

Open lists remove a competitive element from the game

question: Does Vi's might boost from recycling cards persist after the player ends their turn?
answer:
Ruling: The might boost only lasts until the end of the turn in which the cards were recycled. Once the player ends their turn, the effect is gone.

Sequence:

Player recycles cards during their turn

Vi gains +X might (where X is the number of cards recycled)

Player ends their turn

The might boost is removed

Nuances:

When recycling cards with Vi, you can choose which cards from trash to recycle

Cards are recycled to the bottom of the deck

If recycling multiple cards in the same instance, they must be placed randomly at the bottom of the deck

If recycling one card at a time, randomization is not required

question: Does Fizz Trickster work with Drag Under since the card energy is reduced to 3?
answer:
Ruling: Fizz Trickster does NOT work with Drag Under. Cards like Fizz Trickster look at the base cost (printed number) on the card, not the final modified cost.

Nuances:

This works the same way as Defy with Sky Splitter - it checks the printed energy cost

Cost reductions like Drag Under do not change what Fizz Trickster sees

question: If Warwick moves into the battlefield before damaging units with an action spell, does Warwick still kill them, or should damage be applied before moving Warwick in order for him to trigger?
answer:
Ruling: Warwick triggers immediately when moving into combat, but only units already damaged when the trigger resolves will die. Action spells cannot be played in response to Warwick's trigger because a chain already exists and only Reaction speed spells can be used.

Sequence:

Warwick moves into combat and his "When I attack" ability triggers, forming the initial chain

Only Reaction speed spells can be played in response to this trigger

When Warwick's trigger resolves, he kills any units that are damaged at that moment

After the chain empties, Action spells can be played, but Warwick only checks for damaged units once when his trigger resolves

Nuances:

If you damage units with a Reaction speed spell (like Flurry of Blades) in response to Warwick's trigger, those units will be damaged when Warwick's trigger resolves and will die

When multiple "When I attack" triggers occur simultaneously (like Anivia and Warwick), you can choose the order to place them on the chain

question: When using Mystic Reversal on Time Warp, how many turns does the player who takes control of the spell get?
answer:
Ruling: You take the extra turn from Time Warp, then you take your normal turn (total of two turns).

Sequence:

Take the extra turn granted by Time Warp

Take your normal turn

question: Can you move several characters at one time in Riftbound, and does movement end your turn?
answer:
Ruling: You can move multiple units with the standard move as long as they all have the same destination. Movement does not end your turn; it only taps the creatures, and the turn ends when you decide to pass.

Nuances:

Moving multiple units only works for standard moves

Special moves (like Yasuo legend ability) can only move a single unit

If a special move starts a showdown, that unit will be alone

question: Can you play a unit directly onto a battlefield you control?
answer:
Ruling: You can play a unit directly onto a battlefield you control. You don't move it there; you simply play it there.

Sequence:

Control a battlefield

Play a unit directly to that battlefield (it enters exhausted)

Nuances:

This can be done during combat after conquering a battlefield if you still have mana remaining

The unit is played exhausted to the battlefield

question: If Imperial Decree is played, does playing Stupefy kill units?
answer: Ruling: No, Stupefy does not kill units when Imperial Decree is in play because Stupefy does not deal damage.

question: If Imperial Decree is active and combat damage kills a unit, does it kill the unit twice, breaking through Zhonya's protection?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Imperial Decree will kill the unit even after Zhonya's saves it from combat damage. The unit dies twice - once from combat damage (prevented by Zhonya's) and once from Imperial Decree's delayed trigger.

Sequence:

Combat damage is dealt between equal might units

Imperial Decree's delayed trigger is added as pending

Immediate cleanup occurs: damaged units are killed and Imperial Decree's trigger is finalized

Zhonya's replaces the death from combat damage and is removed from the board

Imperial Decree's trigger resolves and kills the unit again

Nuances:

The damage is only relevant for adding Imperial Decree's effect to the chain; when the effect resolves, it simply kills the unit regardless of current damage state

It doesn't matter whether Zhonya's was hidden or already revealed before the combat

question: When using Baited Hook to kill Watchful Sentry (which has a deathknell), what is the order of resolution for the deathknell trigger, the card played from Baited Hook, and Karma's trigger?
answer:
Ruling: When Baited Hook kills Watchful Sentry, all pending triggers finalize in the order they went on the chain: deathknell finalizes first, then the unit played with Baited Hook finalizes and resolves immediately, then Karma's trigger finalizes last (and can choose the unit played with Hook).

Sequence:

Baited Hook ability goes on the chain targeting Sentry

Baited Hook resolves: controller kills Sentry (deathknell pending), looks at 5 cards, banishes and plays one (that card pending), recycles the rest (Karma trigger pending)

All pending items finalize in chain order: deathknell first, then the played unit (which resolves immediately, with any WYPM pending), then Karma trigger

After cleanup, if there's a WYPM it finalizes

Players get priority between each item resolving on the chain

Nuances:

Karma can choose the unit played with Baited Hook since it finalizes after that unit

If the played unit has a WYPM (When You Play Me), it becomes pending on the chain and finalizes after another cleanup step

question: Can you play a hidden Zhonya's from a battlefield in response to a Deathkneel trigger during combat cleanup to save a different unit, and what happens to the Zhonya's?
answer:
Ruling: There is no clear window to play Zhonya's from hidden during combat cleanup. According to the rules, no Focus or Priority is passed during a cleanup (320.1), which would prevent playing the hidden Zhonya's in response to a Deathkneel trigger. However, there is debate about whether priority is gained between the Special Cleanup and the "clear contested status" step (440.1.b) of Combat Cleanup.

Sequence:

Unit dies during combat, triggering Deathkneel

Special Cleanup occurs (which includes regular Cleanup procedures)

During Cleanup, all gear at battlefields is recalled to base (322.5)

Hidden cards at battlefields not controlled by the same player are removed to trash

Contested status is cleared (440.1.b)

Nuances:

Some interpret the rules to allow priority after Special Cleanup but before clearing contested status (312.2.c), which would allow playing Zhonya's while the battlefield is still contested

This interpretation is disputed and likely not the intended interaction

Hidden units must be played to their battlefield, but gear (including Zhonya's) is always played to base regardless of where it was hidden

The question has been submitted for official clarification but no response has been received yet

question: Can you cast spells (specifically non-Action spells like Super Mega Death Rocket) during your teammate's turn in 2v2 when the game is in a neutral state?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, players may play spells during their teammate's turn in 2v2, as long as the timing rules of the spell apply and the game is in the appropriate state.

Nuances:

Actions can only be used to start a chain, never while a chain is already open (Closed State)

Spells that are not Actions cannot be played during a showdown

In a neutral state with no open chain, either teammate can play an Action during their team's turn

Non-Action spells like Super Mega Death Rocket can be cast on a teammate's turn if timing rules allow

question: Can you pay the accelerate cost for a card found with Baited Hook to have it enter ready?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you can pay the accelerate cost for a card found with Baited Hook to have it enter ready.

question: When can Sett: Brawler's ability to remove a buff to give might be used - is it an action/reaction or can it be used whenever?
answer: Ruling: The ability is standard speed, meaning it can only be used on your turn outside of chains or showdowns. All effects without ACTION or REACTION keywords are standard speed, and there are no effects that can be used "whenever".

question: How should a judge handle a missed Zaun Wardens conquer trigger, and should the player be given a choice about whether to resolve it and take a warning?
answer:
Ruling: Judges should not give players choices about whether to take warnings. For missed triggers, if it's still the current turn, it's the opponent's courtesy whether to allow the trigger to resolve retroactively. If the turn has passed, the trigger is lost. The opponent who didn't notice the missed trigger receives a Failure to Maintain Game State warning (tracking only, never upgraded).

Sequence:

If trigger is missed during the current turn: opponent decides whether to allow retroactive resolution

If turn has passed: trigger is lost and cannot be resolved

Opponent receives Failure to Maintain Game State warning (tracking only)

Nuances:

Zaun triggers should be considered advantageous to the controller even though they include a discard cost, so if forgotten they result in a warning and the trigger should be resolved according to the appropriate remedy

Violations that are detrimental to the player generally don't have penalties

Giving players choices about penalties invites metagaming and should be avoided

question: If a player scores a hold point from a battlefield, then moves their last unit out (making it uncontrolled), then moves another unit into that same battlefield during the same turn, does a showdown occur and can they score again?
answer:
Ruling: The battlefield becomes uncontrolled when the last unit leaves. When a unit enters that battlefield, a showdown occurs because the player is attempting to gain control of a battlefield they don't control. However, the player does not score or conquer again because they already scored from that battlefield this turn.

Sequence:

Player scores hold point from battlefield

Player moves last unit out, battlefield becomes uncontrolled

Player moves another unit into the battlefield

Showdown occurs (non-combat)

If player gains control, no additional scoring occurs

Nuances:

The showdown is non-combat

The restriction on scoring/conquering applies because the battlefield was already scored this turn

question: Does Warwick's 'when I attack' effect trigger when he is defending and an opponent unit moves in to start a showdown?
answer:
Ruling: No, 'when I attack' effects do not trigger when defending. Attack triggers only activate when their source is given the attacker designation, which does not happen when your units are defending and not applying contested status.

Nuances:

The defending player's units do not receive attacker designation

Units that are not applying contested status cannot be the attacker

question: Can a player play a reaction card (Defy) that they draw mid-chain resolution from another card effect (Discipline), or must they wait until the entire chain finishes resolving?
answer:
Ruling: Players can play reactions during chain resolution, not just before it starts. After each chain item resolves, if more items remain on the chain, priority goes to the controller of the next chain item, and both players can add new reactions before the next item resolves.

Sequence:

Chain is built with all initial actions/reactions

Players pass priority and the top chain item begins resolving

After it resolves, if more items remain, priority goes to the controller of the next chain item

Both players can now play reactions before the next item resolves

This continues until the chain is empty

Nuances:

This differs from games like Yu-Gi-Oh where chains must fully resolve once they begin

If a player draws a reaction card mid-chain (like from Discipline), they can play it when they receive priority

Priority alternates based on who controls the next pending chain item

question: Can 5 energy MF (Memory Flux) ready enemy units like Dune Drake?
answer: Ruling: Yes, 5 energy Memory Flux can ready enemy units such as Dune Drake.

question: When Last Stand is cast on a unit with a buff, does it double the base Might then add the buff, or double the total current Might including the buff?
answer:
Ruling: Last Stand doubles the unit's current Might at the time the spell resolves, including any buffs already applied. A 3 Might unit with +1 buff becomes 8 Might (4 × 2), not 7 Might.

Sequence:

Unit has base 3 Might

Buff increases it to 4 Might

Last Stand resolves and doubles current Might to 8

question: When playing Icathian Rain, when are targets selected - at activation or at resolution? Can the opponent react before targets are chosen?
answer:
Ruling: Targets are selected at activation when you play Icathian Rain, not at resolution. The opponent reacts after targets have already been chosen.

Sequence:

Step 1: Play Icathian Rain and pay its cost

Step 2: Select all 6 targets at activation

Step 3: Opponent has opportunity to react

Step 4: Card resolves with the previously selected targets

Nuances:

If you target a unit with Deflect 1 six times, you must pay 6 additional Power at activation

If a hidden unit is revealed in response after targets are selected, that unit cannot be affected because targets cannot be changed after selection

The "Do this 6 times" wording is a shortcut for selecting 6 instances of damage allocation, all chosen at activation

question: Can Warwick split his combat damage to deal 1 damage to 5 different enemy units, or must he assign lethal damage to one unit before moving to the next?
answer:
Ruling: Combat damage must be assigned to one unit until it would receive lethal damage before you can assign damage to another unit. You cannot split 1 damage across multiple units.

Sequence:

Choose the order in which defending units will take damage

Assign enough damage to the first unit to be lethal (equal to its health)

Only after assigning lethal damage to one unit can you assign damage to the next unit

Continue until all combat damage is assigned

Nuances:

To maximize Warwick's multi-target damage ability, you need to pre-damage enemy units before his attack ability resolves

Pre-damage can be done by casting spells like Flurry of Blades either before moving Warwick to the battlefield, or after moving him but before his "when I attack" ability resolves

Warwick's ability triggers during the showdown chain ("when I attack"), not during the combat step, so damage must be dealt before his ability resolves

question: Is there a tracker for official dev rulings on Riftbound rules questions?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, there is an official dev tracker available at https://riftrules.net/riotrules that compiles rulings made by official sources outside of official documents.

Nuances:

Some rulings on the tracker may be older and have already been incorporated into newer versions of the core rules

question: If Sprite creates a chain when it enters play as a temporary, and I flip Sprite Call in response, will I get the hold point from Sprite Call?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you will get the hold point from flipping Sprite Call in response to the chain created by Sprite entering play as a temporary.

question: Does temporary resolution go on the chain/stack like a trigger?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, temporary resolution goes on the chain as a triggered ability and can be reacted to by both players.

Sequence:

The trigger condition occurs at the controller's Beginning Phase

The temporary trigger goes onto the chain

Both players can react to it

Nuances:

Units with temporary can be saved via effects like Zhonay's (this is not optional)

question: If Sett's The Boss ability saves a unit by removing its buff, and that unit has -4 might from Smoke Screen, does the unit die again with 0 max might?
answer:
Ruling: The unit does not die. Units only die when they have non-zero damage equal to or greater than their might. A unit with 0 might and 0 damage does not meet the lethal damage condition.

Sequence:

The Boss's effect replaces death with not death

The buff is removed from the unit

The -4 might from Smoke Screen remains as a continuing effect

The unit survives at 0 might because it has 0 damage (non-zero damage is required for lethal damage)

Nuances:

Healing removes damage, but does not remove continuing might modification effects

Recall moves units to base, but does not remove continuing effects

The Boss only replaces the death itself, it does not remove other continuing effects

question: If you kill Vanguard Captain with Baited Hook and then play Spectral Matron from the Baited Hook, can Spectral Matron pull out the Vanguard Captain that was just killed?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Spectral Matron can pull out the Vanguard Captain that was just killed with Baited Hook.

Sequence:

Baited Hook kills Vanguard Captain

Vanguard Captain goes to trash

Baited Hook fully resolves

Spectral Matron is played from Baited Hook

By the time Spectral Matron is fully played, Vanguard Captain is already in trash and available to be pulled

question: How does Blue Teemo's ability work, specifically regarding the sequence of targeting and revealing cards, and can you play him from hidden with no valid targets?
answer:
Ruling: When Teemo's effect triggers, you choose targets first, then reveal cards with hidden to determine damage. You can play Teemo from hidden even if there are no valid targets since he is a unit; you just won't do the trigger.

Sequence:

Choose targets when the effect triggers

Reveal cards with hidden

Split damage according to the number of cards with hidden revealed

Nuances:

The exact number of targets (whether it's up to 5 targets or a single target) was not definitively resolved in this thread

Whether "up to 5" can include 0 targets was questioned but not answered

question: Does Kai'Sa need to survive combat in order to draw a card when you conquer?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Kai'Sa must survive combat to draw a card even if you conquer.

Sequence:

Combat damage is dealt in the Combat Damage Step

Units that die are removed during Combat Cleanup

Conquering happens at the end of the Resolution Step

Kai'Sa must still be alive when conquering occurs to trigger her draw ability

question: Do you have to start a game with a chosen champion unit on your board, or can the chosen champion zone be empty?
answer:
Ruling: In constructed formats, you must have a chosen champion that matches your legend. In sealed format, you are not required to have a legend or champion card, and if you're missing either or both, you draw an extra card on first turn.

Nuances:

In sealed format, you can use 3 colors and your chosen champion does not have to match the legend (e.g., Ahri Legend with Nocturne in champion zone)

There is likely no strategic reason to leave the chosen champion zone empty in constructed, as having an extra card in hand is valuable

question: If Aurora pulls Kadregrin as the last card of the deck, do you burn out or recycle first? Also, if you have two Auroras and the first one pulls Kadregrin, do you draw then dig with the second Aurora, or dig then draw?
answer:
Ruling: You fully resolve Aurora before any triggers happen, so you recycle the deck first, then Kadregrin's draw trigger occurs.

Sequence: (for double Aurora pulling Kadregrin)

Both Auroras go on the chain

Resolve first Aurora, find Kadregrin

Kadregrin's trigger goes on the chain

Resolve Kadregrin's draw trigger

Resolve second Aurora

question: Can you use Pokemon cards as tokens in tournament-legal Riftbound play?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can use Pokemon cards (or other alternative items like dice, glass beads, or other TCG cards) as tokens in tournament play, as long as they can clearly show exhausted/ready states and you clearly distinguish what each token represents.

Nuances:

Each different token type must be clearly distinguishable (you cannot use the same Pokemon card to represent both a recruit token and a spirit token)

For streamed games, there may be different requirements

question: Does Defy counter a spell based on its printed cost or the total cost paid including additional costs (like Rocket Barrage's additional cost or Accelerate)?
answer:
Ruling: Defy only looks at the printed cost of a card, not the total cost paid including additional costs like those from Rocket Barrage or Accelerate.

Nuances:

This applies even in hypothetical scenarios where Defy could counter units with Accelerate costs

Additional costs paid during activation do not affect whether Defy can counter the spell

question: Does Svellsongur itself gain Deflect when attached to a unit that has Deflect?
answer:
Ruling: No, Svellsongur does not gain Deflect. The effect text is active for the unit it's attached to, not the equipment itself.

Nuances:

When an opponent targets Svellsongur directly (e.g., with Salvage), they do not need to pay the Deflect cost even though the equipped unit has Deflect

The copied keyword only applies to the unit wearing the equipment, not to the equipment card itself

question: If I conquer a battlefield on my turn, my opponent conquers it on their turn, then I reconquer it on the same turn (opponent's turn) by killing their unit with Ride the Wind, do I get a conquer point?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you get a conquer point and the card draw. You can only score 1 point per battlefield per turn, so if you already scored at that battlefield during your own turn, you cannot score there again until the next turn cycle.

Nuances:

If this would be the final point of the game, you cannot score it unless you have scored at every battlefield "this" turn. In that case, you would draw 1 extra card instead of getting the final point.

Other cards may override the one-point-per-battlefield-per-turn rule if they explicitly say otherwise.

question: Can you chain 3 Nocturnes into each other by playing Gemcraft first, then playing Nocturne to trigger Vision again and reveal another Nocturne?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can chain multiple Nocturnes into each other this way.

Sequence:

Play Gemcraft first

Play Nocturne, triggering Vision

If Vision reveals another Nocturne, play it and trigger Vision again

This can continue for as many Nocturnes as are revealed

question: Can Mystic Reversal be played after the player who played Bullet Time has recycled X amount of runes?
answer:
Ruling: No. Mystic Reversal must be played before Bullet Time resolves. The power cost for Bullet Time (recycling runes) is paid during resolution, and you cannot play spells during another card's resolution as there is no priority window at that time.

Sequence:

Bullet Time is played

Priority window exists where Mystic Reversal could be played

Bullet Time resolves (runes are recycled as part of resolution)

No priority window exists during resolution to play Mystic Reversal

Nuances:

Reminder text on cards is not rule text and does not override priority window rules

You must play Mystic Reversal in a priority window before Bullet Time begins resolving

question: When playing Promising Future with Lux Champion, if you reveal and play another 5-cost spell from the top 5 cards, when do you draw cards from Lux's ability?
answer:
Ruling: When you play Promising Future, the cards chosen from it are put on the pending chain first, then Lux's ability trigger is added to the pending chain. When cards move from pending chain to the chain, the 5-cost spell from Promising Future goes on the chain first, then Lux's draw ability resolves. If that 5-cost spell is also a spell, it triggers Lux's ability again after it resolves.

Sequence:

Play Promising Future

Cards from Promising Future are put on the pending chain

Lux's ability trigger is put on the pending chain (last)

Cards move from pending chain to chain

The 5-cost spell from Promising Future goes on the chain

Lux's draw ability goes on the chain and resolves

The 5-cost spell resolves

If it was a spell, Lux's ability triggers again after it resolves

question: Can you tap energy before playing Divine Judgment and retain the excess energy after Divine Judgment discards down to 2?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can tap energy before playing Divine Judgment and retain the tapped energy even after Divine Judgment discards your untapped energy down to 2.

Sequence:

Tap the desired amount of energy (e.g., all 10)

Play Divine Judgment

Divine Judgment discards untapped energy down to 2

Previously tapped energy remains available to spend

question: Is note taking allowed in in-person Riftbound tournaments (e.g., tracking cards seen from Sabotage or cards recycled)?
answer: Ruling: Yes, note taking is allowed in in-person tournaments according to the tournament rules.

question: Can you use a signature spell if you have the Champion unit but not the Legend?
answer: Ruling: No, Signature Spells can only be included in your deck if your Legend matches. Having the Champion unit alone is not sufficient.

question: If Zhonya saves a buffed unit from death, does the unit retain its buffs?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the buffed unit retains its buffs when saved by Zhonya.

Nuances:

Units only lose temporary characteristics (buffs, "this turn" effects, etc.) when they change zones

Zhonya preventing death means the unit never actually changed zones (didn't go to trash, hand, or banish)

question: What happens when defending and someone triggers Face Breaker in a 1v1 combat? Does the attacker go back to base?
answer:
Ruling: If a combat ends and units from 2 players are still present, attacker units are recalled.

Nuances:

This applies specifically when Face Breaker triggers during 1v1 combat while defending

question: When playing Last Breath on Yasuo readied from Base, does he deal damage twice (8 total) or once (4), and does he die this round? Also, when a card returns from battlefield to Base, is it ready or exhausted?
answer:
Ruling: Last Breath only readies a unit and has it deal its might as damage to another unit at a battlefield. Nothing else happens as a result of this spell - if you later attack with Yasuo, that's unrelated to Last Breath.

Nuances:

Move abilities do not modify the exhausted state unless they explicitly say so

If a card was exhausted when moved, it stays exhausted; if ready, it stays ready

question: Does Viktor - Leader's ability activate during the opponent's turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Viktor - Leader's ability can activate during the opponent's turn because it is a triggered effect, not an activated ability.

Nuances:

The FAQ restriction on using abilities during opponent turns applies only to activated abilities

Viktor - Leader has a triggered effect, which functions differently from activated abilities

Viktor - Leader is a unit, not a legend

question: When Sprite Call is played as a hidden card from battlefield A and creates a Sprite during a showdown at battlefield B, where can the Sprite be played?
answer:
Ruling: When a hidden spell causes you to play a unit, you must play that unit at the battlefield where the hidden card was located.

Nuances:

If Sprite Call were played from hand instead of as a hidden card, the Sprite could be played to any battlefield you control or to the base

The restriction applies specifically because the card is hidden, not because of the showdown timing

question: When Cemetery Attendant targets a champion unit in the trash, does the champion return to the chosen champion location on the board or to hand?
answer:
Ruling: The champion unit goes to your hand, not to the chosen champion location.

Nuances:

Chosen champions are treated as normal units/cards except at the start of the game when they are in the chosen champion zone

Hallowed Tomb battlefield is the only card that would return a chosen champion to the chosen champion zone

question: When attempting to win by conquering both battlefields on the same turn (going from 7 points to 8), do you draw a card for each battlefield conquest attempt that you lose, or just one card for the turn?
answer:
Ruling: The thread does not contain a clear answer to this question. The original poster stated their understanding of win conditions but did not receive a response about the card draw mechanics during failed conquest attempts.

Sequence: Not applicable - question was not answered in the thread.

Nuances: The asker confirmed they understand the three ways to win with 7 points: hold for 8, hold 7 and conquer for 8, or conquer 7 and conquer for 8.

question: Can you chain a reaction when someone hides a card?
answer:
Ruling: No, hiding a card does not open a chain and it instantly resolves.

Nuances:

Hiding a card always happens instantly

The hidden status means no one knows it's a permanent, so permanent-related rules don't apply in the typical way

question: When Player A moves a unit to an open battlefield and Player B uses Ride the Wind to move a unit onto that battlefield, who is the defending player?
answer:
Ruling: Player B is the defending player.

Sequence:

Player A moves a unit to an open battlefield

The open showdown finishes

Player B becomes the defender when using Ride the Wind to move a unit onto the battlefield

question: When does Ahri legend's Nine-Tailed Fox effect trigger, can it be missed, and what happens if the opponent plays too quickly?
answer:
Ruling: Ahri's effect triggers when attackers and defenders are established, before "when I attack" effects. It is a defender trigger that resolves before attacker triggers in the initial chain (LIFO order). This trigger can be missed if not declared in time.

Sequence:

Attackers and defenders are established

Ahri's effect triggers (defender trigger)

Initial chain forms with attacker triggers, then defender triggers

Chain resolves LIFO (defender triggers resolve before attacker triggers)

Nuances:

The Ahri player can miss the timing if they do not declare the -1 effect when appropriate

If the opponent plays too fast or skips combat steps (shortcuts), the defending player is entitled to intercept and rewind to proper order to activate Ahri's effect

The trigger can only be missed if enough time was given and the defender failed to declare it before the opponent begins stating actions/reactions to start a chain

question: Can I hold priority during showdown to play multiple reactions in a row, or does focus pass automatically after the chain resolves?
answer:
Ruling: You automatically hold priority when there is an open chain and you play an item to it. You can play multiple reactions before passing priority. However, you cannot hold focus - once the chain you opened with focus closes, the next player in turn order gains focus.

Sequence:

When you play an item to an open chain, you automatically hold priority

You can play multiple reactions in a row before passing priority

Once you pass priority, your opponent can do the same

If both players pass priority consecutively, the topmost item on the chain resolves

When a chain opened with focus closes, focus automatically passes to the next player in turn order

Nuances:

Priority and focus are distinct mechanics - you can hold priority but not focus

question: Does Unyielding Spirit prevent damage from Challenge and similar spells that make units deal damage to each other?
answer:
Ruling: Unyielding Spirit does not prevent damage from Challenge or similar spells (like Gentleman's Duel). These spells cause units to deal damage to each other, not the spell itself dealing damage.

Nuances:

Unyielding Spirit only prevents damage dealt by spells themselves

It does not interact with removal spells that don't deal damage (like Hidden Blade, Cull, Rebuke)

This follows the same ruling as Void Gate, which does not add damage to Challenge because the units are dealing the damage, not the spell

Unit abilities that deal damage (like Green Yas/Shark) are prevented by Unyielding Spirit, but Challenge is treated differently because it makes units deal damage to each other

question: If I move a unit away from a battlefield I'm holding/conquered and then move it back to the same battlefield on the same turn, do I gain points again?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot gain points by moving a unit away from and back to the same battlefield on the same turn. You can only score once per turn per battlefield.

Nuances:

You could use an ability like Ride the Wind during your opponent's turn to move to a battlefield and conquer it again on their turn, since it would be a different turn.

question: In a Match (1v1 Best of 3), how do you determine the First Player in subsequent games?
answer: Ruling: The loser of the previous game chooses who plays first in the next game.

question: Can Lee Sin activate his abilities or play his signature spell (Dragon's Rage) during Showdown when defending a battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: You can only activate abilities during your turn in a neutral open state. Dragon's Rage cannot be played in combat because it does not say action or reaction on it.

Nuances:

Buffs (specifically the keyword 'buff') are permanent and will persist when you pass turn to your opponent

Other might increases that are not specifically labeled as 'buff' are not permanent

question: When conquering a battlefield where units die in the process, do death triggers (like Viktor/Deathknell) and conquer triggers (like Zaun Warrens) go on the chain at the same time, or does one happen before the other?
answer:
Ruling: Death triggers occur before conquer triggers. Units die first during the resolution step, triggering abilities like Deathknell and Viktor. After those triggers resolve, the battlefield is conquered and conquer triggers go on the chain.

Sequence:

Units with lethal damage die during the resolution step

Death triggers (Deathknell, Viktor, etc.) go on the chain

Death triggers resolve

Battlefield is conquered (if no defending units remain but attacking units do)

Conquer triggers (like Zaun Warrens) go on the chain

Conquer triggers resolve

Nuances:

In the original example with Viktor, Gemcraft Seer, and Zaun Warrens: Vision triggers from Gemcraft Seer must resolve before Zaun Warrens triggers, even if you wanted to draw first

Players can play reactions to triggered abilities during the resolution step, but cannot activate abilities

The resolution step processes sequentially - each sub-step depends on the previous one completing

question: Can Karthus cause Ekko to trigger his deathknell twice by floating the first set of power to get double value?
answer:
Ruling: No, Karthus cannot cause Ekko to trigger his deathknell twice. You must recycle Ekko to ready the runes, and you cannot recycle him twice from a single death.

Nuances:

The recycle part of Ekko's triggered ability is a condition, not a cost

Triggered abilities don't have costs; costs are paid when effects enter the chain

If you fail to recycle Ekko, you don't ready the runes

Ekko's deathknell can trigger on an opponent's turn whenever he dies

question: After a spell chain resolves during combat, does the attacking unit immediately conquer, or do players get priority again to play more spells before damage assignment?
answer:
Ruling: After a spell chain resolves during combat, players get priority again and can start another chain before the attacking unit conquers. Damage assignment only occurs when both players pass with an empty chain.

Sequence:

Player A attacks with Poro and passes priority

Player B plays Void Seeker targeting Poro

Player A plays Defy targeting Void Seeker

Defy resolves, Void Seeker is countered

Chain is now empty, but players get priority again

Player B can play another Void Seeker before Poro conquers

Damage assignment only happens when both players pass with an empty chain

question: When a unit with Skyfall of Areion and Trinity Force equipped holds at Reckoner's Arena, which effects trigger and in what order?
answer:
Ruling: When a unit equipped with both Skyfall of Areion and Trinity Force holds at Reckoner's Arena, you gain 3 points total and draw 2 cards. The hold trigger, Trinity Force's hold trigger (which becomes a conquer effect via Skyfall), and Reckoner's Arena's trigger all go on the chain simultaneously.

Sequence:

Unit holds, gaining 1 point

Three triggers go on the chain at the same time: the unit's hold effect, Trinity Force's hold effect, and Reckoner's Arena's trigger

When Reckoner's Arena's trigger resolves, it activates the unit's conquer effects: Trinity Force's conquer effect (scoring 1 point) and the unit's conquer effect (drawing 1 card)

Final result: 3 points gained (1 from hold, 2 from triggers) and 2 cards drawn

Nuances:

Skyfall of Areion makes hold effects also count as conquer effects for the equipped unit

Reckoner's Arena itself does not become a conquer effect due to Skyfall

Both the Trinity Force hold trigger and the unit's own hold trigger become conquer effects that Reckoner's Arena can activate again

question: Can Kaisa's 'Daughter of the Void' ability be used to pay the power cost to hide a hidden spell?
answer:
Ruling: No, Kaisa's ability cannot be used to pay the power cost to hide a spell. The ability can only be used to play spells, and hiding is not the same as playing.

Nuances:

Hiding can consist of units or gears as well as spells, so it would be impossible for an opponent to know if you truly hid a spell without revealing what you're hiding first

question: Does Darius Executioner's 'Other friendly units have +1 might here' ability work in base, or only on the battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: The ability works in base as well as on the battlefield. 'Here' refers to wherever Darius Executioner is located, including your base.

Nuances:

The keyword 'here' is not restricted to battlefield locations only

question: If Vayne Hunter is buffed with Cleave (gaining Assault +3), does she keep the buffed Assault when bounced to hand and replayed?
answer:
Ruling: No, Vayne does not keep the buffed Assault when bounced to hand. When units move between the board and any other zone, they lose any temporary modifications they received.

Nuances:

This applies to any unit moving between the board and any other zone (hand, deck, etc.)

The loss of buffs applies to temporary modifications

question: If Volibear is killed in response to his attack trigger, does his ability still deal damage?
answer:
Ruling: The triggered ability resolves, but since Volibear is no longer at a location, "here" doesn't reference anything valid and the ability fails to find its targets. No damage is done.

Sequence:

Volibear attacks and triggers his ability

Hidden Blade kills Volibear in response

The triggered ability resolves

The ability fails to find targets because "here" is undefined (Volibear is no longer at a location)

No damage is dealt

question: Can Defy counter triggered abilities like Leona's attack ability?
answer:
Ruling: No, Defy cannot counter triggered abilities. Defy can only target spells, not abilities on the stack.

Nuances:

Triggered abilities (like those from attacking) are abilities, not spells

Counter effects that target "spells" cannot affect abilities

question: Does Mageseeker Warden prevent units with Accelerate from entering ready, and does it prevent Sprite Call and Sprite Mother tokens from entering ready?
answer:
Ruling: Mageseeker Warden does not stop Accelerate or Sprite tokens from entering ready.

Nuances:

Anything that enters ready is not affected by Warden's ability that prevents spells and abilities from readying enemy units and gears

question: If a temporary unit dies and there's a hidden card on that battlefield, can you reveal the hidden before cleanup removes it?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can reveal and play the hidden card before losing it. When the temporary unit's triggered ability resolves at the start of your turn, it starts a chain which gives you a window to play the hidden card before the unit dies and you would lose control of the battleground.

Sequence:

At the start of your turn, the temporary unit's triggered ability goes on the chain

This creates a window where you can play the hidden card

After the chain resolves, the temporary unit dies

If you no longer control the battleground after the unit dies, the hidden would be trashed

Nuances:

A cleanup occurs when an item on the chain resolves, not just at end of turn

If you play another temporary unit during this window, it won't die until your next turn

question: If a damaged unit receives a Might boost that brings its current Might back to or above its printed value, does it still count as damaged for effects like Warwick?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the unit still counts as damaged. Damaged units receive damage counters that remain on them until after combat or at the end of the round, regardless of whether their current Might equals or exceeds their printed Might.

Sequence:

Unit takes damage and receives a damage counter

Damage counter remains even if Might is boosted back to original value

Damage counter is only removed after combat or at end of round

Nuances:

Boosting Might does not remove damage counters or change a unit's damaged status

question: When Vayne conquers Zaun Warrens, can you choose the order of triggers, and are you forced to use Vayne's bounce effect before the Battlefield discard/draw?
answer:
Ruling: You choose the order of the triggers. You are not forced to use Vayne's bounce effect as it says "you may", but you must resolve the Zaun Warrens effect as much as possible.

Sequence:

Both triggers happen at the same time (both are "when conquer")

You choose which order to resolve them

Vayne's effect is optional ("you may")

Zaun Warrens effect is mandatory ("do as much as you can")

Nuances:

The "you may" wording on Vayne means you can choose not to bounce her

The Battlefield effect must be resolved as much as possible regardless of order chosen

question: Does Repeat allow you to choose 2 different targets?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you may choose different targets for the Repeat.

Nuances:

Unlike some cards (e.g., Falling Star) that explicitly state "you can choose different units" on the card text, Repeat cards do not include this reminder text, but the ruling still allows different target selection.

question: Can you win the game by holding one battlefield, reaching 7 points that turn, and leaving that battlefield empty to attack and conquer the other battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can win the game this way as long as you've previously scored each battlefield at least once. You can score the final point via conquering.

Sequence:

Score points to reach 7 by holding one battlefield

Leave that battlefield empty

Attack and conquer the other battlefield for the win

Nuances:

You must have scored each battlefield at least once before winning via conquest

question: When a unit is played and its 'when you play me' trigger goes on the chain, but then an opponent takes control of that unit with Hostile Takeover in response, who controls the triggered ability?
answer:
Ruling: The original player who played the unit remains the controller of the triggered ability. Taking control of the unit does not change the controller of the trigger.

Sequence:

Player plays a unit with a 'when you play me' trigger

The trigger is created and its controller is established as the player who played the unit

Opponent takes control of the unit with Hostile Takeover

The trigger remains controlled by the original player

Nuances:

Triggered abilities behave like activated abilities once on the chain

The controller of a trigger is established when it goes on the chain and does not update in real time

If controller updated in real time, removing a unit in reaction to its trigger would make the trigger uncontrolled and cause issues with target definitions (like 'enemy')

Reflexive triggers generated by spells would have no defined controller by the time they finalize if controller updated in real time, since the spell would already be in the trash

question: Do units ignore the chain, or do they resolve immediately when placed on it?
answer:
Ruling: Units use the chain. As soon as they are put onto the chain, they resolve off of it immediately.

Sequence:

Unit is placed on the chain

Unit resolves immediately off the chain

Any abilities triggered by this occur normally

question: If Sett already has a buff, can you stack the triggers so Monastery of Hirana draws a card and then Sett's trigger refunds the buff?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can stack the triggers. When both Sett and Monastery of Hirana trigger simultaneously on conquest, you choose the order. You can resolve Hirana's trigger first (drawing a card and removing Sett's buff), then resolve Sett's trigger (which will buff him since he's no longer buffed).

Sequence:

Both Sett's conquer trigger and Hirana's conquer trigger go on the chain simultaneously

You choose to place Sett's trigger on the chain first, then Hirana's trigger

Hirana's trigger resolves first, drawing a card and removing Sett's buff

Sett's trigger resolves second, buffing Sett since he is no longer buffed

Nuances:

Sett's trigger is added to the chain even if he is already buffed; it simply won't do anything if he's still buffed when it resolves

Buffed units can always be targeted by buff effects (unless a card specifies non-buffed units), even if the effect won't do anything to them

question: Can you score a point from the same battlefield twice in one turn by leaving it empty and re-entering it?
answer:
Ruling: No, you can score each battlefield only once per turn, regardless of whether you leave and re-enter it.

Nuances:

If you lose control of a battlefield during your turn and regain control in the same turn, you do not score another point

Regaining control of a battlefield during your turn (after losing it) does not count as "conquering" it, as conquering is specifically part of the scoring process

You can be in control of a battlefield without having conquered it

question: Does Sun Disc interact with The Harrowing?
answer: Ruling: Yes, Sun Disc interacts with The Harrowing.

question: Are clear sleeves legal in Riftbound?
answer:
Ruling: Clear sleeves are not legal. The back of your cards must have an opaque sleeve on the outside.

Nuances:

Clear inner sleeves are allowed as long as the outer sleeve is opaque

All cards in a deck must be sleeved alike

Opaque inner sleeves with clear outer sleeves may be problematic because imperfections in the inner opaque layer would be difficult for a judge to see

question: If an 8 Might unit has 4 damage on it, what is its Might value in showdown, and how much Might does an opponent need to kill it?
answer:
Ruling: Damage does not reduce a unit's Might value. An 8 Might unit with 4 damage on it still has 8 Might, but an opponent only needs 4 Might to kill it in showdown since the unit already has damage equal to the difference.

Sequence:

A unit accumulates damage separately from its Might value

When damage on a unit equals or exceeds its current Might value, the unit dies

In showdown, both units deal damage to each other based on their Might values

If an 8 Might unit already has 4 damage, it only needs 4 more damage to reach its Might threshold and die

Nuances:

Negative Might effects (like Stupify or Smokescreen) DO reduce current Might value, unlike damage

Might represents both offensive power and the damage threshold for death, but is not the same as HP

question: How do multiple units attacking a single stronger unit work in terms of showdowns and damage? Can multiple units move together to create one showdown, and when does damage heal?
answer:
Ruling: Multiple units moving TO the same battlefield location can be moved at once to create a single showdown. Damage is assigned based on total combined might (not individually per unit), and damage heals at the end of each showdown and at the end of turns.

Sequence:

Move multiple units to the same battlefield location simultaneously to create one showdown

Each player assigns damage however they want based on total might

Damage heals at the end of the showdown

If you want multiple showdowns at the same location, you must move units separately (triggering separate showdowns), but the defending units will heal between showdowns

Nuances:

Units must move TO the same location at the same time to be in the same showdown; showdowns trigger immediately when units arrive at a battlefield the player doesn't control

You cannot ready a unit and then add more units to join that showdown - the showdown happens immediately

To conquer a battlefield, at least one of your units must survive the showdown

If units on both sides survive, attacking units are recalled to base

All units on the board heal after combat, not just those involved in the showdown

question: Trial Deck Upgrades?
answer: This question was not answered in the thread. It was redirected to a different channel as it was not a rules question.

question: Does Unyielding Spirit protect every unit on the board regardless of who controls them?
answer: Ruling: Yes, Unyielding Spirit protects every unit on the board no matter who is the controller.

question: If you cast Singularity for 6 damage on Mind Splitters (7 might units) and then play Watcher (which reduces might by 3 to a minimum of 1), do the Mind Splitters die?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the Mind Splitters die. Watcher reduces their might from 7 to 4, and they already have 6 damage marked on them, so they die when their damage meets or exceeds their might.

Sequence:

Singularity deals 6 damage to the Mind Splitters (7 might units)

Mind Splitters are now 7 might with 6 damage marked

Watcher is played, reducing their might by 3

Mind Splitters become 4 might with 6 damage marked

Mind Splitters die because damage (6) exceeds might (4)

Nuances:

Damage does not reduce might; it is tracked separately

Watcher's might reduction applies to the unit's current might value, not the damaged value

The "minimum of 1" clause on Watcher does not prevent this interaction because the units start at 7 might

question: Can you use a React card in response to another React card (specifically, can Deny counter Hidden Blade)?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you can use reactions to respond to other reactions. In the scenario described, Deny can counter Hidden Blade.

question: Does conquering a battlefield and using its effect start a chain, or does it happen instantly?
answer:
Ruling: Battlefield effects work the same as unit effects - triggered effects (like "When you conquer") start a chain, while passive effects do not.

Sequence:

You must go through showdown steps to conquer a battlefield (simply moving to it is not enough)

At the end of the showdown, if only your units remain at the battlefield, you conquer it

The battlefield's triggered effect then starts a chain

If you control multiple effects that trigger simultaneously (like a unit effect and battlefield effect), you choose the order to put them on the chain

Nuances:

Moving to a battlefield does not automatically conquer it - you must complete the showdown with only your units remaining

The showdown itself also causes a chain before the conquest trigger resolves

question: When a combat has both a 'when I attack' and a 'when I defend' trigger, which trigger goes on the chain first and which resolves last?
answer:
Ruling: Attacker triggers go on the chain first, then players who are neither attacker nor defender, then defender triggers. Since the chain resolves first-in-last-out, defender triggers resolve first.

Sequence:

Attacker adds their triggers to the chain

Players who are neither attacker nor defender add their triggers

Defender adds their triggers to the chain

Chain resolves in reverse order (defender triggers resolve first, attacker triggers resolve last)

question: In Riftbound, if a player conquers both battlefields during their opponent's turn and reaches 9 points, do they win immediately, or must they control both battlefields simultaneously at the end of the turn?
answer:
Ruling: You win immediately upon reaching 9 points by conquering both battlefields, even if you don't control them simultaneously. You only need to successfully score at both battlefields, not hold them at the same time.

Sequence:

Opponent gains 7th point for holding at start of their turn

Opponent moves to your battlefield, you respond by moving away and conquering their battlefield (8 points)

Opponent conquers the battlefield you left (opponent reaches 8 points)

Opponent readies and moves back to where your unit is, you respond by moving away again

This second move allows you to conquer the second battlefield during opponent's turn, reaching 9 points and winning

Nuances:

You cannot score again from a battlefield you already held during that turn, even if you temporarily lose control of it

Conquering can occur on your opponent's turn if your unit moves onto a battlefield it wasn't on at the start of that turn

The winning condition only requires scoring at both battlefields, not simultaneous control

question: When conquering with Qiyana at Candlelit Sanctum, can you look at the two cards from Sanctum before deciding whether Qiyana draws or channels a rune?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can look at the two cards from Candlelit Sanctum before deciding whether Qiyana draws or channels a rune.

Sequence:

Conquer with Qiyana at Candlelit Sanctum

Look at the top two cards from Sanctum's ability

Choose whether to draw or channel a rune with Qiyana

Nuances:

You choose for Qiyana when the ability resolves, not in advance

The choice is made on resolution because you're not choosing a target, a location for a unit to be played to, the destination for a move, or whether to pay an optional additional cost

question: When a damage spell with bonus damage from Ravenborn Tome or Annie, Fiery is played and then Mystic Reversal is used on it, how much damage does it deal?
answer:
Ruling: Annie, Fiery does not add bonus damage after Mystic Reversal because it is a passive that only affects "your" spells. For Ravenborn Tome, the bonus damage is likely added when the spell is put on the chain, so it would retain the bonus damage after being Mystic Reversal'd.

Nuances:

The rules for "when you play a spell" triggers with Mystic Reversal are currently unclear and awaiting official clarification

The Ravenborn Tome ruling is based on interpretation and has not been officially confirmed

question: How should a tied/drawn match be reported in tournament software - as 1-1-0 or 1-1-1?
answer:
Ruling: The correct reporting depends on what actually happened during the match. If players completed game 2 when time was called, report 1-1-0. If players were in game 3 and that game ended in a draw due to time (after the +5 turns with equal score), report 1-1-1.

Sequence:

If match ends after game 2 completes when time is called: report 1-1-0

If match goes to game 3 and that game draws due to time running out: report 1-1-1

Nuances:

For intentional draws (not based on time), players must report 0-0-3, not 1-1-1 or 1-1-0

Players must have actually played games to report game wins during a draw

question: How does buff work in Riftbound, including permanence, interactions, and whether units can have multiple buffs?
answer:
Ruling: A buff gives +1 might to a unit as long as the unit has it, and units can only have one buff at a time. Buffs stay on the unit until it dies or is spent for other benefits.

Sequence:

A unit can only receive a buff if it doesn't already have one

The buff remains on the unit until death or spent

The +1 might bonus applies continuously while the buff is present

Nuances:

You can target a unit that already has a buff with a buff effect, but it won't gain another buff (matters for legal targeting and sequencing)

Many cards allow spending buffs from units for other benefits

question: When a unit is defending alone with Yi's +2 might bonus and gets attacked by Leona Zealot (which gives -8 might), does the +2 apply before the -8, or does the -8 overwrite the +2?
answer:
Ruling: Both are passive effects that apply simultaneously in the arithmetic layer. You add all bonuses first, then subtract all penalties, with a minimum of 1 might.

Sequence:

Start with base might

Add all bonuses (including Yi's +2)

Subtract all penalties (including Leona's -8)

Apply minimum of 1 might

Nuances:

Yi's ability is a "While" effect, not a "When" effect, so it applies continuously

In the arithmetic layer, addition comes before subtraction

You need the base might plus additions to total more than 8 to avoid being reduced to 1 might by Leona's effect

question: Does Vex's cost reduction ability reduce the additional cost imposed by Deflect?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Vex's cost reduction applies to Deflect costs because Deflect is an additional cost to the spell being played.

Nuances:

This does not apply to reflexive trigger spells

question: For Volibear's attack ability that deals 5 damage, when do you choose targets and assign damage - before the trigger resolves or when it resolves?
answer:
Ruling: When Volibear attacks, the trigger goes on the chain and you choose targets at that time. When the trigger resolves, you then assign the 5 damage between the chosen targets (must assign at least 1 damage to each).

Sequence:

Attack with Volibear, trigger goes on the chain

Choose targets for the damage

When trigger resolves, assign the 5 damage between chosen targets

Nuances:

You must assign at least 1 damage to each chosen target

Because targets are chosen before resolution, opponents can respond by buffing units before damage is assigned

question: Can Reaction cards be used in response to playing a card that doesn't have a 'when you play me' effect?
answer:
Ruling: When you play/gear a unit, a chain is still formed, but as a permanent it instantly resolves without giving priority to either player, so you cannot react to it being played on the board.

Sequence:

A card is played/geared

A chain is formed

The permanent instantly resolves without priority being given

No opportunity to use Reaction cards

Nuances:

This applies specifically to permanents (units)

The chain exists but resolves immediately without allowing reactions

question: If multiple Zhonya's Hourglasses are in play, do they all get used up when a friendly unit dies, or just one?
answer:
Ruling: Only one Zhonya's Hourglass gets used up when a friendly unit would die.

Sequence:

The first Zhonya's Hourglass triggers and resolves

After it resolves, the unit is no longer being killed

The other Zhonya's Hourglass triggers fizzle because their trigger condition is no longer met

question: If a player wins a second Summoner Skirmish (already having a bye from a previous win), does the bye automatically trickle down to second place?
answer:
Ruling: No, the bye does not automatically trickle down to second place if a player wins a second Summoner Skirmish.

Nuances:

Players may discuss prize distribution before playing finals games, with the Tournament Organizer's permission

Such discussions must be communicated openly and only involve guaranteed tournament prizing

A player can choose to concede after prize distribution is announced (winner gets X, second place gets Y)

These agreements are not binding beyond a player's reputation, so caution is recommended especially when physical prizes haven't arrived yet

question: When using Falling Star to target Lonely Poro and another unit, does the order of targeting matter for whether Lonely Poro's deathknell triggers?
answer:
Ruling: You can order the Falling Star triggers to kill the other unit first, leaving Lonely Poro alone when it dies, which will cause its deathknell trigger to go on the chain (though it won't draw a card since Lonely Poro is already dead).

Sequence:

Falling Star creates two separate triggered abilities

Each trigger resolves in its own chain link

If you target the other unit first, it dies first

Then Lonely Poro dies alone, triggering its deathknell

The deathknell trigger goes on the chain but doesn't draw since Poro is dead

Nuances:

The deathknell trigger will still go on the chain even though Lonely Poro won't actually draw a card

From the Poro player's perspective, you want to kill Poro first to deny the trigger

From the opponent's perspective, you can kill the other unit first to enable the trigger

question: Can you play Ride the Wind (an action spell) in response to an opponent's Fox Fire spell to remove a unit from the battlefield and cancel the spell?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play Ride the Wind in response to Fox Fire. Action spells cannot be added to an existing chain - they can only start a chain. When an opponent casts a spell, they start a chain, and you can only respond with reaction spells, not action spells.

Sequence:

Opponent casts Fox Fire, starting a chain

You may respond with a reaction spell (like Discipline)

Your reaction spell resolves first

Fox Fire resolves second

After the chain fully resolves, you get an opportunity to play action spells in the open game state

Nuances:

Actions can only be played in open game states (when no chain exists)

You cannot play an action to counter an action, only a reaction can respond to spells in a chain

Reaction spells can also start chains, and can only be responded to with other reactions

Some spells trigger showdowns (those that move units into battlefields) while others do not (damage/stat modification spells)

question: If Hook kills a buffed Soaring Scout and tutors Karthus, does Scout's Deathknell trigger before or after Karthus enters the board?
answer:
Ruling: Karthus will not be on board before the Deathknell enters the chain. The Deathknell trigger will enter the chain first, then Karthus will be played.

Sequence:

Hook kills Scout, Scout enters as pending

Karthus is banished and begins being played, enters as pending on top of Scout

Hook finishes resolving

Scout is finalized and the Deathknell trigger enters the chain

Karthus is finalized and immediately played

Scout's Deathknell resolves

Nuances:

Pending items are finalized in the same order they are put on the chain (which is opposite to how items on the chain resolve)

Karthus was not on board before the Deathknell fully entered the chain, so it doesn't trigger twice

question: When are abilities like shield checked in combat - are they checked once at the start of showdown or rechecked throughout combat when the battlefield state changes?
answer:
Ruling: Assault and Shield statuses are applied immediately after combat starts, before when I attack/defend triggers. They cannot be reacted to and remain active throughout the entire combat, even for units that enter combat afterwards.

Sequence:

Combat begins

Assault and Shield statuses are applied immediately

When I attack/defend triggers occur

Statuses remain active for the rest of combat

Nuances:

If a unit like Wielder of Water gains might from attacking alone, it will recheck after every cleanup step (such as after Ride the Wind resolves) and lose the might gain if it's no longer alone

Units that enter combat after it has started still benefit from Shield/Assault statuses that were applied at the start

question: If I play Disciplined and my opponent plays Defy, then I play Defy targeting their Defy, will I be able to draw a card off Disciplined?
answer:
Ruling: If the second Defy targets the first Defy, then Disciplined will resolve and you will draw a card.

Sequence:

Disciplined is played

Opponent plays Defy targeting Disciplined

You play Defy targeting opponent's Defy

Your Disciplined resolves and you draw a card

question: When a game loss or match loss penalty is issued, which game or match does it apply to - the current one, the next one, or does it depend on timing?
answer: Unable to extract a clear answer from the provided thread. The thread contains only the question being asked, with no responses or rulings provided.

question: If Draven, Audacious dies in combat but you win the combat, does his 'when I die in combat' ability trigger before his 'when I win a combat' ability, and which effect resolves?
answer:
Ruling: When Draven dies in combat but you win, only his 'when I die in combat' ability triggers and resolves. His 'when I win a combat' ability does not trigger because he is already in the Trash when that would check.

Sequence:

Draven's 'when I die in combat' ability triggers during step 2b of Cleanup and is added as a pending item to the chain

Draven is sent to the Trash

Draven's 'when I win a combat' ability cannot trigger because he is no longer in play

When cleanup finishes, Draven's pending 'when I die in combat' item resolves and your opponent scores a point

question: Who has priority to play an action spell at the beginning of combat/showdown?
answer:
Ruling: The attacker gains Focus at the start of a showdown and becomes the active player, allowing them to play an Action or Reaction first, regardless of who was the active player before the showdown.

Sequence:

Attacker gains Focus at the start of showdown

Attacker may play an Action or Reaction

If attacker chooses not to play anything, or plays something and the chain fully resolves, Focus passes to the next relevant player

If attacker passes priority and defender plays a spell, priority goes back to the attacker who can then play a reaction

Nuances:

This is a change from old rules where the defender had priority

Focus is different from priority: Focus allows playing actions outside of open play states (like during showdowns), while priority determines who can play the next reaction in a chain

When the last effect on a chain resolves during a showdown, focus and priority go to the next player (except for the initial chain when it always goes to the attacker first)

If you play a reaction as defender and it resolves, you do not retain priority to start a new chain with an Action

question: In a showdown, can you play an action in response to another action if opponent passed priority, or only reactions?
answer:
Ruling: When there is anything on the chain, only reactions can be played. Actions can only be played when the chain is empty.

Sequence:

First action (En Garde) is played and chain resolves

Unit gets +1 from En Garde

After chain is empty, opponent can open a new chain with an action (Ride The Wind)

Unit goes back

All players pass priority

Damage occurs

Nuances:

An action can be played after another action resolves, but not while it's on the chain

The opponent must wait for the chain to fully resolve before playing their action

question: If Hidden Blade targets a unit on a battlefield, but that unit is moved to a base in response, does the unit die and does anyone draw 2 cards?
answer:
Ruling: The unit is no longer at the battlefield and cannot be a legal target for Hidden Blade. The unit does not die and no one draws cards.

Nuances:

The draw effect is a separate instruction, but without a legal target, no controller can be determined to draw the cards

question: Do the reflexive triggers from Falling Star and Icathian Rain trigger Dreaming Tree if you choose your own unit on the battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, the reflexive triggers from Falling Star and Icathian Rain do not trigger Dreaming Tree because it is the reflexive trigger targeting the unit, not the spell itself.

Nuances:

This same principle applies to Kai'sa Legend's ability - you cannot tap Kai'sa to pay for Deflect when playing these spells since it's not the spell targeting

You can use Kai'sa's ability to pay for Deflect on regular spells, just not on reflexive triggers like Falling Star and Icathian Rain

question: Can players use the scoring numbers on the playmat to track score at high OPL, or must score be tracked in writing?
answer:
Ruling: At high OPL, score must be tracked in writing. The scoring numbers on the playmat are for casual play only.

Nuances:

The playmat scoring may be used for show purposes on stream

Players may use both the playmat display and written tracking simultaneously (playmat for visual/show, written for official record)

Score trackers of any sort can be used but written tracking must still be maintained alongside them

Electronic devices are not allowed at the table at high OPL

question: Does Ravensbloom Student's trigger go on the stack/chain where it can be reacted to, or does it immediately gain power?
answer:
Ruling: The trigger goes on the chain and can be reacted to before it resolves.

Nuances:

Only Reaction spells can be used to respond to the trigger, not Action spells

There may not be 3 damage Reaction spells currently available in the game

question: If a Sand Soldier with Eye of the Herald attached is on a battlefield, can you play Azir Ascendant to the same battlefield, recycle 1 green to target that Sand Soldier (already on the same battlefield), switch the equipment to Azir, and does this create a token? Also, how does Azir interact with Vilemaw's Lair - can Azir swap with a unit on that battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: You can target a unit on the same battlefield with Azir's ability and switch equipment to Azir, but no token is created because the unit did not actually move. When Azir swaps with a unit at Vilemaw's Lair, both units end up at Vilemaw's Lair due to "can't beat can" rules.

Sequence:

Play Azir Ascendant onto the same battlefield as Sand Soldier with Eye of the Herald

Recycle 1 green to target the Sand Soldier on the same battlefield

Switch Eye of the Herald from Sand Soldier to Azir

No token is created because there was no movement

Nuances:

If a unit is targeted to move to the battlefield it is already on, it is not considered to have moved

For Vilemaw's Lair interaction: if either Azir or the target unit was originally at base, both units will end up at Vilemaw's Lair after the swap

question: If a judge makes an incorrect ruling that affects the outcome of a game, what is the correct procedure to correct this?
answer:
Ruling: Most of the time judge mistakes will not be caught until well after the call has been made, so the vast majority of the time the resolution is to acknowledge the mistake and move on.

Nuances:

At low OPL events, the resolution is typically to move on

The appropriate response may vary at higher OPL events, though no specific procedure was identified in the rules

question: What advice is there for judging a first Nexus Night event, particularly regarding when to give warnings?
answer:
Ruling: At Nexus Night (low OPL), the most important thing is to correct mistakes and keep play moving. Punishments should be reserved for serious problems or nefarious intent, not minor errors.

Sequence:

When called over, slow down and listen first

Take in the relevant information

Understand the line of play that did happen

Determine how it should have happened

Correct the mistake and keep play moving

Nuances:

Nexus Night is low OPL, so the approach should be more educational than punitive

Focus on correcting mistakes rather than issuing warnings for minor infractions

question: If Gust is cast on a spell and the opponent reacts with En Garde to increase the unit's might above 3, does Gust still take effect?
answer:
Ruling: Gust will not have any effect if En Garde increases the unit's might above 3 before Gust resolves.

Sequence:

Gust is cast targeting a spell

En Garde is played in reaction, increasing the unit's might above 3

Gust still resolves but has no effect

Nuances:

Gust still counts as having been played and resolved, which matters for effects that care about cards or spells being played, even though it has no effect on the target

question: Can you use Defy on a spell that targets your unit with Deflect, even though Deflect increases the spell's cost?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can use Defy on a spell targeting a unit with Deflect. When an effect checks a card's cost, it only checks the printed cost, not any additional costs from keywords like Deflect.

Nuances:

Deflect is considered a "mandatory additional cost" but does not change the printed cost of a card

You cannot Defy a card that has a high printed cost even if it was played for less due to cost reduction effects

question: When Hidden Blade is played from hidden, can it target units at any battlefield or only the battlefield where it was hidden?
answer:
Ruling: When Hidden Blade is played from hand, it can target a unit at any battlefield. When played from hidden, it can only target units at the battlefield where it was hidden.

Nuances:

Hidden cards that require a target must pick from the battlefield they were hidden at, unless the card explicitly restricts targeting in a way that makes it impossible to target something on the current battlefield (like requiring a target at a different location)

Saying "any battlefield" would be equivalent to "a battlefield" and doesn't prevent targeting the current battlefield, so it wouldn't allow targeting other battlefields when played from hidden

If Hidden Blade is played from hand targeting a unit at one battlefield, and that unit moves to a different battlefield before resolution, the target is still valid because it's still at a battlefield

question: What is the difference between a combat and a showdown, and can a showdown occur without a combat?
answer:
Ruling: A showdown occurs whenever a unit moves into a battlefield. A combat occurs when units controlled by opposing players are present at the same battlefield. A showdown can occur without a combat when moving to an empty battlefield.

Sequence:

Move to empty battlefield = Showdown without combat

Move to occupied battlefield = Showdown with combat

Nuances:

A showdown is not derivative of combat; it is a part of combat when combat occurs, but can also exist independently (like how a wheel can be part of a car but also of a bike)

question: If I have 2 units at the same location and move one away during showdown, does Mask of Foresight trigger to give the remaining unit +1 for being alone?
answer:
Ruling: No. "When I attack/defend" triggers only when a unit becomes an attacker/defender. If you attack with 2 units, they are not alone when they become attackers, so the trigger misses. Moving a unit away afterward does not cause a new trigger because the remaining unit already was an attacker/defender.

Nuances:

"While" effects (like Wielder of Water or Yi) would apply when the condition becomes true during combat

"When" effects (like Mask of Foresight) must have their condition met at the moment the unit is assigned as attacker/blocker

The rules may change in future versions to handle "when I attack/defend" triggers differently

question: When multiple units enter a battlefield simultaneously during a showdown, does the turn player or attacker choose the order they go on the stack?
answer:
Ruling: The attacker always has priority to choose the order units go on the stack during a showdown, not the turn player.

Sequence:

When a charmed Yasuo enters a battlefield with Ahri already present

The attacker decides which unit's ability goes on the stack first

question: When a reflexive trigger targets a unit with Deflect, can you choose not to pay the Deflect cost, and what happens to the ability?
answer:
Ruling: When a reflexive trigger targets a unit with Deflect, you can choose whether to pay the Deflect cost. If you choose not to pay, the ability does not finalize and is removed from the chain.

Sequence:

Reflexive triggers are created as pending items

When choosing targets for each pending trigger, if you target a unit with Deflect, you must decide whether to pay the cost

If you refuse to pay the Deflect cost, that trigger does not finalize and is removed from the chain

All pending items must finalize (or be removed) before players can add reactions

Nuances:

This is different from regular spells/abilities played from hand - those require you to pay Deflect cost when initially played if targeting a Deflect unit

The ability that doesn't finalize never reaches the chain fully, so it doesn't count for effects that care about finalized spells/abilities
