answer: No clear ruling was provided in this thread. The discussion raised a concern about potential abuse of intentional draw rules in 4-player side events (based on an issue from Star Wars Unlimited), but no resolution, rule clarification, or consensus answer was reached.

question: Can a player float energy from runes before recycling one for a Seal's power cost, and can a Seal pay for itself?
answer:
Ruling: You can exhaust runes to float energy before recycling a rune to pay for a Seal's power cost. A Seal cannot pay for itself, but one Seal can pay for another Seal.

Sequence:

Exhaust runes to float energy before paying costs

Recycle one rune to pay for the Seal's power cost

The Seal enters play ready and can be used the same turn

Use the floated energy and additional runes to pay for other cards

Nuances:

Seals have an energy cost of 0 but require 1 power (paid by recycling a rune)

A Seal cannot pay for its own power cost

One Seal can pay for another Seal's power cost

question: Can Forge of the Fluft allow the controller to attach an already attached equipment to another unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Forge of the Fluft can attach equipment that is already attached to one unit to a different unit.

Nuances:

This makes detaching a redundant mechanic in some cases, though detaching still has its uses.

question: If Player A passes focus and Player B passes focus, does combat have to start or can Player A then choose to play an action?
answer:
Ruling: No, Player A cannot play a card after both players pass focus. Combat happens when both players voluntarily pass focus.

Sequence:

When a unit is moved to the battlefield, "When I attack" then "When I defend" are added to the chain

Player B has the opportunity to react (passing priority)

Player A then has focus for a new chain, then Player B

This cycle continues until both players pass focus

Once both players pass focus, combat begins

Nuances:

Focus (the opportunity to play Actions) is separate from priority

Priority is passed starting with the player with Focus when a chain is created, then focus automatically passes

When any chain item is placed, the player who placed it gets priority first

question: If a spell targets a unit at a battlefield, and the unit is moved to a different battlefield before the spell resolves, does the spell still affect its original target?
answer:
Ruling: As long as the target is still at "a battlefield" (any battlefield), the spell will still affect it and not be mistargeted, even if it moved to a different battlefield than where it was originally targeted.

Nuances:

If a spell requires multiple targets to be at the "same battlefield" (like Facebreaker requiring a friendly and enemy unit at the same battlefield), and that condition is no longer true on resolution, the spell will whiff and neither target will be affected.

The spell still resolves even when targets become illegal; it doesn't fizzle (which would imply no resolution at all).

question: If someone Charms me into their battlefront, and I win, do I get a point for conquering (assuming I didn't previously control that battlefront this turn)?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you get a point for conquering that battlefront when you win, as long as you didn't previously control it this turn.

question: When casting Fallen Star or Icathian Rain, do you have to retarget your own units if your opponent uses Retreat to remove their units?
answer:
Ruling: It depends on when your opponent plays Retreat. Fallen Star and Icathian Rain create reflexive triggers that don't declare targets until after the spell itself resolves.

Sequence:

The spell (Fallen Star/Rain) is added to the chain

Opponent can react to the spell before triggers are created

If no reaction, the spell resolves and creates damage triggers

Targets are declared when triggers finalize onto the chain

Opponent can react to the triggers after targets are declared

Nuances:

If opponent reacts to the spell itself (before triggers finalize), you must retarget any remaining legal targets when the triggers are created, which can include your own units

If opponent reacts to the triggers after they've finalized with declared targets, the targets cannot be redeclared and the triggers resolve with 0 effect

If all units are removed before triggers finalize, the triggers fail to finalize and are not added to the chain (the spell still resolves and costs are paid)

The spell does not return to your hand - it is discarded normally

In tournament play, if you announce targets when casting, this is a shortcut that locks in those targets unless your opponent responds

question: When a character with an 'on attack' trigger attacks a defender with an 'on defend' trigger, what is the order these triggers go on the chain and resolve?
answer:
Ruling: Attack and defend triggers are part of the same chain. Attack triggers go on the chain first, which means they resolve last (after defend triggers resolve).

Sequence:

Attack triggers go on the chain first

Defend triggers go on the chain second

Defend triggers resolve first (last in, first out)

Attack triggers resolve last

question: Can Nocturne be played by paying one rune when using Stacked Deck or Mystic Poro?
answer: Ruling: Yes, Nocturne can be played by paying one rune when you use Stacked Deck or Mystic Poro.

question: Can an opponent play multiple Cleaves on a unit that was Charmed into battle?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the opponent can play all three Cleaves (assuming the unit survives) on a unit that was Charmed into battle.

Sequence:

Player A plays Charm

Player A passes

Player B passes

Charm resolves, showdown begins

Player B has focus first (as the attacking player)

Player B plays Cleave and passes

Player A passes

Cleave resolves

Player A passes focus

Player B can play another Cleave

This repeats until Player B is out of Cleaves or chooses not to play more

Nuances:

Player A has focus between each Cleave and can start chains by playing appropriately timed cards or activating abilities

Ravenbloom does not trigger from Defied spells

Countered spells do not count as being played; cards are considered played after they resolve

question: When playing a unit with Dazzling Aurora, do you still pay the power cost of that unit?
answer: Ruling: No, you do not pay the power cost. When an effect allows you to play a card for free, you do not pay its power cost.

question: Can you react to end of turn abilities, and how does this work for cards like Sona and Aurora?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, end of turn abilities are normal triggered abilities that create a chain and allow reactions.

Sequence:

End of turn ability triggers

Ability goes on the chain

Players can react to the ability on the chain

question: After a reaction resolves during a showdown, does the opponent get priority to play the newly drawn card before the original action resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, each player receives priority after an element on the chain resolves.

Sequence:

Player takes an action during showdown

Opponent plays a reaction (e.g., a discipline)

The reaction resolves

Both players receive priority (opponent can play the newly drawn card)

If no further responses, the original action resolves

question: If a 5 Might Sett with a buff gets Smokescreened down to 1 Might, and then you spend Sett's buff to play Call to Glory, what is Sett's final Might?
answer:
Ruling: When you spend Sett's buff to play Call to Glory while Smokescreen is active, Sett ends at 3 Might. You apply increases and decreases in the arithmetic layer: 4 Might (base) + 3 Might (Call to Glory) - 4 Might (Smokescreen) = 3 Might.

Sequence:

Sett starts at 5 Might (4 base + 1 from buff)

Smokescreen reduces him by 4 Might to 1 Might

Spend Sett's buff to play Call to Glory (Sett drops to 0 Might temporarily: 4 base - 4 Smokescreen)

Call to Glory resolves, granting +3 Might

Final calculation: 4 (base) + 3 (CtG) - 4 (Smokescreen) = 3 Might

Nuances:

Units only die when they have non-zero damage marked on them greater than or equal to their Might. Sett doesn't die just for being at 0 Might without damage marked.

question: When Draven Legend player wins a combat at Treasure Hoard, what is the order of resolution for: drawing a card (Draven Legend effect), scoring a point (Conquer), and choosing to pay 1 for Gold (Battlefield effect)?
answer:
Ruling: The order is correct as stated: (1) Draw for winning combat (Draven Legend effect), (2) Scoring a point (Conquer), (3) Choosing to pay 1 to get a Gold (Battlefield effect).

Sequence:

Draven wins between combat cleanup and the step that removes contested

The contested status is removed and the Draven player conquers

The player gains a point and conquer triggers go on the chain

Conquer triggers resolve

Nuances:

When multiple "When I attack" effects trigger simultaneously on different game objects, the attacking player chooses the order

question: Can different sleeve colors be used for main deck, rune deck, battlefields, and token units in Riftbound tournaments?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can use different sleeve colors for main deck, rune deck, battlefields, and token units/buffs. The requirement for sleeves to be the same color only applies within a given deck (main deck or rune deck), not across different card sets.

Nuances:

Battlefields should all be in one color of sleeve to avoid giving away information, but that color does not have to match the main deck or rune deck

Tokens aren't cards and sleeve rules basically don't apply to them since they never exist in private/secret zones where their identity needs to be concealed

You can use the same color or different colors for tokens, or even clear sleeves (though clear sleeves cannot be used for cards)

Some players use only 2 colors to save money (e.g., main deck and battlefields in one color, runes and legend in another)

The legend can be in a separate magnetic case or slab and doesn't have to match the main deck sleeves

question: Does Champion Voli's 5 damage resolve before the opponent can play Rebuke during a showdown?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the 5 damage resolves before Rebuke can be played. Rebuke cannot be used as a response to Voli - Furious' ability.

Sequence:

Voli's 'on attack' ability is added to the initial chain of the showdown

Either player can play reactions on this chain

The initial chain finishes resolving (including the 5 damage)

Actions (like Rebuke) can only be played during open states after the initial chain has finished resolving

Nuances:

Actions can only be played on open states during showdowns, not as responses to abilities on the initial chain

Reactions can be played on the initial chain, but Rebuke is an action, not a reaction

question: Can I react to the buff from Karma when my opponent recycles a card with her Vision ability?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can react to Karma's buff ability when your opponent recycles a card due to her Vision ability.

Sequence:

Playing Karma triggers Vision

When Vision resolves, if a card was recycled, Karma's buff ability triggers

The buff ability goes on the chain

There is a priority window where players can respond, first to the player who controls Karma, then to other players in turn order

question: Why does Hidden Blade fail to draw cards when its target dies before resolution, but Discipline still draws a card when its target dies or is removed?
answer:
Ruling: Hidden Blade fails to draw cards when its target dies because "its controller" cannot be referenced once the target no longer exists. Discipline still draws a card because it uses "draw 1" (referring to the caster) rather than "its controller" (referring to the target).

Nuances:

The difference is in the card text wording: "draw 1" vs "its controller draws 1"

When a card refers to "its controller" (meaning the target's controller), it needs the target to exist to determine who draws

When a card says "draw 1" without reference to the target, the caster draws regardless of whether the target still exists

question: If you have multiple Gemcraft Seers in play, does Vision stack (e.g., 2 Seers = Scry 2) or do you just look at the top card multiple times?
answer:
Ruling: Vision does not stack from multiple sources. You look at the top card multiple times separately.

Sequence:

First Vision trigger resolves, you look at the top card and decide to put it on top or bottom

Second Vision trigger resolves, you look at the top card again (which may be the same card if you left it on top)

Nuances:

If you put the card on top during the first Vision, you will look at that same card again for the second Vision

question: Does Stand United interact with Lee Sin Ascetic's buffs? Specifically, if Lee Sin has 5 buffs, will Stand United give him +1 buff and then a total of +12 might?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Stand United interacts with Lee Sin Ascetic's buffs. If Lee Sin has 5 buffs, Stand United will give him +1 buff (for a total of 6 buffs), and each buff will provide +2 might instead of +1, resulting in +12 total might.

Sequence:

Lee Sin starts with 5 buffs

Stand United gives Lee Sin +1 buff (now 6 buffs total)

Each buff now provides +2 might due to Stand United's effect

Total might bonus: 6 buffs × 2 might = +12 might

Nuances:

Each Buff is tracked individually as a game object

Buffs can be referenced, counted, or targeted by other effects

question: Is recalling a regular action you can do at any time to bring a unit back to base, or does it require a card to specifically state 'recall'?
answer:
Ruling: Recall is a specific action that only occurs when a card effect explicitly states "recall." It is not a standard action available at any time. Recall does not count as moving.

Nuances:

Using a standard move action to bring a unit from the battlefield to base is not a recall

Recalls are limited actions that happen during specific moments

Units can only move via card effects or by using the standard move action (exhausting to move)

question: When does Leona's stun effect require declaring a target - at initialization or resolution?
answer:
Ruling: Leona's stun effect targets, and targets must be declared when you put the ability onto the chain (at initialization), not at resolution.

Sequence:

Leona's effect goes on the chain when showdown starts

You must immediately declare which enemy unit at the battlefield is the target of the stun

The stun resolves later when the ability resolves from the chain

Nuances:

An ability targets if it must choose a specific game object to affect (not if it affects all objects of a set)

Even if there is only one valid target, you still must declare it as the target

question: Does Wielder of Water count as alone when a hidden card is at the same Battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Wielder of Water counts as alone when a hidden card is at the same Battlefield because hidden cards technically don't exist until revealed.

Sequence:

While the card remains hidden, Wielder of Water maintains its alone bonus

When a hidden unit is revealed, Wielder of Water immediately loses the alone bonus

If the hidden card is a spell (not a unit), Wielder of Water keeps the alone bonus even after revelation

Nuances:

This applies even if the hidden card is a unit like Paaka Cub

Only revealed units cause Wielder of Water to lose the alone status

Revealed spells do not affect the alone status

question: Can First Mate ready an exhausted Volibear Legend?
answer: Ruling: No, First Mate cannot ready an exhausted Volibear Legend because a legend is not a unit.

question: Can Sprite Call be used during an attack to play an additional attacker at a battlefield you don't control?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play units at a battlefield you don't control. You can use Sprite Call for defense, or play the sprites beforehand and move them in with your other attacking units.

Sequence:

Play sprites before the attack

Move them to the battlefield with other attacking units

Nuances:

Sprites enter ready, so they can be played before attacking and then moved in

You cannot play them retroactively in response to opponent actions like buffing their units

question: Can you spend a buff on a unit controlled by your teammate in 2v2 to pay the cost for cards like Troll Chant?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot spend buffs on units controlled by your teammate. A player can only spend buffs on units they control, unless a card specifically allows otherwise.

Nuances:

Cards may override this restriction if they explicitly specify spending buffs on friendly units or teammate units

question: Can Ride The Wind move a unit without Ganking from battlefield to battlefield, and does this trigger a showdown?
answer:
Ruling: Ride The Wind has no movement restriction, so any unit (with or without Ganking) can move from battlefield to battlefield. Moving to a battlefield triggers a showdown regardless of whether the opponent has units there.

Nuances:

Standard Move has the restriction of requiring Ganking to move between battlefield to battlefield (otherwise it must be battlefield to base)

If the opponent has units at the destination battlefield, it becomes combat and the showdown will be staged if there's already one ongoing

Whoever applied contested to the battlefield first is considered the attacker

question: Can Ornn equip gear to another unit during the opponent's turn, specifically if a unit equipped with gear is killed?
answer:
Ruling: No, Ornn cannot equip gear during the opponent's turn. Ornn's ability only creates Power and does not grant the Equip ability Reaction timing.

Nuances:

You can equip during the opponent's turn if you have an equipment with the Quickdraw ability

You can equip during the opponent's turn if you have a unit with Weaponmaster

The Equip tag does not have Reaction on it, so it cannot be used at reaction speed unless specifically granted that timing

question: If Hidden Blade targets a unit that survives due to Unlicensed Armory, does the Hidden Blade player still draw 2 cards?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you still draw 2 cards when Hidden Blade targets a unit that survives. The draw effect is not conditional on the unit dying.

Nuances:

The draw effect checks for controller, not owner. If the unit is returned to hand before Hidden Blade resolves, you do not draw.

If you react to Hidden Blade with something that kills the chosen unit before Hidden Blade resolves, you do not draw because the unit is gone and has no controller when Hidden Blade checks.

question: Does Eager Apprentice's cost reduction activate if he's the attacker?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Eager Apprentice's cost reduction activates when he is the attacker.

Nuances:

While attacking, a unit is still considered to be "at a battlefield"

question: When a chain resolves, does priority pass to the next player, or can you resolve your action and play another action before passing priority?
answer:
Ruling: Priority must pass to the next player when a chain resolves. You cannot resolve your action and then play another action before passing priority.

Nuances:

This is technically handled by the Focus mechanic, not just priority passing during the active chain.

question: When Switcheroo is used on a unit with an Assault bonus, does the opponent's unit gain the Assault bonus again after switching might values?
answer:
Ruling: When Switcheroo switches might values, the Assault bonus is not reapplied. The attacking unit keeps its Assault bonus but now applies it to the switched (lower) might value.

Sequence:

Assault bonus is applied when a unit enters combat as an attacker

Switcheroo switches the current might values of both units

The Assault bonus remains active but is now calculated from the new (switched) might value

The unit that was originally attacking maintains the Attacker designation with Assault, but at reduced effectiveness

Nuances:

If a unit with Assault 2 has 4 total might (2 base + 2 Assault) and switches with a 1 might unit, the result is: the attacking unit has 1 might with Assault 2 (still 1 might total), and the other unit has 4 might

If the attacking unit then loses the Attacker designation (e.g., via Flash), it would lose the Assault bonus entirely

question: Can two of the same battlefield be used at the same time in a game?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if both players select the same battlefield, then two of the same battlefield can be used at the same time.

Nuances:

This only occurs when both players independently select the same battlefield during battlefield selection.

question: How does Bellows Breath work? Can you choose the same unit multiple times?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot choose the same unit multiple times. You choose zero, one, two, or three units at the same location and deal each of them 1 damage.

Nuances:

With repeat paid, the maximum damage to a single unit is 2 (choosing it once in each resolution of the ability)

question: When Caitlyn is given Tank (e.g., via Lecturing Yordle), does she get assigned as a blocker first or last, and who decides? Also, if Caitlyn is in a battle formation with a creature that has Tank, what is the blocking order?
answer:
Ruling: When Caitlyn is given Tank, the attacker decides whether to assign her as a blocker first OR last.

Nuances:

The opponent (attacker) gets to choose the order

This applies when Caitlyn receives Tank from effects like Lecturing Yordle

question: Does Fox-Fire kill everything with 4 might or lower individually, or any number of units whose combined might totals 4 or less?
answer:
Ruling: Fox-Fire kills any number of units whose combined might is 4 or less (e.g., a 2 might and a 2 might, or a 3 might and a 1 might). You must choose and declare targets when playing the spell, before opponents can react.

Sequence:

Choose targets when playing the spell (units whose combined might is 4 or less at a single battlefield)

Opponent can react knowing your targets

Spell resolves and kills the targeted units (if still legal targets)

Nuances:

All targeted units must be at the same battlefield ("at a battlefield" means only one battlefield)

If an opponent buffs a targeted unit in response, making the combined might exceed 4, the targets become illegal and the spell has no effect

This works similarly to other targeted removal like Gust - you can buff units out of range as counterplay

question: Can Relentless Pursuit be used to attach equipment that is already attached to another unit under your control?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you can use Relentless Pursuit to attach equipment that is already attached to another unit under your control.

question: Are the Tournament Rules region-specific with respect to Standard-legal sets, particularly regarding whether Chinese cards from newer sets can be played before their English release outside of China?
answer:
Ruling: China has their own rule documents, suggesting region-specific tournament rules exist.

Nuances:

The location of Chinese rule documents is uncertain

This implies Chinese cards from staggered releases would follow region-specific legality

question: Does Ravenborn Tome increase the damage of Falling Star's reflexive triggers, making it deal 4+4 damage instead of 3+3?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ravenborn Tome increases each instance of damage from Falling Star to 4+4. The Tome adds damage to the spell, and the reflexive triggers still count as the spell dealing damage, even though they cannot be countered.

Nuances:

The reflexive triggers are not spells themselves and cannot be countered with cards like Wind Wall

The Tome explicitly states "each instance of damage the spell deals is increased by one"

This is different from abilities that instruct something other than the card itself to deal damage (like Carnivorous Snapvine)

Challenge damage would not be boosted because the units deal damage to each other, not the spell or ability

question: Does Tank affect spell damage, and what happens when a unit with Tank is played as a reaction to a spell targeting another unit?
answer:
Ruling: Tank only applies to combat damage and does not affect spell damage. When a unit with Tank is played as a reaction to a spell targeting another unit, the spell damage is not redirected or prevented.

Nuances:

Tank has no effect outside of the combat damage step

Playing a unit with Tank in response to spell damage does not change the spell's target or prevent the damage

question: Can a Hidden Zhonya's at one battlefield be flipped to save a unit during a showdown at a different battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, a Hidden Zhonya's can be flipped from one battlefield to save a unit at a different battlefield. When flipped, it immediately recalls to base, and since it doesn't target, it isn't restricted to the current battlefield.

Sequence:

Zhonya's is flipped from its hidden battlefield

It immediately recalls to base

From base, it can save any unit at any battlefield

Nuances:

This applies to Hidden cards generally, but with restrictions: Hidden cards can be flipped at any time you can play a reaction, but if the card has to target or is a unit, it must be played to/affect the battlefield it was hidden at

Zhonya's works across battlefields because it both recalls to base when flipped AND doesn't target a specific unit

question: When Ravenbloom Student triggers from multiple spells being played, what is the timing and sequence of spell resolution and the +1/+1 counter triggers?
answer:
Ruling: Ravenbloom Student gets its +1/+1 counter after each spell resolves. Each spell fully resolves before the triggered ability goes on the chain and resolves.

Sequence:

First spell resolves

Ravenbloom Student trigger resolves (gets +1/+1 counter)

Second spell resolves

Ravenbloom Student trigger resolves (gets +1/+1 counter)

Third spell resolves

Ravenbloom Student trigger resolves (gets +1/+1 counter)

Nuances:

Each triggered ability that gives the +1/+1 counter is itself a triggered ability that goes on the chain and can be responded to

Opponents can respond to the trigger while it's on the chain (e.g., removing the Student with a Gust before the counter resolves)

question: Does it matter whether a card targets or not, and do Snapvine and Last Breath target differently?
answer:
Ruling: Whether or not something targets determines if you need to select targets as you put it onto the chain. Last Breath should target both the friendly unit and the enemy unit.

Nuances:

Targeting is currently ambiguous in the rules and under discussion

Generally, if a card has you select/act upon an object from some set of possible objects (instead of acting upon an entire set of objects), it targets that object

Cards with "Then" in their text (like Dragon's Rage) create additional ambiguity about what they target

Snapvine targets and also says "a" battlefield not "this" battlefield, so you play it to your base and it fights a unit at a battlefield

question: Can the attacker activate a reaction card after both the attacker and defender have passed focus in combat?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play a reaction after both players pass focus. Once both players pass focus in succession, combat moves to the damage step where no one has priority.

Sequence:

Attacker passes focus

Defender passes focus

Combat resolves and moves to damage step (no priority available)

Nuances:

If you pass focus and your opponent plays anything, focus comes back to you before combat resolves

Both players must pass focus in a row for combat to resolve

Reactions do not state "play at any time"

question: Can a hidden Zonyah's be activated if a Bryndhir Thundersong was played on the turn by an opponent?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot activate Zonyah's after Bryndhir's effect resolves, but you can play it in response to Bryndhir's ability when it goes onto the chain.

Sequence:

Opponent plays Bryndhir Thundersong

Bryndhir's ability goes onto the chain

You can respond by activating hidden Zonyah's at this point

Once Bryndhir's effect resolves, you cannot activate Zonyah's

Nuances:

You cannot respond to Bryndhir being played itself, only to the ability when it goes onto the chain

question: When dazzling finds a unit, can it be played anywhere or only to your base/a battlefield you control?
answer:
Ruling: When dazzling finds a unit, it follows the same restrictions as playing any card - you can play it to your base or a battlefield you control unless the unit card itself specifies otherwise.

Nuances:

Some units like Sneaky Deckhand or Deadbloom Predator have text that allows them to be played to different locations, overriding the default restriction

question: Does damage heal on units that were not involved in combat?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, damage is healed on every unit at the end of combat, even those not involved in the combat.

Nuances:

This applies to units damaged earlier in the turn (e.g., by Challenge) that remain at base while other units engage in combat

Healing occurs during the combat resolution/cleanup step for all marked units

question: Does Kai'Sa's ability (which ignores power cost to play a spell) trigger Lux's ability (which triggers on playing 5+ cost spells)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, playing a 5+ cost spell with Kai'Sa's conquer ability will trigger Lux Legends' ability to draw an extra card.

Nuances:

The spell still has its original cost value even though you ignore the power cost to play it

Kai'Sa's ability allows you to ignore the cost, but doesn't change what the spell's cost is for the purpose of other card effects

question: Can a player pass priority after playing a reaction, and if both players pass, play another reaction before the first reaction resolves?
answer:
Ruling: No. When you play a reaction you hold priority, but if you pass priority and your opponent also passes, both players have passed sequentially and the top item on the chain resolves.

Sequence:

Player plays a reaction and holds priority

Player passes priority

Opponent passes priority

Top item on chain resolves (both players passed sequentially)

After an item resolves, both players get priority again (whoever has the latest item on the chain gets priority first)

Players can now respond to remaining items on the chain

Nuances:

You can play multiple reactions while holding priority without passing

After a reaction resolves, you can still play reactions to earlier items still on the chain

question: Can you hold priority to chain a reaction after an action to prevent the action from being denied or countered?
answer:
Ruling: No, holding priority does not protect your action from being countered. Counter spells like Defy can target any spell on the chain, not just the most recent one.

Sequence:

You can add multiple spells to the chain before passing priority

Opponent can target any spell on the chain with a counter, not just the most recent

Alternatively, you can let the chain partially resolve, allowing the reaction to resolve first, then counter the action afterward

Nuances:

There is no way to truly "block" an opponent from countering your spell by chaining reactions after it

Even if you let your reaction resolve first, the opponent can still counter the action once it's the only spell remaining on the chain

question: How does the repeat mechanic work with targeting - do you have to target the same cards or can you choose different targets?
answer:
Ruling: When you use repeat, you can choose different targets for each repetition. For example, Piercing Light can KO multiple different units with 2 or less might across the battlefield and back row.

Sequence:

Declare repeat

Pay the additional costs

Make all targeting choices

Then the opponent gets an opportunity to react

Nuances:

By the time an opponent can play a spell in reaction, they will know exactly what all the targets are

If a player passes priority without repeating, they cannot choose to repeat later

question: When Watcher reduces all units' Might by 2 and then Rumble, Scrapper (who gives +1 Might to all mechs) is killed by the same spell, what is the final Might of the mech tokens?
answer:
Ruling: The mech tokens end up at 0 Might but do not die. Units can have 0 Might without dying.

Sequence:

Arcane Shift begins resolving, playing Watcher to base

Watcher's ETB effect is not on the chain yet (Arcane Shift must fully resolve first)

Arcane Shift deals 3 damage to Rumble, Scrapper, killing it

Arcane Shift finishes resolving

Watcher's ETB effect goes on the chain and resolves, reducing all units' Might by 2

At the time Watcher's effect applies, the mech tokens are at 4 Might (3 base + 1 from Rumble still active)

Watcher's effect snapshots and reduces them to 1 Might (4 - 2, limited to minimum 1)

After Watcher's effect resolves, Rumble's +1 Might buff is removed as a state-based effect

The tokens drop from 1 Might to 0 Might

Nuances:

Watcher's effect is snapshotted when applied and limited at that time

Rumble's continuous effect is always checked and has no limitation

Units at 0 Might do not die

question: In a multiplayer game, if Player A controls a Battlefield and Player B moves their unit to start a showdown, can Player C use movement cards like Ride The Wind or Zenith's Blade to move their unit to that Showdown?
answer:
Ruling: Player C can cast the movement spell when priority passes to them, but the spell will fail to move the unit because a battlefield cannot have units from more than 2 players at it at any point.

Sequence:

Player B moves their unit to start a showdown at Player A's battlefield

Priority passes around the table, including to Player C

Player C can cast movement spells like Ride The Wind

The movement effect fails because the battlefield already has units from 2 players

Nuances:

Priority still goes around the table to all players during a showdown, even if they cannot successfully move units to that battlefield

question: Can a player activate hidden cards at a battlefield that is not involved in the current showdown?
answer:
Ruling: Hidden cards can be activated during a showdown at a different battlefield, but they must affect the battlefield they are hidden on, so they cannot impact combat at the showdown location.

Nuances:

The activation itself is legal regardless of where the showdown is occurring

Hidden cards have an additional requirement that they must affect the battlefield where they are hidden

This applies to both hidden units and hidden spells

question: If a single unit dies while you have 2 Zhonya's Hourglasses in play, do both activate or only one?
answer:
Ruling: Only one Zhonya's Hourglass will apply. Both replacement effects are available, but you can only replace the same death event once.

Sequence:

Both Zhonya's replacement effects apply to the same death event

The owner chooses the order in which they apply

The first Zhonya's replaces the death with a recall

The second Zhonya's has nothing to replace since the unit is no longer dying

Nuances:

Zhonya's is a passive replacement effect, not a trigger, so it doesn't use the Chain

Replacement effects can intercede other effect resolutions

The same principle applies to combinations like Guardian Angel + Zhonya's

question: What happens to equipment attached to a unit when you take control of that unit?
answer:
Ruling: The answer depends on whether the controlled unit moves to your base or stays on the board. For effects like Hostile Takeover where the unit stays on the board but doesn't move to your base, the equipment remains attached. For effects like Possession where the unit moves to your base, the equipment falls off because rule 106.2.d states other players cannot have game objects they control in another player's base.

Nuances:

Taking control is different from ownership

If you take control of gear itself, you can have it in your base

If you choose to detach equipment from a controlled unit, it would go to the opponent's base as they are the owner and controller of that equipment

The comprehensive rules may need updates to fully clarify base-to-base transitions and whether equipment can exist at an opponent's base while attached

question: If I have no units on battlefield and my opponent has 1 unit (Ahri) and 1 Hidden Card, and I use a spell to deal damage to kill Ahri, does the Hidden Card get trashed or can my opponent reveal it as a reaction?
answer:
Ruling: The opponent can reveal the Hidden Card as a reaction on the same chain as the kill spell before it resolves, preventing the Hidden Card from being trashed.

Sequence:

You cast a spell targeting the opponent's only unit on the battlefield

Before the spell resolves, the opponent can reveal their Hidden Card as a reaction

If revealed, the Hidden Card enters the battlefield and prevents itself from being trashed

The spell then resolves

Nuances:

Hidden Cards cannot be revealed as a reaction on the same turn they are played

If a player has no units remaining on a battlefield with a Hidden Card, that card gets trashed

Not all Hidden Cards are units (e.g., Hidden Blade), so targeting the only unit can still force suboptimal plays

When a Hidden Card is flipped up, that's when it counts as being played and can be responded to (e.g., with Windwall)

question: When playing Teemo Strategist from hidden during an attack on Fortified Positions (with Viktor Innovator in base), what is the correct trigger ordering, specifically when do Viktor's and Teemo's triggers go on the chain?
answer:
Ruling: The ordering described is correct. After Teemo resolves as a permanent, both Viktor Innovator's trigger and Teemo Strategist's defend trigger occur simultaneously, so you can choose the order they go on the chain.

Sequence:

Ahri Inquisitive's attack trigger goes on the chain first (opponent is contesting)

Fortified Position's defend trigger goes on chain (target must be chosen immediately)

No reactions can go between attack trigger and defend trigger

Attacker has priority and passes

Defender has priority and reacts by flipping Teemo from hidden

Teemo resolves (nothing can react to a permanent)

Viktor Innovator's trigger and Teemo's defend trigger both trigger simultaneously and can be ordered by the controller

question: Can the 8th point be scored by conquering battlefields if you don't control all previously scored battlefields?
answer:
Ruling: To get the 8th point from conquering, you only need to have scored all other battlefields previously; you don't need to actually control them at the time you score the 8th point.

Nuances:

A player can conquer one battlefield, retreat from it, then conquer another battlefield to score the 8th point, as long as they had scored all other battlefields at some point.

question: What speed can Baited Hook be played at?
answer:
Ruling: Baited Hook is played at base speed because it does not have the Reaction keyword.

Nuances:

In Riftbound, cards are literal with their timing - if a card doesn't have the "Reaction" keyword, it cannot be used as a reaction

The tap symbol (turn sideways icon) does not indicate reaction or action speed by itself

Hidden cards are an exception as they gain the Reaction keyword and can be flipped at reaction speed

question: Does the might bonus from assault and shield stay after combat ends?
answer: Ruling: No, the might bonus from assault and shield does not stay after combat ends. The cleanup at the end of combat clears the attacker and defender statuses.

question: If I use Voidseeker on a unit and the opponent flashes it to their base, do I still draw a card?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you still draw a card even if the unit is flashed to base in response to Voidseeker.

Nuances:

The draw part of Voidseeker has no dependency on the damage part due to the period separator between the two effects

Even if there were a comma instead of a period, you would still be able to draw (similar to how "discard 1, draw 1" triggers resolve with DAMAYC)

question: Can you stack the play effects of Albus Ferros and Cithria of Cloudfield to give Cithria a buff before using that buff for Albus's effect?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can stack the play effects to give Cithria a buff before using that buff to trigger Albus's effect.

Sequence:

Stack the play effects

Resolve Cithria's effect first to give her a buff

Use that buff to satisfy Albus's effect condition

question: When conquering a battlefield at 7 points with Zaun Warren and an empty hand, can you choose the order of drawing from the conquer attempt and Zaun Warren's discard-then-draw effect?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot choose the order. Scoring the point (or drawing a card when at 7 points) happens as part of the conquer effect itself and does not use the chain. Zaun Warren's trigger only goes on the chain after the conquer is complete.

Sequence:

You conquer the battlefield and immediately draw a card (instead of scoring point 8) as part of the conquer effect

Zaun Warren's conquer trigger then goes on the chain

When Zaun Warren's trigger resolves, you discard then draw

Nuances:

The scoring/card draw is part of the conquer effect itself, not a separate triggered ability

Zaun Warren only triggers after the conquer is done, so it cannot be stacked before the conquer's built-in effects

question: Can Nocturne be played after using Stacked Deck when an opponent contests a battlefield you control?
answer:
Ruling: No, Nocturne cannot be played in this scenario because Stacked Deck does not draw cards - it only looks at cards from the top of your deck. Nocturne's ability specifically triggers when you look at cards from the top of your deck and don't draw them, but in this case you would need to actually see Nocturne during the look effect, not draw it.

Nuances:

Stacked Deck does not resolve "at a battlefield" - it resolves on the stack

Nocturne can be played to any battlefield you control when its trigger condition is met

The key issue is that Stacked Deck's effect is looking at cards, not drawing them

question: Does Ornn's legend ability affect the equip cost of equipment (i.e., is equip cost considered a 'gear ability')?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the equip cost is affected by Ornn's legend ability because equip is an activated ability for Gear.

Nuances:

Equip is classified as an activated ability of Gear cards

question: Can Ancient Henge's energy-to-power conversion reaction be used during Bullet Time's resolution to pay for Bullet Time's variable cost, or must it be tapped in advance?
answer:
Ruling: Ancient Henge can be used during Bullet Time's resolution to pay for the variable cost. You do not need to tap it in advance or declare how much energy you want to convert before resolution.

Sequence:

Play Bullet Time

During Bullet Time's resolution, when you need to pay the variable cost

Use Ancient Henge's reaction ability to convert energy to power as needed

Nuances:

This works because Ancient Henge is a reaction with an add ability, and it can be used during resolution when Bullet Time requires you to pay a cost

This simplifies energy generation to work 'whenever needed' without keeping reaction windows in mind

question: Can you react with hidden cards or reactions when a triggered ability occurs?
answer:
Ruling: You can react to triggered abilities.

Nuances:

This applies even if you have hidden cards or reactions available

question: Can you react to your opponent's damage assignment during the combat damage step of a showdown by playing a discipline to give your unit +2 might?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play cards during the combat damage step in response to damage assignment.

Nuances:

There are no triggers to react to during this period

Players cannot play actions during the combat damage step

question: Does Riftbound have an 'intervening if' rule, and does Dune Drake trigger on attack regardless of conditions?
answer:
Ruling: Riftbound does not have an "intervening if" rule. Dune Drake triggers on attack no matter what, functioning like a conditional ASSAULT 2.

Nuances:

Even if Riftbound had Magic's "intervening if" rule, Dune Drake's ability wouldn't qualify as one because the condition is not intervening between the trigger condition and the effect.

question: Can I play Retreat in response to my own Retreat to get 2 exhausted runes?
answer:
Ruling: No, this does not work. When the first Retreat resolves (last on the stack), it cannot find the owner anymore, so you don't channel the 1 rune.

Sequence:

Play first Retreat

Play second Retreat in response

Second Retreat resolves first, returns the unit

First Retreat resolves, but cannot find the unit to return, so no rune is channeled

question: When playing a card with Accelerate from the trash using Soulgorger, can you pay the additional cost to have it accelerated?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can still play the card with Accelerate when playing it from trash via Soulgorger, but you must pay both the Accelerate cost (additional energy and power) and any other costs required by the effect that allows you to play it from trash.

Nuances:

The Accelerate cost is paid in addition to, not instead of, other costs required to play the card from trash

question: Does Kaisa's legend ability work with hiding cards?
answer:
Ruling: Kaisa's legend ability cannot be used to hide a card because hiding is not considered playing a card, and the card does not count as played until it is flipped as a reaction.

Nuances:

Hiding a card is distinct from playing a card

A hidden card only counts as played when it is flipped as a reaction

question: Does Maddened Marauder have to move a ready unit, since exhausting is a cost to pay for movement? Does the same apply to Stormbringer?
answer:
Ruling: Moving by an effect is not a standard move. Only the standard move requires you to exhaust the unit.

Nuances:

Units can be moved by effects regardless of their state (ready or exhausted) to any place unless stated otherwise

question: If I play En Guard on my unit at a battlefield with Dreaming Tree (3+ might), and my opponent reacts with Gust, do I still get the Dreaming Tree draw?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you still get the Dreaming Tree draw. Dreaming Tree chains directly to the spell that targeted your unit, so it triggers before your opponent can respond with Gust.

Sequence:

En Guard is played

Dreaming Tree triggers and chains to En Guard

Opponent can then respond with Gust

Dreaming Tree resolves regardless of what happens after

question: In a summoner skirmish, what are the rules on performing ABCD (Awaken, Begin, Channel, Draw) steps at the start of turn, including: 1) Does order matter? 2) Can you do steps in any order with hold battlefield triggers? 3) What happens if you forget to awaken a legend and realize mid-turn?
answer:
Ruling: You must perform ABCD steps in the correct order (Awaken, Begin, Channel, Draw). Holding battlefield triggers occur at the end of the Begin phase. If you skip a step and move to a later one, judges may not allow you to go back.

Sequence:

Awaken

Begin (hold battlefield triggers happen at end of this phase)

Channel

Draw

Nuances:

Shortcutting is technically allowed if you explain it once and give your opponent time to react, but it's best practice to follow proper order to avoid issues

At casual events like Nexus Nights, players are more lenient about shortcutting

At competitive events, judges have ruled that skipping steps (like channeling before drawing, or drawing before performing Begin phase triggers) means you cannot go back

If you forget to awaken a legend and catch it mid-turn, both players would likely receive a warning (the Kaisa player for General Error, the opponent for Failure to Maintain Game State) and play continues

question: When Nine-Tailed Fox's ability triggers to give attacking 1 might units -1 might (minimum 1), and then Siphon Power gives those same units +1 might, what is their final might value?
answer:
Ruling: The units end up with 2 might. Minus might effects "snapshot" at the time of their resolution, so when Nine-Tailed Fox's trigger resolves against 1 might units, it gives them -0 might due to the "minimum of 1 might" condition. The effect doesn't retroactively update when Siphon Power later increases their might.

Sequence:

Nine-Tailed Fox's trigger resolves first, attempting to give the 1 might units -1 might

Due to the "minimum of 1 might" clause, the effect snapshots and gives them -0 might (they stay at 1 might)

Siphon Power then gives them +1 might

Final result: 2 might units

Nuances:

The "minimum of 1 might" clause causes the effect to snapshot at resolution time and does not retroactively update if the unit's might changes later in the turn

question: Does damage from Challenge (and similar non-combat abilities) persist until combat happens or the turn ends?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, damage from Challenge persists on units until combat resolves on any battlefield or the turn ends. The damaged unit does not need to participate in that combat to be healed.

Sequence:

Challenge deals damage equal to each unit's might to the other

Damage remains on both units

When any combat occurs on any battlefield, damage is removed from all units at the end of combat

Alternatively, damage is removed at end of turn

Nuances:

Combat only occurs when battlefields are contested, not from abilities like Challenge

A unit can be healed by sending a different unit to contest a battlefield and trigger combat

If either unit involved in Challenge leaves the field before it resolves, no damage is applied because the might value is no longer available

question: When The Boss saves a buffed unit that has damage marked on it, does the unit retain its previously marked damage or is it healed?
answer:
Ruling: The Boss heals the unit when saving it, so it will have no damage marked after being saved.

Sequence:

Buffed unit at 4 Might has 3 damage marked

Falling Star deals 3 damage (first instance)

The Boss saves the unit by spending the buff

Unit is healed to 0 damage

Unit now has 3 Might (buff spent)

Second Falling Star instance deals 3 damage and kills the unit

Nuances:

The Boss requires spending the buff to save the unit, which reduces the unit's Might

Even though the unit is healed, it can still die to subsequent damage if its Might was reduced by spending the buff

question: When a unit with buffs is taken over by Possession, does the new owner keep the buffs that were applied to it?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, when a unit is taken over by Possession, the new owner keeps the buffs that were applied to the card.

Nuances:

Buffs are applied to the card itself, not to the owner, so they transfer with the card when control changes.

question: If Ezreal kills Lucian with his defender trigger before Lucian's attacker trigger resolves, does Lucian still deal damage?
answer:
Ruling: No, Lucian does not deal damage. If Lucian dies to Ezreal's trigger before his own trigger resolves, the returned value would be Null and wouldn't do any damage.

Sequence:

Ezreal's defender ability triggers first

Ezreal deals 3 damage to Lucian, killing him

Lucian's attacker trigger attempts to resolve

Since Lucian is no longer in play (in trash), the ability executes what it can but cannot deal damage

Nuances:

The trigger doesn't completely disappear, but it returns a Null value since the source is no longer present

The ability executes what it can, but cannot deal damage when the source unit is in the trash

question: Can you play the effect of a hidden card targeting the other battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, hidden cards cannot target units or make choices at a different battlefield than where they were hidden. All choices must be made at the battlefield where the card was hidden, if able.

Nuances:

Some cards like Tideturner can get around this restriction because they specify "another" battlefield in their text

Some cards like Stand United still have effects beyond their targets that can apply elsewhere

Hidden cards can still be played from one battlefield to react to events at another battlefield, as long as the card doesn't require targeting (you can play a hidden card from battlefield 1 during a showdown at battlefield 2 if it doesn't need to target)

Hidden cards cannot be played the same turn they are hidden

The restriction on hidden cards only applies to their targeting, not to when they can be played as reactions

question: Does Emperor's Divide work with Blade Dancer (Irelia's ability that triggers when you target or choose a unit)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Emperor's Divide works with Blade Dancer. The spell targets/chooses the units being moved, not just the battlefield and number.

Sequence:

When you play Emperor's Divide, you choose which specific units to move as part of placing the spell on the chain

This counts as targeting/choosing units for Blade Dancer's trigger

The units are selected before resolution, not during or after

Nuances:

Emperor's Divide is worded similarly to Foxfire, which also targets units

Spells like Whirlwind do NOT trigger Blade Dancer because the unit selection happens after resolution (both players may select, and it's a "may" selection made after the spell resolves)

The key distinction is whether you choose/target units when placing the spell on the chain versus selecting units during or after resolution

question: Does Grand Stratagem give a snapshot buff at resolution, or does it passively buff units that enter the board after it resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Grand Stratagem gives its buff only to units present on the board when it resolves. Units that enter the board after resolution do not receive the buff.

Sequence:

Grand Stratagem resolves

It buffs all units currently on the board at that moment

Any units entering the board afterward are not affected

question: When Gust is used in reaction to Discipline targeting a unit, does Gust resolve first and does the Discipline player still draw a card after their target is returned?
answer:
Ruling: When you react with Gust to an opponent's Discipline, Gust resolves first and returns the unit. The opponent still draws a card from Discipline even though the target unit is no longer present.

Sequence:

Gust resolves first, returning the unit that was targeted by Discipline

Discipline then resolves as much as possible

The Discipline player draws 1 card (does not require information about the unit to draw)

Nuances:

Spells always resolve as much as possible even if they lose their target

The arithmetic value change rules are for simultaneous positive and negative value changes (like Discipline and Smoke Screen used together), not for this interaction

question: When recycling cards during mulligan or with effects like Dazzling Aurora, do you need to shuffle the recycled cards before placing them at the bottom of the deck?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, when 2 or more cards are recycled simultaneously (whether during mulligan or from card effects), they must be placed at the bottom of the deck in a random order, which requires shuffling them.

Nuances:

While shuffling only 2 cards can be easily manipulated, your opponent has the opportunity to shuffle again

You won't gain much information from knowing the order of cards on the bottom of your deck

question: Does Darius (5c Red 5 Might) count himself as the second card played, and can he become ready again if exhausted when a second card is played?
answer:
Ruling: Darius can count himself as the second card played. If Darius is exhausted at a battlefield and a second card is played that turn, he will become ready.

Sequence:

Play Darius as the second card of the turn

Darius's effect triggers, counting himself

If Darius was already exhausted when the second card is played, he becomes ready

question: When Ezreal attacks and the defender has Reaver's Row, does Ezreal's damage land before the defender can move a unit off, or can the unit move off safely before taking damage?
answer:
Ruling: When Ezreal attacks, the defender can move their unit off safely using Reaver's Row before Ezreal's damage resolves. If the target is no longer present when Ezreal's ability resolves, it deals no damage.

Sequence:

Ezreal's trigger goes on the chain first (as attacker)

Reaver's Row trigger goes on the chain second (as defender)

Reactions may happen

Reaver's Row resolves (unit moves)

Reactions may happen

Ezreal's ability resolves (but target is gone, so no damage)

Nuances:

If Ezreal is the defender instead, the order reverses: Reaver's Row stacks first, then Ezreal, so Ezreal resolves first and would deal damage before the unit can move

question: Can you respond to an opponent playing a unit with a reaction spell?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot respond to an opponent playing a unit. Units leave the chain directly without a round of priority, unlike spells which linger on the chain.

Nuances:

Units, gear, and abilities that Add resources all leave the chain immediately without allowing responses

In the scenario described, Vayne would enter readied (not exhausted) because there is no opportunity to respond by removing your unit from the battlefield before Vayne enters

question: Does a unit heal damage when moving to an empty battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Units do not heal when moving to an empty battlefield. Going to an empty battlefield is a showdown but not combat, and units only heal after combat or at the end of the turn.

Nuances:

Moving to an empty battlefield counts as a showdown

A showdown is not the same as combat

Units heal after combat

Units also heal at the end of the turn

question: What happens when a player kills the controller's only unit at a Contested Battlefield during staged Combat (while the controller still has a Hidden card there), and when can the Hidden card be played?
answer:
Ruling: This is currently a hole in the rules. When the unit is killed, Combat stops being staged (since units from two opposing players are no longer present), but the Contested status remains with no mechanism to remove it. The battlefield becomes stuck in a state where it's controlled by one player, contested by another, but neither a Showdown nor Combat can be staged.

Sequence:

Player A moves unit to Player B's controlled battlefield, applying Contested and staging Combat

Player A kills Player B's only unit (Poro) via Shakedown during the trigger reaction

During cleanup, Combat stops being staged (no units from two opposing players present)

Contested status remains but cannot be removed (only removed during Showdowns/Combats)

No Showdown stages (battlefield is controlled, not uncontrolled)

No Combat stages (only one player has units present)

Battlefield becomes stuck: controlled by B, contested by A, with no staged event

Nuances:

The Hidden card cannot be played because there's no mechanism to progress the game state

A future rules update should remove Contested status when Combat stops being staged due to lack of opposing units

If Contested were removed and no units present, battlefield would become uncontrolled

If Contested were removed with units present, a new Showdown/Combat would stage

question: Does Fox-Fire targeting a group of units change how Deflect costs are paid?
answer:
Ruling: Fox-Fire targeting a group of units does not change how Deflect works. You must pay Deflect costs for each targeted unit that has Deflect.

Sequence:

Deflect costs are paid when selecting the targets

This applies to each unit with Deflect in the targeted group

question: Do skirmish tournaments have a mandatory top-8 cut, and what determines the tournament structure?
answer:
Ruling: Summoner Skirmish tournaments on Carde.io automatically enforce a top-8 cut after Swiss rounds. The number of Swiss rounds is determined by player count and handled automatically by the system.

Sequence:

Swiss rounds are played based on player count (9-16 players = 4 rounds, 17-32 players = 5 rounds, 33-64 players = 6 rounds)

After Swiss, automatic top-8 cut occurs

Top-8 seeding is determined by tiebreakers: OMW > GW > OGW

Matchups are 1v8, 2v7, 3v6, 4v5

Nuances:

The top-8 cut is mandatory for Summoner Skirmish specifically because the Carde.io system enforces it

For who chooses to go first in top cut: tournament rules make no distinction between top cut and Swiss, so it should be random for game 1. Some TOs have house-ruled that higher seed chooses to avoid intentional draws, but this is not an official rule.

question: If a hidden card at a battlefield is flipped and used to defend in the same showdown, will its trigger activate twice?
answer: Ruling: No, the trigger will not activate twice in the same showdown.

question: If Sett-Brawler and an opponent's unit deal lethal damage to each other in a showdown, can Sett-The Boss's ability be used to recall the Brawler before it dies from the lethal damage?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Sett-The Boss's ability can be used to recall the Brawler before it dies. Both units will exchange damage and receive lethal damage, but cleanup that kills units with lethal damage happens after the damage is dealt, allowing Sett-The Boss's ability to trigger and recall the Brawler to base before cleanup occurs.

Sequence:

Sett-Brawler and Darius exchange damage in the showdown (both receive lethal damage)

Sett-The Boss's ability can be activated to recall the Brawler

Cleanup phase occurs where units with lethal damage would be killed

The recalled Brawler survives at base; Darius dies

question: What happens during combat resolution if there are still units from 2 players present in a combat showdown?
answer: Ruling: If there are still units from 2 players present during the combat resolution step of a combat showdown, the attackers are recalled to base.

question: When Ekko Recurrent dies in combat, do you recycle him and ready your runes before combat cleanup, and can you use those runes to finish off damaged units?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot use the readied runes to deal further damage to units damaged in combat. Deathknell resolves after combat cleanup.

Sequence:

Combat damage is dealt

Combat cleanup occurs (damaged units heal)

Deathknell triggers and resolves (Ekko is recycled and runes ready)

No reaction window exists after Deathknell to use the readied runes

Nuances:

The rules as written don't perfectly match this intended timing, but the FAQ on Kog'Maw clarifies that Deathknell resolves after combat cleanup

question: If you hold a battlefield at the start of turn, then leave it and move back to conquer it again in the same turn, do you trigger the battlefield's conquest effects again?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot conquer a battlefield if you have already held it that turn. Once you've scored a battlefield by holding it, moving back to it later in the same turn does not trigger conquest effects.

Sequence:

If you hold a battlefield at start of turn, you score it

If you then leave the battlefield and return to it later that turn

Even if you win a showdown and gain control, you do not conquer it again

No conquest effects trigger

Nuances:

Conquering is a subset of scoring, not a separate mechanic

This applies even if the battlefield changes control between when you held it and when you return (e.g., through active defender mechanics)

question: If I use Ride the Wind during a showdown to move to another battlefield, what happens to the first showdown and can I get points from both?
answer:
Ruling: You need to let showdowns complete to get their point. If you use Ride the Wind during a showdown as an action, that showdown still continues and must conclude normally with combat damage assigned by units at that battlefield.

Sequence:

Use Ride the Wind during a showdown as an action

The original showdown continues, passing focus normally

Combat damage is assigned by units at that battlefield

The showdown concludes and you get the point

If conditions are met for a different showdown at the new battlefield, that showdown happens immediately

You can potentially get points from both showdowns

question: Can Vi's ability be activated multiple times per turn as long as you can recycle, and what are the timing restrictions?
answer:
Ruling: Vi's ability can be activated any number of times in a turn as long as you can recycle, since there are no restrictions on the card limiting frequency. However, since it's not an action or reaction, you cannot activate it on your opponent's turn, and your opponent can respond to you activating Vi.

Sequence:

You can only activate Vi's ability on your own turn

You can activate it multiple times as long as you have cards to recycle

Your opponent can respond to each activation

Nuances:

The ability is neither an action nor a reaction, which restricts when it can be used

question: How many times can you recycle cards from trash to give +1 to Vi(Destructive) per turn?
answer:
Ruling: You can recycle as many cards as are in your trash to give +1 to Vi(Destructive) per turn. There is no exhaust cost or other limit on the ability.

Nuances:

The ability must be used on your turn and not during a showdown, as it does not have a (re)action timing

Your opponent will have an opportunity to react after each instance of +1

question: Can a player wait for their opponent to assign damage after a showdown ends, then play a reaction to buff their unit so it survives?
answer: Ruling: No, you cannot play reactions during damage assignment. Damage assignment happens outside the showdown and does not grant priority to play reactions.

question: Can judges play in Nexus nights at the local level?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, judges can play in Nexus nights at the local level, but the event must be run at Casual OPL (Organized Play Level). The designated Judge of that event would not be able to play.

Nuances:

Nexus nights should be run at Casual OPL anyway

Not all people qualified as Judges are affected by this restriction

If a judge plays in a Skirmish, it would be bumped down to a Casual event

Skirmish events are advised to be held at Competitive OPL

question: Can you float runes (mana) in Riftbound, specifically: exhaust a rune to float mana, play a Seal to recycle the exhausted rune, then use the floated mana for something else?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can float runes in Riftbound. You can exhaust a rune to float mana, play a Seal to recycle that exhausted rune, and then use the floated mana to play something else.

Nuances:

This is described as a very common strategy in the game

question: Can a player use Mystic Reversal to target a spell that was taken by an opponent's Mystic Reversal, and when can they respond?
answer:
Ruling: A player can use Mystic Reversal at two different points: either to take control of the opposing Mystic Reversal itself (which would target their own spell and let them make choices for it again), or after the opposing Mystic Reversal resolves to take control back of their original spell.

Sequence:

Option 1: Respond to opponent's Mystic Reversal by playing your own Mystic Reversal targeting their Mystic Reversal, which targets your own spell and allows you to make choices for it again

Option 2: After opponent's Mystic Reversal resolves and they declare playing your spell, respond with Mystic Reversal to take control back of that spell

Nuances:

Both options have equivalent outcomes in this situation

There may be strategic implications for choosing one option over the other in different scenarios

question: Can you use a reaction ability (like Gust) in response to a unit's Assault or Shield ability triggering?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot react to Assault or Shield abilities.

Nuances:

Assault and Shield are passive abilities that activate automatically as soon as their condition is fulfilled

Once the condition is met, the unit immediately gains the effect without using the stack or allowing reactions

question: In starter deck events, can you exceed 40 cards in your deck and can you include more than 3 copies of a card?
answer:
Ruling: You can exceed 40 cards in your deck at starter deck release events, but you must still follow the 3-copy-per-card limit.

Nuances:

Release events are not Riot sanctioned, so the 40 card + 8 sideboard tournament rule does not apply

In sealed events with 6 packs, you can use more than 3 copies of a card in your 25 card deck

question: When you take an open battleground, what does this trigger and what cards can be played?
answer:
Ruling: Taking an open battleground triggers a showdown. During a showdown, you can play cards and activate abilities that have Action or Reaction printed on them.

Nuances:

Focus is not a card type; it is a term used to give a player priority

Examples of what can be played: cards like Disintegrate or abilities like Kai'Sa

Examples of what cannot be played: abilities like Lee Sin (which presumably don't have Action or Reaction)

question: Can I play Deathbloom Predator to an opponent's battlefield and simultaneously play a friendly unit with Ganking to attack together?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot move multiple units simultaneously when playing them from hand. You can only move one unit at a time when playing cards.

Nuances:

This same restriction applies when using Set's signature spell - you cannot move other units with it

Multiple units can only be moved at the same time through standard movement, which is the inherent capacity of moving units by exhausting them

Any movement that involves playing a unit from hand is restricted to moving only that single unit

question: How do multiple stat modification effects (Leona Zealot's -8M to minimum 1M, Trifarian War Camp's +1M, and Darius's +1M) interact in layer 673.3, and does timestamp order matter?
answer:
Ruling: Leona Zealot's effect applies last always, regardless of when she was played. For other effects in the same layer (673.3), timestamp order determines the sequence.

Sequence:

Effects apply in timestamp order (when the card/effect entered play)

Leona Zealot's -8M (minimum 1M) applies last, after all other effects in that layer

Nuances:

The "minimum of 1M" clause makes ordering matter significantly

It's unclear whether timestamp is based on when the card is played or when the effect becomes active for each individual unit

Layering rules are expected to receive an update for further clarification

question: Can you target a unit at a base and move it to the same base just to trigger Dragons Rage effects?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot move a unit to its own current location to trigger Dragons Rage effects.

Nuances:

"Move" requires a destination that is different from the unit's current location

question: Does Nocturne come into the game exhausted or ready when played from Teemo's ability?
answer: Ruling: Nocturne enters exhausted. All units are played exhausted unless an effect or ability specifies that they enter ready.

question: When does Mask of Foresight's ability trigger, and does it trigger again if a unit becomes alone later in combat?
answer:
Ruling: Mask of Foresight triggers when a unit is first marked as attacker/defender and is alone at that time. It does not trigger again if a unit becomes alone later during combat.

Sequence:

The ability triggers at the moment a unit is marked as attacker or defender

This happens before passive stat increases

The buff persists until end of turn once granted

Nuances:

If your lone attacker/defender is removed from combat and then you move something else in, the mask triggers for the new unit since it is marked as attacker/defender and is alone

If two units are defending together (like on Reavers Row) and one is moved back, mask does NOT trigger for the remaining unit because it was not alone when first marked as defender

If a unit is defending with a hidden unit and the hidden unit is revealed, mask does NOT trigger again even if one dies, because the trigger only happens when first determined as defender

question: Can you attempt to buff a unit that already has a buff (and can't receive more) in order to trigger 'when this unit is buffed' effects?
answer:
Ruling: You can attempt to buff a unit that already has a buff and cannot receive more, but the buff will resolve without effect and will not trigger 'when this unit is buffed' effects.

Nuances:

Card text supersedes rules text, so units like Lee Sin with specific text allowing multiple buffs can receive more than one buff despite the general reminder text

The attempt to buff resolves without effect when the buff cannot be granted, meaning triggered effects looking for successful buffs will not activate

question: If Blue Teemo triggers and the trigger is reacted to by Gust (removing Teemo), do you still get the top 5 check or does the effect fizzle?
answer:
Ruling: You still reveal the top 5 cards, but deal no damage because "here" is not defined anymore. Abilities already on the chain in Riftbound don't fizzle and resolve as much as possible by the current boardstate.

Nuances:

Effects only fizzle if countered by specific counter effects (like Defy and Wind Wall)

The ability resolves partially based on what is still valid at resolution

question: Can Zhonya's Hourglass save a unit on a different battlefield than the one it's hidden at?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Zhonya's Hourglass can save a unit on any battlefield regardless of where it is played from, because it is played to base (not to a battlefield) and does not target, so there are no battlefield restrictions on its effect.

Sequence:

Zhonya's Hourglass is played to base, even when played from hidden

Since it doesn't target, there are no battlefield restrictions on its effect

It can affect units on any battlefield

Nuances:

Gear cards cannot be played to any location except base - they do not have location choices when played

The hidden rules only limit where units can be played to (must be to that battlefield), but do not create restrictions for gear cards

When playing a card, units choose a valid location but gear do not make such choices

question: Can your opponent know what cards are in your sideboard?
answer:
Ruling: Your opponent cannot see what cards are in your sideboard. They can only count the number of cards in your sideboard (either 0 or 8 cards).

Nuances:

It is recommended to shuffle your entire sideboard into your main deck and then remove what you don't want when sideboarding, so your opponent doesn't know how many cards you swapped

You are entitled to look at your own sideboard and count your opponent's sideboard at any time

The sideboard must be distinguishable from other cards, but there are no specific rules about whether it must be visible on the playmat (it can be in your deck box)

question: How does Deflect work with spells/abilities that don't use the keyword 'choose', and can you decline to pay Deflect costs?
answer:
Ruling: Spells and abilities that select game objects are considered to target even if they don't use the word "choose", and Deflect costs must be paid for them. Players may only decline to pay Deflect costs for triggered abilities (not activated spells/abilities), in which case the triggered ability is removed from the chain without resolving.

Sequence:

When a triggered ability targets a unit with Deflect, the controller may choose whether to pay the Deflect cost

If they decline to pay, the triggered ability is removed from the chain (it does not resolve)

If they pay, the ability resolves normally

For activated spells/abilities, Deflect is a mandatory additional cost that must be paid

Nuances:

Deflect only applies at the moment a unit is chosen as a target; gaining Deflect after being targeted has no effect

For reflexive triggers (like Falling Star's damage instances), each trigger can independently have its Deflect cost declined

The original spell that creates reflexive triggers still counts as played even if the reflexive triggers are removed from the chain

To force an opponent to pay Deflect for reflexive triggers, you must give the unit Deflect before the spell creating the triggers resolves

question: When combat resolves at one battlefield, does damage get removed from units at other battlefields that were not involved in the combat?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, when combat fully resolves, all marked damage is cleared from all units at all locations, including units at battlefields that were not involved in the combat.

Sequence:

Combat occurs at one battlefield

Combat fully completes and enters the resolution step

All marked damage is cleared from all units at all locations simultaneously

Nuances:

This applies even to damage dealt earlier in the turn (such as from Hextech Ray) to units at different battlefields

This rule is not intuitive and can lead to misunderstandings about staging or baiting reactions

question: When is a lane captured during combat - before or after the opponent gets to respond when focus is passed to them?
answer:
Ruling: A lane is captured after damage assignment, which occurs only after both players have passed priority consecutively without playing cards. Units must survive through all chains (including any chains the opponent initiates after receiving focus) before the lane is captured.

Sequence:

Combat is initiated and chains resolve

Both players must pass priority consecutively

Damage assignment occurs

Lane conquest/capture happens

Nuances:

There is no limit to the number of chains that can occur

If both players pass consecutively, showdown ends

If the attacker (who has priority first) passes without playing anything and the opponent also passes, the attacker does not get another chance to play something

question: Do tokens come into play exhausted or ready?
answer:
Ruling: Tokens come into play exhausted.

Nuances:

This applies to Viktor tokens and tokens from other decks

question: Does Tryndamere's ability activate when he wins combat while Holding and equipped with Skyfall of Aerion?
answer:
Ruling: No, Tryndamere's ability does not activate when Holding because his ability triggers "when I attack" and you don't Hold after an attack (only when you attack).

Nuances:

Even if Tryndamere is attacked and deals damage, this doesn't trigger his ability because it specifically requires him to attack

The Hold keyword only applies when the unit attacks, not when it is attacked

question: Can you have two of the same champion card on the battlefield at the same time?
answer:
Ruling: You are allowed to have the same champions on the board. Champions are normal units with no restriction on duplicates.

Nuances:

Your chosen champion is special only in that they always start next to your legend and can be played from there

This rule may have been confused with Legends of Runeterra, where you cannot play a champion from hand if it is already on your board

question: When Showstopper is used on a unit and the showdown ends in a tie, does the recalled unit return to base exhausted?
answer:
Ruling: No, the unit does not return to base exhausted. Recall does not change the exhausted/ready state of a unit.

Nuances:

This applies regardless of whether the showdown ends in a tie or any other outcome

The unit maintains whatever exhausted/ready state it had when recalled

question: Does Charming Traveling Merchant activate its ability?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Traveling Merchant's ability triggers when moved by Charm or any other effect. The ability states "When I move" and will trigger regardless of how the movement occurs—whether voluntary or caused by an opponent's effect.

Sequence:

Charm is played targeting Traveling Merchant

Charm resolves, moving Traveling Merchant to a different battlefield

Traveling Merchant's triggered ability "When I move, discard 1, then draw 1" goes on the chain

The ability resolves: discard 1 card, then draw 1 card

Nuances:
