Ruling: The attacking unit gets recalled and the defending unit conquers. Since Player 1 applied contested status, they become the Attacker, meaning Player 2 gets the point.

Sequence:

Player 1 attacks empty battlefield

Player 2 moves and readies a unit (creating a non-combat showdown)

Player 1 uses Facebreaker, stunning both units

The non-combat showdown resolves first

Then combat showdown begins

Attacker is recalled, Defender conquers

Nuances:

Stun lasts until the beginning of end phase (not just for one showdown), so the stunned units remain stunned through both the non-combat and combat showdowns

The distinction between non-combat and combat showdowns matters for timing, though in this case the outcome is the same

question: Can Frostcoat Cub destroy a unit with only 2 Might (or can units with 0 or negative Might survive without damage)?
answer:
Ruling: Units only die when they have non-zero damage marked on them that is greater than or equal to their Might. A unit with 0 or even negative Might will not die until it takes at least 1 damage.

Nuances:

Units can go to negative Might under current rules

Even if a unit's Might is reduced below zero (e.g., to -1 or -2), it remains alive as long as it has no damage marked on it

question: If I conquer Monastery of Hirana with Settlement Brawler already buffed, can I choose to draw a card (spending the Settlement Brawler's buff) and then buff Settlement Brawler again with Monastery of Hirana's effect?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can draw a card by spending Settlement Brawler's existing buff and then buff it again with Monastery of Hirana's effect.

Sequence:

Both "when you conquer" triggers happen simultaneously

You choose the order to resolve them

You can resolve Settlement Brawler's draw effect first (spending its buff), then resolve Monastery of Hirana's effect to buff Settlement Brawler again

question: Are units continuously checked for Attacker/Defender status during a Showdown, and how does this work for units like Blue Teemo and Yellow Shen that enter during combat?
answer:
Ruling: Units are continuously checked for Attacker/Defender status during a Showdown as part of the Clean-up check. When a unit like Blue Teemo is revealed as a REACTION during an open chain, its Defender trigger goes on top of the current chain.

Sequence:

Units entering during a Showdown are checked for Attacker/Defender status during Clean-up

If a unit is revealed as a REACTION while a chain is open, its trigger goes on top of the existing chain

The trigger does not become pending in this scenario

Nuances:

Pending status is primarily relevant when something is played while something else resolves (e.g., cards played as part of Promising Future's resolution)

Even pending effects finalize onto the chain on top of any other potential effects already there

question: Can you score points from the same battlefield multiple times in one turn, and what counts as 'conquering' a battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: You can only score a battlefield once per turn, even if you take control of it multiple times during that turn. However, you can score once per battlefield per turn, meaning you can hold your own battlefield for 1 point and conquer your opponent's battlefield for another point in the same turn.

Sequence:

When you first successfully attack a battlefield in a turn, you conquer it and score it

Any subsequent times you take control of that same battlefield in the same turn do not grant additional points

You can still score other battlefields that same turn

Nuances:

Taking control of a battlefield multiple times only counts as "conquering" once (the first time you get a point from it)

If you are at 7 points and successfully attack a battlefield, you have still "conquered" and "scored" it even though you don't receive a point due to the win condition

question: When Hostile Takeover steals Rek'sai after her 'When I Attack' ability has triggered but before it resolves, who controls the ability?
answer:
Ruling: When Rek'sai's 'When I Attack' ability triggers and goes on the chain, the controller of that ability is locked as whoever controlled Rek'sai at the time it triggered. If Hostile Takeover steals Rek'sai after the ability has triggered but before it resolves, the original controller (the attacker) still controls and resolves the ability.

Sequence:

Rek'sai attacks and her 'When I Attack' ability triggers

The ability goes on the chain with the current controller locked in

Hostile Takeover is played in reaction, stealing Rek'sai

When Rek'sai's ability resolves, it is still controlled by the original owner who triggered it

question: Can a player play a Reaction speed card (like Shen) during a Showdown to defend against an attack, even though the Reaction isn't responding to a specific spell or ability?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Reaction speed cards can be played during a Showdown. Whenever you can play an Action speed card, you can also play a Reaction speed card.

Sequence:

When contesting an empty battlefield or a battlefield controlled by the opponent, a Showdown occurs

During a Showdown, players can play Action cards while there are no effects on the chain waiting to resolve

Since Reaction cards have all the advantages of Action cards, they can also be played during this window

The defender could play Shen as a reaction to the attack, forcing the attack to hit Shen first

Nuances:

Action speed has all the advantages of base speed

Reaction speed has all the advantages of Action speed and base speed

Whenever you can play base speed cards, you can play Action or Reaction speed cards

question: If I kill my own Phoenix with a spell, can I return it with its ability?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Phoenix can return itself with its ability even if you kill it with your own spell.

Nuances:

This interaction was explicitly covered in the FAQ

question: If Lucian is moved to a battlefield with Relentless Pursuit (already ready), can he use his ready ability when he conquers a second battlefield later that turn?
answer:
Ruling: Lucian's printed ready ability can only be used the first time he conquers each turn. You must use it when it triggers and cannot save it for a later conquest.

Sequence:

When Lucian enters play exhausted, play Relentless Pursuit to move him to battlefield 1

He conquers and triggers both his printed ready ability and Pursuit's return-to-base ability

Resolve Pursuit's ability first to move him back to base

Resolve his printed ability to ready himself

Use a standard move action to move him to battlefield 2

He conquers again and triggers Pursuit's return-to-base ability (but not his printed ready ability)

Resolve Pursuit's ability to return him to base

Nuances:

Moves granted by Relentless Pursuit do not exhaust the unit

Lucian's ready ability only triggers the first time he conquers each turn, not on subsequent conquests

When multiple "when I conquer" abilities trigger simultaneously, you can order them however you want

Relentless Pursuit's return-to-base ability lasts the entire turn and applies to all conquests that turn

question: What happens when Volibear Furious starts a combat at a location with one unit with less than 5 might and a Hidden Blade hidden there that kills him?
answer:
Ruling: If Hidden Blade resolves and kills Volibear Furious, his ability can no longer establish where "here" is and he won't deal the damage from his ability.

Sequence:

Volibear Furious starts combat at the location

Hidden Blade is played and resolves

Volibear dies

Volibear's damage ability fails to resolve because "here" is no longer defined

question: If the opponent has a 4 Might unit on Reavers Row and I attack with a 4 Might unit, I have priority first. If I pass priority and my opponent chooses to retreat instead of using Reavers, can I still use Cleave after they retreat, or is it too late?
answer:
Ruling: Reavers Row goes onto the initial chain in combat. When it resolves, the defender decides whether to retreat. After they decide (whether they retreat or not), the rest of the showdown continues and you can use Cleave then.

Sequence:

Reavers Row triggers and goes onto the initial chain in combat

When Reavers Row resolves, the defender decides whether to retreat

After the retreat decision is made, the showdown continues

You can use Cleave during the continued showdown

Nuances:

You cannot use Cleave before the battlefield (Reavers Row) triggers during the showdown

question: When a unit with Cleave moves to a battlefield, is the Assault bonus a passive effect or a trigger ability that the opponent can react to? Similarly, can an opponent react to Shield when a unit with Shield moves to their battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Assault and Shield are passive abilities, not triggers. When a unit with Cleave moves to a battlefield, it instantly gains the Assault might bonus without creating a reaction window.

Sequence:

If the unit has no move triggers: The unit moves to the battlefield and instantly gains the Assault bonus with no opportunity to respond

If the unit has move triggers: The unit arrives at the battlefield, the move trigger goes on the chain (allowing responses), and the Assault bonus applies only after that chain fully resolves

Nuances:

Units with move triggers are considered at the battlefield when their move trigger is on the chain, but combat has not yet begun

If a unit with Cleave and a move trigger initiates combat, opponents can respond to the move trigger (e.g., with Gust) before the Assault bonus applies and combat begins

If combat is already ongoing at the battlefield and the unit joins as the attacker, it gets the Assault bonus before the move trigger chain fully resolves

There is no "move limbo" - permanents are either at their Origin before moving or their Destination after moving

question: How does a hidden Tideturner chain resolve, and does it go onto the chain as a champion permanent?
answer:
Ruling: Permanents (including champions like Tideturner) do create and go on chains, but upon finalizing they immediately resolve without any reactions possible.

Sequence:

Tideturner is played and goes on the chain

Upon finalizing, Tideturner resolves immediately without reactions

Tideturner's "When you play me" trigger happens immediately after the permanent resolves

This trigger creates a new chain (or adds to an existing one)

You declare a unit at a different location than Tideturner's

Reactions can now be played to this trigger

When the trigger resolves, both the target and Tideturner are moved simultaneously

Nuances:

The permanent itself resolves without reactions, but its triggered ability can be reacted to

Tideturner has a card errata requiring the target to be at a different location than Tideturner's location

question: Can you float mana during your opponent's turn by tapping runes in response to an opponent's action?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can float mana during your opponent's turn by tapping runes in response to actions like an opponent attempting to kill your attacker.

Nuances:

Currently runes don't have the reaction keyword, but this is acknowledged as something that will be fixed in future rules

The ability to tap runes at reaction speed is necessary to pay for reaction-speed spells during your own turn as well

Energy and power pools are emptied at the end of each turn and at the end of each beginning step

question: For Hextech Ray, do you target when you play it or when it resolves?
answer:
Ruling: You declare the target when you play Hextech Ray from your hand, but the target is rechecked for validity before the card resolves.

Sequence:

Play Hextech Ray from hand and declare target

Pass priority

Before resolution, recheck if target is still valid

If target is still valid (e.g., still on battlefield), resolve the effect

Nuances:

If the target is moved from battlefield to base before resolution, they do not take damage

This is different from Falling Star, which is a reflective trigger where you play the card without targets, pass priority, and then declare targets as reflective triggers on the stack when it resolves

question: Can you Gust your own 3 might Ravenbloom Student?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can successfully Gust your own 3 might Ravenbloom Student. The spell will return it to your hand before the Student's "when you play a spell" trigger can activate and increase its might to 4.

Sequence:

You cast Gust targeting your 3-might Ravenbloom Student

Gust fully resolves and returns the Student to your hand

Only after Gust finishes resolving is it considered "played"

Ravenbloom Student's trigger would activate, but the Student is already in your hand, not on the battlefield

Gust successfully returns the Student to your hand

Nuances:

"When you play" triggers only activate after a card finishes resolving, not when it is cast or finalized

Since the Student is removed from the battlefield as part of Gust's resolution, it cannot receive the +1 might buff from its own trigger

Target legality is checked both when the spell is cast and when it resolves, but in this case the Student is removed before it can become 4 might

question: At what point is something considered slow play and can a judge give a time extension for it?
answer:
Ruling: There is no hard and fast rule for what constitutes slow play. If you feel your opponent is playing too slowly, you can call a judge to watch for it, or ask your opponent nicely to keep a good pace.

Nuances:

Most players will play faster if asked nicely in the first instance

question: Does Ravenbloom Student get +1 Might before an opponent can play a reaction spell in response to an action spell?
answer:
Ruling: No, Ravenbloom Student does not get the +1 Might before your opponent can play a reaction spell. Effects that trigger from playing a card require that card to resolve fully first.

Sequence:

Action spell is played and goes on the chain

Opponent has opportunity to play reaction spells while the action spell is unresolved

Action spell resolves

Ravenbloom Student's ability triggers and grants +1 Might

Nuances:

If the action spell gets countered, it does not count as resolved and Ravenbloom Student will not trigger

question: If I use Possession on a Watcher that was played this turn, whose units get -3 Might?
answer:
Ruling: When you take control of a Watcher with Possession, your units (the new controller's units) will get -3 Might to a minimum of 1 Might.

Sequence:

Watcher is played and its trigger is created

The trigger locks in what "enemy" units are at the time it's created (based on original owner)

Possession is played, taking control of the Watcher

The trigger resolves, affecting what were "enemy" units when the trigger was created (now your units)

Nuances:

Taking control of a unit is different from playing it

Control of the game object that created a trigger only matters when the trigger is being created, not when it resolves

Once a trigger goes on the chain, its ownership is already determined

question: Can a unit have multiple equipment?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, a unit can have multiple equipment.

Nuances:

This was confirmed by Riot staff when equipment was first revealed, though it is not explicitly stated in the written rules.

question: If someone plays Time Warp, does the player whose turn would have been next still get holding points?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not get holding points. Time Warp inserts an extra turn for the caster after their current turn, so you never enter your Beginning Phase to score holding points.

Sequence:

The Time Warp caster finishes their current turn

The Time Warp caster takes an additional turn

Then the next player's turn occurs

Nuances:

You only score holding points during your Beginning Phase, so if you don't take a turn, you don't score points from holding

question: When a unit with a Conquer ability conquers a site that also has a Conquer trigger, what order do the abilities resolve in?
answer:
Ruling: When multiple Conquer abilities trigger simultaneously (from both the conquering unit and the conquered site), you can choose the order in which they resolve.

Nuances:

This applies to scenarios like Sett conquering Monastery of Hirana (you can choose whether to use Sett's buff for the Monastery's draw effect first, or trigger Sett's ability first to get the buff)

This also applies to scenarios like Qiyana conquering Sigil of the Storm (you can choose whether Sigil's effect or Qiyana's channeling happens first)

This ruling resolves potential contradictions between multiple conquer triggers

question: If Soulgorger's on-play effect brings out a Magma Wurm, does Soulgorger enter the battlefield ready or exhausted?
answer:
Ruling: Soulgorger enters exhausted. The "when I'm played" effect triggers after Soulgorger is already on the battlefield exhausted, so Magma Wurm enters after Soulgorger is already in play.

Sequence:

Soulgorger is played and enters the battlefield exhausted

Soulgorger's "when I'm played" effect triggers

Magma Wurm enters the battlefield from the effect

Nuances:

"When I'm played" effects trigger when a unit touches the table anywhere, not just when played to the battlefield

question: If you use Zenith Blade to move a unit with a 'when attacking' trigger into an already existing showdown, does the when attacking trigger activate?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the when attacking trigger activates, but only if you are the attacker in the showdown. If you are the defender, the when attacking trigger does not activate.

Sequence:

Determine whether you are the attacker or defender in the existing showdown

If you are the attacker: the unit's when attacking trigger activates when moved into the showdown

If you are the defender: the when attacking trigger does not activate

Nuances:

If your opponent started the showdown trying to conquer an open battlefield, you would be the defender and don't get the trigger

If you started the showdown in any way and then move a unit with Zenith Blade, you will get the trigger

This ruling is based on developer statements but may not be fully supported by current written rules (RAI vs RAW situation)

question: Can Sett's ability be activated outside of my turn, and does he ready himself at the start of my turn or only after conquering?
answer:
Ruling: Sett's ability can be activated on any turn, not just your own. Sett readies himself both at the start of your turn and after conquering.

Sequence:

Sett readies at the start of your turn

Sett readies after conquering

question: Can you use Mystic Reversal on Windwall and change Windwall's target to Mystic Reversal itself to make Windwall fizzle?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot target Mystic Reversal with Windwall. Mystic Reversal will have already resolved and left the chain by the time you choose new targets for Windwall.

Sequence:

Mystic Reversal resolves and takes control of Windwall

As part of Mystic Reversal's resolution, you may choose new targets for Windwall

After following all instructions (including choosing new targets), Mystic Reversal goes to the trash

Mystic Reversal is no longer on the chain when target selection occurs

You must choose a legal target that exists on the chain (Windwall was already targeting something)

Nuances:

You could redirect Windwall if there's another effect on the chain (e.g., if you played Discipline, then Mystic Reversal, you could target either the original spell or Discipline)

The "may choose new targets" wording is important - it's optional

There is ongoing debate about whether choosing new targets requires re-finalizing the spell and what implications this has for additional costs like deflect, but this doesn't change the core answer

question: If Hidden Blade kills the Recruit in response to Falling Star being played, does Falling Star fizzle or must Kaisa target her own 3 Might unit?
answer:
Ruling: Falling Star must target Kaisa's own unit. The spell does not fizzle (spells always resolve in Riftbound), and because Falling Star uses a reflexive trigger that chooses targets after the spell resolves, the Recruit is already dead when targets must be selected.

Sequence:

Falling Star is played

Hidden Blade is played in response, killing the Recruit

Hidden Blade resolves

Falling Star resolves and creates a reflexive trigger

The reflexive trigger chooses targets (at this point the Recruit is dead)

Kaisa must select her own 3 Might unit as the target

Nuances:

This interaction is specific to spells with reflexive triggers like Falling Star and Itachian Rain that choose targets after the spell resolves

Other spells that deal damage directly choose targets when the spell is played and would have no effect if the target is killed in response

question: If you play Surprise Defense at Fortified Position, do you get the battlefield trigger the first time you become a defender there?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not get the trigger. The battlefield needs a player to control it to have a valid understanding of "you" in its text, so Surprise Defense does not trigger battlefield abilities that reference "you."

Nuances:

This represents a change from previous rules where Reaver's Row did work with Surprise Defense

Battlefields with "you hold" and "you conquer" text are not drastically changed by the new rules clarification

question: Can units be played directly to battlefields you control, or only to your base?
answer:
Ruling: Units can be played to either your base or a battlefield you control.

Nuances:

The claim that Chinese rules differ on this point is incorrect; there is one set of rules for all regions.

question: Does Yasuo's ability trigger when attacking only, or when defending too?
answer: Ruling: Yasuo's ability only triggers when he attacks, not when defending.

question: Can Caitlyn's ability only be used during your turn when she is ready at a battlefield and the opponent has a unit on the other battlefield, with no showdown or chain happening?
answer:
Ruling: Caitlyn's ability can only be used on your turn when she is ready at a battlefield, the opponent has a unit on the other battlefield, and no showdown or chain is happening.

Nuances:

All conditions must be met simultaneously: it must be your turn, Caitlyn must be ready at a battlefield, an opponent unit must be at the other battlefield, and no showdown or chain can be in progress.

question: Does Heimerdinger trigger all exhaust abilities of your cards simultaneously when exhausted, or does he gain those abilities and you choose which one to activate?
answer:
Ruling: Heimerdinger does not trigger all exhaust abilities at once. He gains all exhaust abilities from your cards, and you must choose which one to activate when you exhaust him.

Nuances:

Heimerdinger copies the abilities themselves, not their effects

You still need to pay any additional costs (like energy or power) required by the chosen ability

Only one ability can be activated per exhaustion

question: If a unit has damage marked on it from a spell, and then Watcher reduces its Might, does the unit die?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the unit dies. When damage marked on a unit is greater than or equal to its Might, it dies. Might values can change, and if they decrease while damage is marked, it can kill the unit.

Sequence:

A 4 Might unit has 3 damage marked on it from a spell

Watcher is played, reducing the unit's Might to 1

The unit now has 3 damage marked and 1 Might

Since damage (3) >= Might (1), the unit dies

Nuances:

There is no "health" stat in Riftbound; damage and Might are separate values

Damage marked on a unit does not reduce its Might value

A unit dies when damage marked equals or exceeds its current Might, regardless of how the Might changed

question: When Leona Zealot is in play and reduces a stunned unit's might by 8, does her effect snapshot when the stun occurs, or does it continuously apply as buffs are added to the stunned unit?
answer:
Ruling: Leona Zealot's might reduction is a passive ability that continuously applies, not a snapshot effect. Stunned units always have -8 might while Leona's conditions are met, and this reduction is recalculated whenever the unit's might changes.

Sequence:

Start with the unit's base might

Add all might increases (buffs, auras, etc.)

Subtract Leona's -8 (if the unit is stunned and conditions are met)

Apply minimum of 1 might

Nuances:

The key difference is that Leona says stunned units "have" -8 might (passive, continuous) rather than "give" -8 might (snapshot, one-time)

"If" signifies a passive ability that continuously applies

"When/At" signifies a triggered ability that would snapshot

Passive abilities do not create chains and happen automatically/persistently if conditions continue to be met

Even if a unit gains additional might buffs after being stunned, Leona's -8 continues to apply to the total calculation

question: If my opponent reveals Tideturner and I use Gust on it in response, does the swap effect fizzle?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, using Gust on Tideturner (or the unit it targets) in response will cause the swap effect to fail. The ability will resolve but do nothing.

Sequence:

Opponent reveals Tideturner and its ability goes on the chain, selecting a target unit

You play Gust in response, returning either Tideturner or the targeted unit to hand

Gust resolves, removing the unit from the board

Tideturner's ability attempts to resolve but cannot evaluate the referential information ("my location" for Tideturner's position, or "its location" for the target's position)

No swap occurs; the ability resolves to no effect

Nuances:

Triggers generally don't care where their source goes after being placed on the chain, but Tideturner specifically fails because it contains referential information ("my location", "original location", "their location") that cannot be evaluated when the referenced unit is no longer on the board

If a unit changes zones to or from a non-board zone and returns, it's treated as a different object and is no longer a legal target

"Original location" refers to where Tideturner was when the play effect began resolving, and this information cannot be defined if Tideturner has left the board

question: If an opponent attacks a battlefield I control, do I still have control of it, and can I use abilities like Ornn's Forge when defending?
answer:
Ruling: When an opponent attacks a battlefield you control, you retain control of it while it is simultaneously in a contested state. You can use abilities that require control of the battlefield (like Ornn's Forge) when defending.

Nuances:

A battlefield can be both controlled by a player and in a contested state at the same time

question: If I tap 3 runes but don't use them, does the floating energy pass on to my enemy's turn or does it disappear after my turn ends?
answer:
Ruling: Unspent Energy/Power disappears after each Draw Step and at the End of each turn (including your opponent's turn and draw phase).

Nuances:

Energy disappears at multiple points: after each Draw Step, at the end of your turn, at the end of your opponent's turn, and at the end of your opponent's draw phase

question: If a unit is moved out of a showdown during the showdown, does combat damage still go through and trigger Zhonya's save ability, or does combat fizzle?
answer:
Ruling: The showdown continues through all steps and phases, but a unit moved out of the showdown location will not be involved in the damage step. It will not deal or be dealt combat damage since it is no longer at the same location.

Sequence:

The showdown continues through all steps and phases

The moved unit is not involved in the damage step

No combat damage is dealt to or by the moved unit

Nuances:

Zhonya's save ability would not trigger because the unit does not take combat damage when moved out of the showdown location

question: If I use Charm to move an enemy unit to a battlefield I control, am I the attacker or defender?
answer:
Ruling: You are the defender. The attacker is determined by which player controls the units that applied the contested status to the battlefield, not by who played the spell that moved the units.

Nuances:

The current rules could be read as "the player who played the spell is the attacker," but this interpretation is incorrect

A future Comprehensive Rules update will clarify that the attacker is the controller of the units that applied contested status

If you control a battlefield and use Charm to bring an enemy unit there, the enemy unit applies the contested status, making your opponent the attacker and you the defender

question: Can Zhonya's Hourglass be played hidden in your base, or does it have to be played at a battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot play Hidden cards in your base. Zhonya's Hourglass must be played Hidden in a battlefield you control, or it can be played in your base by paying its cost normally (not Hidden).

Nuances:

If Zhonya's is Hidden in a battlefield, it only applies to that battlefield when you react with it

If Zhonya's is in your base (played normally), it will prevent the death of the next friendly unit killed no matter what battlefield

question: Is there another round of priority at the end of a turn, allowing a player to cast a meditation before the turn passes?
answer: Ruling: No, there is no additional priority round at the end of a turn. You cannot cast a meditation after your opponent ends their turn but before your turn begins.

question: If I have two Vi's on the board, can they both benefit from each card recycled?
answer:
Ruling: No, both Vi's cannot benefit from each card recycled.

Nuances:

Only one Vi will trigger per recycled card

question: When Blitzcrank pulls an opponent's unit to my battlefield, who is the attacker and who is the defender?
answer:
Ruling: When Blitzcrank pulls an opponent's unit to your battlefield, the pulled unit's controller becomes the attacker and you become the defender.

Sequence:

Blitzcrank enters your battlefield (which you already control)

Blitzcrank's "When you play me" trigger activates

The trigger moves an opponent's unit to your battlefield

The pulled enemy unit enters a battlefield controlled by a different player, applying contested status

The pulled unit's controller becomes the attacker; you become the defender

Combat stages and resolves

Nuances:

The attacker is determined by who applied contested status to the battlefield

Since Blitzcrank was played to a battlefield you already control, it does not apply contested

The enemy unit being moved to your battlefield is what applies contested status, making its controller the attacker

question: Can you score a point on your opponent's turn with a surprise defense?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can score a point on your opponent's turn with a surprise defense. The defender can score and conquer at the end of combat as long as they did not control the battlefield before combat began.

Sequence:

The attacker applies contested status to the battlefield

Combat occurs

If the defender wins and did not control the battlefield before combat began, the defender scores instead of the attacker

Nuances:

The attacker is the one who applied contested status, but they are not necessarily the one who scores at the end of combat

The defender can only score if they did not control the battlefield before combat began

question: When multiple units die at the same time while Zhonya's Hourglass is in play, who chooses which unit is recalled?
answer: Ruling: The controller of the Hourglass chooses which unit is recalled when multiple units die simultaneously.

question: Does Taric grant Fiora the Mighty keyword when they are both at a battlefield, making her 6 might instead of 5?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Fiora becomes 6 might while defending with Taric at the battlefield. Taric grants her the Shield keyword, which increases her might to 5, making her Mighty, and then she gains +1 might from being Mighty.

Sequence:

Taric grants Fiora the Shield keyword

The Arithmetic layer applies, seeing Shield and increasing Fiora to 5 might

At 5 might, Fiora becomes Mighty

The layers loop again and she gains +1 might from being Mighty, reaching 6 total

Nuances:

If Taric leaves at any point during the showdown, Fiora drops to 4 might (assuming no other might alterations)

question: When the last unit of a showdown dies, are you still in the showdown? Can the other player cast an action afterwards?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you are still in the showdown when the last unit dies. The other player can cast an action afterwards.

Sequence:

An action is cast that kills the last unit

The showdown continues

The other player can cast an action in response

The showdown only ends when all players have passed focus

question: When Tideturner's effect is on the chain and Tideturner is bounced to hand by Gust before the effect resolves, does Tideturner's movement effect still work?
answer:
Ruling: Tideturner will stay in hand and the other friendly unit won't move either. Nothing will happen when the effect resolves.

Sequence:

Tideturner is played and its effect is added to the chain

Opponent responds with Gust, bouncing Tideturner to hand

Gust resolves

Tideturner's effect tries to resolve, but moves only occur between locations on the board

Tideturner's "original location" is now the hand (resolved during resolution)

Since hand is not a board location, neither Tideturner nor the other unit moves

Nuances:

Hand is referred to as a "location" (lowercase) in rules text, but is not a "Location" (capital L) on the board

Moves are only between locations on the board, not to/from hand

question: Can you play multiple non-Action/non-Reaction spell cards during your turn outside of showdowns to deal enough damage to kill a single unit (e.g., two 3-damage spells to kill a 5-might unit)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play multiple spell cards during your turn outside of showdowns. Damage remains marked on units until the end of any combat or the end of turn, so you can play consecutive spells to accumulate enough damage to kill a unit.

Sequence:

Play the first spell in a chain, it resolves and marks damage on the target

Play the second spell in a new consecutive chain, it resolves and marks additional damage

The accumulated damage remains until end of combat or end of turn

Nuances:

Cards without Action or Reaction timing can only be played on your turn, not during showdowns

Multiple cards must be played in consecutive chains, not in the same chain

Damage is cleared at the end of any combat (only if units from both sides are involved) or at end of turn

Moving to an open battlefield does not heal units

question: Does Traveling Merchant draw a card if you have no cards in hand to discard?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Traveling Merchant draws a card even if you have no cards in hand to discard.

Nuances:

If the card said "discard 1 to draw 1" (with "to") or "Discard 1. If you do..." then you would NOT be able to draw with an empty hand

The current wording allows each part to resolve as much as possible independently

question: When Viktor and multiple non-recruits would die simultaneously (e.g., from an AOE spell or battlefield attack), does Viktor get to choose the order of deaths to trigger his ability, or does the attacker choose?
answer:
Ruling: Viktor does not trigger his ability when he dies alongside other non-recruits because damage is dealt simultaneously and Viktor must see another non-recruit die to spawn a recruit at its base. Since Viktor dies at the same time, he doesn't see the other deaths occur.

Sequence:

Damage is assigned in order

Damage is dealt simultaneously to all targets

Cleanup cannot happen until the effect resolves fully

Nuances:

Viktor's ability requires him to survive to witness another non-recruit's death

The order of damage assignment doesn't matter for Viktor's trigger since all deaths are simultaneous

question: How does time work in Riftbound, how many minutes are allowed for a best of 3, and who wins when time expires?
answer:
Ruling: Time limits are tournament dependent. When time expires, players complete 5 extra turns, then the player with the most points wins. If points are tied, the game is a tie.

Sequence:

Time expires (duration is tournament dependent)

Players take 5 extra turns

Player with most points wins

If points are tied, game is a tie

question: Do hidden units get played exhausted when you react with them from hidden?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, hidden units enter play exhausted when you react with them from hidden.

Nuances:

All units enter play exhausted, including tokens, unless otherwise stated

question: Can activated abilities be used during combat/showdown if the state is open and it's your turn?
answer:
Ruling: During a showdown, only Action and Reaction abilities can be activated. Regular activated abilities (without Action or Reaction keywords) cannot be used during combat/showdown, regardless of whether the state is open or it's your turn.

Nuances:

"Open state" and "showdown open" are different things - activated abilities require a neutral open state, not just any open state

Reaction abilities can be activated during closed states as an exception via the Golden Rule

The rules for activated abilities don't change based on what card type (unit, gear, or legend) has the ability - all follow the same restrictions

question: How does Volibear Imposing's ability trigger? Specifically: (1) Does Volibear need to be on a battlefield to trigger? (2) Does it trigger when you Charm an opponent's unit, or when an opponent Charms your unit?
answer:
Ruling: Volibear triggers when he is on a battlefield AND one or more units controlled by an opponent move to any other battlefield. "Opponent" refers to enemy units (units controlled by your opponent), not the player issuing the move command.

Sequence:

Volibear must be on a battlefield (not in base)

When enemy unit(s) move to a different battlefield than Volibear's, the ability triggers

If multiple enemy units move simultaneously, draw only once

If multiple enemy units move one at a time, draw for each move

Nuances:

Charming an opponent's unit to move it DOES trigger Volibear (you are moving an enemy unit)

An opponent Charming your unit to move it does NOT trigger Volibear (they are moving a friendly unit, not an enemy unit)

The trigger looks at which units are moving (enemy vs friendly), not who is issuing the move command

question: Can you target units with 5 or more Might with Fox Fire?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot target units with 5 or more Might with Fox Fire. All targeted units must be valid targets (total Might ≤4) at the time of activation, and you need at least one valid target to play the spell.

Nuances:

You cannot activate Fox Fire if your opponent controls no units with 4 Might or less

You cannot mix valid and invalid targets (e.g., a 1 Might unit and a 5 Might unit together)

All original targets must have a combined total Might of 4 or less when the spell is put on the chain

question: Is it allowed to organize unofficial online tournaments on simulator platforms, or can you be sanctioned for doing so?
answer:
Ruling: Unofficial online tournaments on simulator platforms are allowed and have been run without issue.

Nuances:

Riftlab has been running tournaments on Tabletop Simulator (TTS) for months without any sanctions or problems.

question: When revealing a unit from hidden (like Teemo Strategist), does it open up a chain that can be reacted to before the unit resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Units played from hidden do enter the chain but immediately resolve without passing priority to opponents. Opponents cannot react to the unit itself being played, but can react to any triggered abilities the unit creates when it enters play.

Sequence:

Unit enters the chain as a pending item

Unit immediately leaves the chain and becomes a game object (resolves)

Priority does not pass after the unit resolves

If the unit has a triggered ability (like Teemo), that ability goes on the chain and passes priority for opponents to react

Nuances:

Units without triggered abilities give no opportunity for opponent interaction

You need priority to react, which requires reaching the Execute step, but this is skipped for units

Only triggered or activated abilities from the unit will pass priority to opponents

question: Does Blitzcrank remember his location when his effect activates, or is 'here' re-evaluated at resolution?
answer:
Ruling: 'Here' is always evaluated at resolution, not when the effect is created or put on the chain.

Sequence:

Blitzcrank's ability triggers and goes on the chain

When the ability resolves, 'here' refers to Blitzcrank's current location at that moment

If Blitzcrank has been moved or killed, the location reference changes accordingly

Nuances:

If Blitzcrank is killed before resolution, there is no 'here' and the ability resolves without effect (the unit doesn't move)

If Blitzcrank is moved to a different battlefield, the pulled unit moves to that new battlefield

If Blitzcrank is moved to base, the pulled unit would recall (since units can't be moved to an opponent's base)

Blitzcrank cannot target a unit already at the same battlefield, but if moved to the target's battlefield during resolution, nothing happens (the unit doesn't move because it can't move to where it already is)

CR 437.2.b only applies to the specific case where a unit tries to enter a battlefield with combat between two other players, causing it to go to base instead

question: For Wraith of Echoes, do you draw a card if it dies itself, or if it dies at the same time as another unit?
answer:
Ruling: You do not draw a card if Wraith of Echoes dies itself, and you also do not draw a card if it dies at the same time as another unit.

Nuances:

This is covered in the rules for triggering abilities and the FAQ

question: Does Fiora become Mighty when she receives a buff that brings her to 5 might, or does she need to be played with a card like En Garde to reach 5 might?
answer:
Ruling: A buff that brings Fiora to 5 might makes her Mighty.

Nuances:

The question arose due to concerns about layers, but buffs applied to Fiora count toward making her Mighty when they bring her to the 5 might threshold.

question: What is the proper remedy when a player accidentally looks at or flips their opponent's hidden card?
answer:
Ruling: The opponent whose hidden card was revealed may choose to either leave it as-is (with the opponent now knowing what it is) or re-randomize it by replacing it with another random hidden card from their hand if available.

Sequence:

If choosing to re-randomize: Take the revealed hidden card back to hand

Select another hidden card from hand randomly (if available)

Place the new hidden card face-down in the same position

The original card returns to hand

Nuances:

If the affected player has no other cards in hand, they can only choose to leave the hidden card as-is or shuffle it back into their deck (losing the card entirely)

The recycled rune used to play the hidden card remains recycled regardless of remedy chosen

If a player accidentally reveals their own hidden card, no remedy is applied - the information simply becomes known

The interpretation of "re-randomize with original randomized source" for hidden cards is unclear in the rules and may need official clarification

question: When Fizz, Trickster plays a spell like Frigid Touch, can you use Repeat for free even if the Repeat cost would make the total exceed 3 energy?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot use Repeat for free. Fizz's ability to ignore costs applies only to the base cost of the spell, not to optional additional costs like Repeat. You must pay the full Repeat cost separately.

Sequence:

Fizz allows you to play a spell with base cost 3 or less, ignoring that base cost

If you choose to pay the Repeat cost, you must pay it in full

For example: Frigid Touch can be played for 0 energy (base cost ignored), but Repeat still costs 2 energy if you choose to use it

Nuances:

When an effect refers to "cost," it refers to the base cost only, not optional additional costs

Fizz's cost limit of 3 or less applies only to the base cost, not to additional costs like Repeat

question: Does the Aurora trigger resolve before end-of-turn damage cleanup/healing?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Aurora triggers before units heal at end of turn. This means you can use a spell to damage a unit at a field, then potentially find a Deadbloom via Aurora to finish it off before it heals.

Sequence:

Aurora trigger resolves

Units heal after Aurora resolves

Nuances:

This interaction allows for strategic plays where partial damage can be converted into kills through Aurora discoveries before healing occurs

question: Can Azir - Ascendant's ability be activated while he is exhausted, and how does the ability work when switching positions with a unit?
answer:
Ruling: Azir's ability can be activated while he is exhausted because exhausting is not a cost for his ability - only 1 green power is required. You must play Azir to the field before you can activate his ability.

Sequence:

Play Azir from champion zone to the field

On a later turn, when an opponent showdowns on your battlefield with a friendly unit guarding, you can recycle a rune to activate Azir's ability and switch positions

Nuances:

Unlike exhaust abilities where exhausting is a cost to activate, Azir's ability only requires paying 1 green power, so exhausted status does not prevent activation

Azir must be on the field (not in champion zone) before his ability can be used

question: If I play a gold token as my first card, will Darius Trifarian's ability trigger as a +2 if he is played then?
answer:
Ruling: No, Darius Trifarian's ability will not trigger if he is played after a gold token. Tokens are not cards, so playing a token does not count toward the "second card this turn" condition.

Nuances:

Tokens do not count as cards for any game effects that reference "cards"

Darius must be the second actual card played in a turn to trigger his ability, not the second thing played

question: Can I win the game by conquering two battlefields for the last point even if I leave one of the two battlefields empty?
answer:
Ruling: You do not need to have units in both battlefields when you get the last point via conquering. You can leave a battlefield empty and still win the game.

Nuances:

You can only score each battlefield once per turn

This ruling applies specifically to winning via the last point through conquest

question: What happens when an attacker attacks a stunned unit with more power than the attacker's power?
answer:
Ruling: If the attacker cannot kill the stunned defender and the attacker is still alive after combat, the attacker returns to base. The defender remains in place.

Nuances:

This interaction is similar to how Kayn works: if any defending unit remains after combat, the attacker bounces to base

The defender does not move because they were not killed

question: Can reactions be played during a showdown, and what is the difference between when you can play actions versus reactions?
answer:
Ruling: Reactions can be played anytime you have priority during a showdown, whether the chain is empty or not. Actions can only be played during a showdown when the chain is empty.

Sequence:

When you have priority, you can play as many reactions as you want

When you pass priority and nobody reacts, you don't get priority again until the first item on the chain resolves

Focus passes automatically once a chain is fully resolved during a showdown

The player with focus can play an action to start a chain, then immediately follow up with reactions without passing priority

Nuances:

You cannot play action spells to an ongoing chain, only to open a chain

You cannot follow up an action with another action even if priority passes back to you during the same chain

Gaining focus also gives you priority

Passing priority during a chain doesn't pass focus; focus only passes once a chain where you had focus is emptied or when you decide to not start a chain

question: Does Deathknell trigger before or after Conquer resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Deathknell happens before Conquer resolves.

Nuances:

The FAQ changed timing for healing effects, but other timing (like Deathknell) is assumed to remain the same until further notice

This means the Kog'maw interaction (killing a 5 might unit) no longer works as it did previously

question: Can you target units on other battlefields with spells while in a showdown?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can target units on any battlefield with spells during a showdown, unless the card specifies otherwise.

Nuances:

Hidden cards are an exception - their on reveal effects are limited to the battlefield they are on

question: If I am turn player and I Charm an enemy unit onto a battlefield I control, who is designated attacker and defender? If I Charm them and I lose, do they gain a point for conquering?
answer:
Ruling: The unit that contests the battlefield becomes the attacker, regardless of how they got there. If you lose the showdown and their unit remains, the opponent scores a point for conquering.

Nuances:

Control of the battlefield determines who is defending, but attacker/defender status is determined by who contested the battlefield first, not who controls it

If you reconquer that same battlefield later in the same turn, you will not score another point from it since you already scored from either holding or previously conquering it that turn

It is possible for units to be defenders at battlefields they don't control, as long as they're present with another player's units that contested it first

Control can be held or lost during a contest, but cannot be gained until the end of a showdown

Attackers and defenders do not change within a showdown, only at cleanup

question: Can a player activate a hidden Tideturner from Battlefield A to swap units when combat is happening on Battlefield B?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can activate hidden cards regardless of where the showdown is happening. Tideturner specifically can target units on another battlefield because the card explicitly says it can.

Nuances:

Hidden cards can normally only target units at their own battlefield unless they explicitly state otherwise

Tideturner is one of the rare cases where a hidden card can target outside its battlefield because the card text allows it

question: When a unit is saved from death by Zhonya's or Guardian Angel, do other attached equipment remain attached to the unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, all equipment stays attached because the unit never died - it was just recalled to base and healed.

Nuances:

All buffs and might changes from spells also remain on the unit

This applies to both Zhonya's and Guardian Angel save effects

question: If an opponent charms my minion into an empty battlefield, do I conquer that battlefield during the opponent's turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you conquer the battlefield during your opponent's turn when they charm your minion into an empty battlefield.

Nuances:

If your opponent charms your unit to an empty battlefield while you have 1 missing point from victory, you don't win the game even if you control the other battlefield

You still draw a card from conquering the battlefield in this scenario

question: If Player 1 plays Dragon's Rage, Player 2 plays Defy targeting Dragon's Rage, and Player 1 plays Mystic Reversal on Defy, what happens?
answer:
Ruling: The player who plays Mystic Reversal gains control of Defy, but since there is only one legal target on the chain (Dragon's Rage) and Defy says "a spell" not "an enemy spell", they must still target Dragon's Rage with Defy.

Nuances:

Mystic Reversal gives control of the spell to its caster, but does not allow retargeting if only one legal target exists

Defy's targeting restriction is "a spell" rather than "an enemy spell", so it can target your own spells

question: When Zhonya's Hourglass is destroyed to prevent a unit from dying, does the unit retain damage marked on it when it is recalled and exhausted?
answer:
Ruling: No, the unit does not retain the damage. Zhonya's Hourglass was errata'd to explicitly heal the unit when it is recalled and exhausted.

Sequence:

Icathian Rain triggers resolve, marking damage on the unit

When lethal damage would be dealt, Zhonya's Hourglass triggers

Zhonya's Hourglass is destroyed instead of the unit dying

The unit is recalled to the base and exhausted

The unit is healed (damage is removed)

question: Can you play a reaction in response to a temporary creature being killed at the start of the beginning phase?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play a reaction in response to a temporary creature being killed in the beginning phase.

Nuances:

Temporary is a trigger that occurs at the start of the beginning phase, which creates a chain that can be reacted to

question: Does Mask of Foresight trigger if you have two units on Reavers Row and use Reavers Row's ability to recall one unit first, leaving the other defending alone?
answer:
Ruling: No, this does not work. When defender triggers happen, they all trigger at the same time based on the game state at that moment. Since both units are defending when triggers are checked, Mask of Foresight never triggers because the unit is not defending alone at that point.

Sequence:

Both units are declared as defenders

All "When You Defend" triggers check simultaneously

Mask of Foresight does not trigger because the unit is not defending alone at this moment

Even if Reavers Row resolves first and recalls one unit, it's too late for Mask to trigger

Nuances:

Mask of Foresight is not a passive effect that continuously checks game state; it only checks when triggers initially occur

You do control the order that simultaneous triggers resolve, but this doesn't help because Mask never triggers in the first place

Attack/defend abilities only activate when a unit is declared attacker/defender for the first time per combat, so recalling and bringing back a unit in the same showdown won't trigger them again

If the opponent recalls their unit with Reavers Row after your unit was already declared an attacker, your unit keeps any buffs from Mask for the rest of combat

question: Can you win the game by gaining the final point through holding a location?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can win the game by gaining the final point through holding a location. The special final point rules only apply to conquering; all other methods of gaining points (holding, card effects, burnout) work normally for the final point.

Nuances:

Conquering is the only method that has special rules when gaining the final point

Holding, card effects, and burnout all function normally when scoring the final point

question: Do triggered abilities from 'on play' effects (like Darius or Ravenbloom Student) trigger when you cast a spell or when it resolves, and what happens if the spell is countered?
answer:
Ruling: Cards are "played" when they resolve, not when they are cast. Triggered abilities from "on play" effects trigger after the spell fully resolves. If a spell is countered (e.g., by Defy), it does not resolve and is not considered played, so it will not trigger any "on play" abilities.

Sequence:

Cast a spell (put it on the chain)

Spell resolves

The spell is now considered "played"

Any "on play" triggered abilities go on the stack

If the chain was empty, this creates a new chain for the triggered ability

Players get priority to respond to the triggered ability

Nuances:

Whether the trigger is on the same chain or a new chain doesn't affect reaction windows - you get a reaction window either way

The term "playing a card" refers to both the act of putting it on the chain and its resolution, but "played" status only occurs upon resolution

Unless something says to do it "as you play", effects happen after resolution

question: If an effect targets exhausted units, does it whiff if the unit becomes ready before the effect resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Effects that are restricted to exhausted units will whiff if that unit becomes ready before the effect resolves. A unit that is exhausted when an effect finalizes is no longer a legal target if it is not exhausted on resolution.

Nuances:

This applies when a unit leaves the play-field and then comes back (it would no longer be exhausted)

The unit must still meet the targeting restriction (being exhausted) at resolution, not just when initially targeted

question: Do Falling Star and Icathian Rain put multiple separate items onto the same chain or separate chains, and when exactly does targeting and damage happen with these spells?
answer:
Ruling: There is only one chain in Riftbound. Falling Star and Icathian Rain create multiple reflexive triggers that are placed as pending items on the same chain after the spell resolves. Targets are chosen and deflect costs are paid when finalizing these triggers to the chain, before they resolve.

Sequence:

Falling Star is played and finalized to the chain

Players can react

Falling Star resolves, creating 2 reflexive triggers as pending items

Targets are picked for both reflexive triggers

Deflect costs are paid for each trigger targeting an enemy unit with deflect

Players can react

First trigger resolves, dealing 3 damage

Players can react

Second trigger resolves, dealing 3 damage

Nuances:

Targets cannot be rechoosen once declared; if a target becomes illegal after selection, that trigger does nothing on resolution

If Retreat is cast before targets are chosen, the opponent can choose different targets; if cast after targets are chosen but before triggers resolve, targeted units can be saved

Players often shortcut by announcing targets immediately when playing Falling Star; if the opponent interrupts this shortcut before targets would be chosen, the Falling Star player can retarget (though there is some debate about the exact interpretation of tournament rules here)

The original Falling Star spell does not target, so no deflect is paid for casting it; deflect is only paid when finalizing the individual triggers

question: If a player forgets to channel runes on their turn, how long do they have to retroactively channel them under the 'full round cycle' rule?
answer:
Ruling: If a player forgets to channel runes on their turn, they can retroactively channel them during the next player's turn, but not on their own subsequent turn.

Sequence:

Player B (second player) forgets to channel runes on their turn

Player B can still channel the forgotten runes during Player A's next turn

Player B cannot channel the forgotten runes once their own next turn arrives

question: Does 6-cost Karma get buffed when you recycle runes to pay for power?
answer:
Ruling: No, Karma does not get buffed when you recycle runes to pay for power because runes are not main deck cards.

Nuances:

"Cards" in card effects refers specifically to main deck cards

Runes, Legends, Battlefields, and Tokens are excluded from the definition of "cards" for card effects

question: If a player responds to an opponent's Action with a Reaction that draws a card, and that drawn card is a Defy, can they still play the Defy against the original Action while it's on the stack?
answer: Ruling: Yes, the turn player can still play Defy against the Action card while it is still on the stack after drawing it from the Reaction's resolution.

question: When Purple Draven moves into Reavers Row and the defending player retreats their only unit using Reavers Row's trigger, does the attacking player score one point for conquering or two points (one for winning combat and one for conquering)?
answer:
Ruling: The precise ruling is not currently known and will be clarified in version 1.2 of the rules.

Nuances:

The interaction depends on the exact wording of rules surrounding 'winning' and 'losing' combat which are not yet finalized

A similar interaction exists that may provide guidance by assumption

question: If P1 is at 7 points with a readied Stalwart Poro in an empty battlefield, and plays Watcher with Accelerate to try to score from both battlefields for the win, can P2 play Gust to bounce the Poro and prevent the loss?
answer:
Ruling: No, P2 cannot prevent the loss at this point. The opponent wins because they don't need to be in control of both battlefields to win - they just need to score a point from both battlefields on the same turn.

Nuances:

P2 should have played Gust during the initial showdown with the Poro at an earlier time to prevent this situation

question: If you use Charm on your turn to move an opponent's unit to an empty battlefield, does the opponent score a point?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the opponent can score a point. When a unit moves to a battlefield not already controlled by that player, a showdown occurs, and if they win the showdown and are able to score on that battlefield, they will score a point.

Sequence:

Unit is moved to a battlefield not controlled by that player

A showdown occurs (non-combat if the battlefield was empty)

If the unit wins the showdown and is still there after, they score

Nuances:

This works even during the opponent's turn (when Charm is used)

Each battlefield can only be scored once per turn, but typically a battlefield won't have been scored yet during an opponent's turn

The battlefield must not already be controlled by the player whose unit is being moved

question: When both the attacker and defender have stunned units, how is combat damage calculated and does the attacker win if they have more total damage?
answer:
Ruling: Stunned units do not deal damage in combat. The attacker had 11 damage (15 minus stunned Lee Sin's 4) and the defender had 10 damage (12 minus stunned Clockwork Keeper's 2). Since neither side can completely eliminate the other's units, this results in a tie, and the attacker's units recall.

Sequence:

Calculate total damage excluding stunned units

Assign combat damage (each side can kill some but not all opposing units)

Because the attacker cannot completely win the fight, the attacking units recall

Nuances:

A combat where both sides have surviving units after damage is called a "tie"

In a tie, the attacker recalls even if they dealt more total damage

question: If you score a battlefield on your turn, then on your opponent's turn they kill your unit and attempt to conquer it, but you play Ride the Wind to win the showdown, do you score the point?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you score the point. You can score a battlefield on your opponent's turn even if you already scored it on your own turn that round.

Nuances:

The only restriction on scoring a battlefield is if you've scored it previously during the same turn (your current turn), not during the same round

question: Does Teemo Strategist trigger when revealed after an opponent moves a unit to his battlefield, or has the window for defend triggered abilities already passed?
answer:
Ruling: Teemo Strategist will still trigger when revealed after an opponent moves a unit to his battlefield.

Sequence:

Opponent moves a unit to Teemo's battlefield

Teemo is revealed from hidden

Teemo gets defender designation during the first cleanup (which happens essentially right away)

Teemo's defend trigger activates

question: When Ahri, Nine Tailed Fox's ability triggers against units attacking from Trifarian War Camp, does Ahri reduce their Might before or after War Camp's buff applies?
answer:
Ruling: Trifarian War Camp's passive applies first, giving attacking units +1 Might before Ahri's ability triggers. Ahri then reduces the buffed units' Might by 1.

Sequence:

Units move to the battlefield and are designated as attackers

Trifarian War Camp's passive immediately applies, increasing their Might (e.g., 1 Might becomes 2 Might)

Ahri's ability triggers on the attacking units, reducing their Might by 1 (e.g., 2 Might becomes 1 Might)

Nuances:

War Camp is a passive effect that applies before triggered abilities like Ahri's

Ahri's ability specifically deals with attacking units, so it triggers after units are designated as attackers at the battlefield

question: Can you equip multiple gear cards to a single unit, or is there a limit?
answer: Ruling: There is no limit to the number of gear cards that can be equipped to a single unit. You can attach as many gear cards as you want to one unit.

question: When do you announce the targets for Dragon's Rage - on cast or when resolving the spell?
answer:
Ruling: Targets are never selected on resolution. Dragon's Rage targets a unit on activation (the unit to be moved and the destination), and then creates a reflexive trigger that targets another unit at the destination.

Sequence:

First part: On activation, target an enemy unit and declare a destination. This moves the unit.

Second part: After the move resolves, a reflexive trigger enters the chain that targets an enemy unit at the previously declared destination to deal damage.

You can respond to either part of Dragon's Rage.

Nuances:

If no move is performed, the reflexive trigger never enters the chain.

To counter Dragon's Rage, move the targeted unit to the destination before the first part resolves - this prevents the move from happening and stops the reflexive trigger from entering the chain.

Moving the unit in response to the first part won't prevent the move if the origin and destination are still different.

A move requires choosing an origin and destination that are different from each other.

If the unit is moved to a battlefield, you can use Flash in response to the reflexive trigger. If moved to your base, Flash will not save the unit.

question: If you move MF (Moonfire), ready a card with her ability, then bounce her and replay her with accelerate, can you move her again and ready another exhausted card?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can move MF, trigger her ability to ready a card, bounce her, replay her, then move her again to ready another card.

Sequence:

Move MF (first time)

Ready an exhausted card with her ability

Bounce MF to hand

Replay MF with accelerate

Move MF again (counts as first time for the new game object)

Ready another exhausted card

Nuances:

When a card is bounced and replayed, it becomes a new game object, so "first time I move each turn" resets

If you have 2 MFs out at the same time, you can trigger both of their abilities

question: If I have 2 Zhonyas on my battlefield and my unit dies, do both trigger and get removed, or can I save one?
answer:
Ruling: When a unit dies with multiple Zhonyas on the battlefield, only one Zhonyas will be used to save the unit. The other Zhonyas will not be wasted.

Sequence:

First Zhonyas trigger resolves and saves the unit

Second Zhonyas trigger has nothing to replace since the unit is already saved

Second Zhonyas remains on the battlefield

Nuances:

This works the same way regardless of whether the Zhonyas are Hidden or not

Even if both triggers are added to the chain, the second one cannot waste itself because the "instead" replacement effect has nothing to replace after the first resolves

question: If I use Dragon's Rage to move an enemy unit from Battlefield 1 to their base (where another unit is), but my opponent uses Flash to move that unit to the base before Dragon's Rage resolves, do the units still damage each other?
answer: The thread does not contain a clear answer to this question. The only response is a link to another Discord thread without any explanation or ruling provided in this thread.

question: Does moving a unit to an opponent-controlled battlefield with Zenith Blade count as attacking, and what happens in combat when the attacker has less total might than defenders but one defender is stunned?
answer:
Ruling: Moving Leona to an opponent-controlled battlefield with Zenith Blade does count as attacking. In the combat scenario described, if both sides have units remaining after combat resolves, the attackers are sent home via retreat.

Nuances:

A unit is considered attacking if it contests a battlefield controlled by an opponent, regardless of whether it arrived via normal move or card effect like Zenith Blade

The retreat rule applies when both sides have units left at the end of combat

question: How many times can you use the repeat mechanic on a single card?
answer:
Ruling: You can pay the repeat cost once per instance of the repeat keyword on a card. A card with one instance of repeat can be repeated once; a card with multiple instances of repeat (either printed or granted by other effects) can be repeated multiple times.

Sequence:

When finalizing a spell to the chain, you choose whether to pay the repeat cost(s)

You must declare all repeats at activation; you cannot pass priority and then decide to repeat later

You pay the cost for each instance of repeat separately

Nuances:

The number next to repeat is the cost to pay, not the number of times you can repeat

Multiple instances of repeat are formatted as separate lines (e.g., "repeat :1Energy:" on one line, "repeat :1Energy:" on another line)

Cards can gain additional instances of repeat from other card effects

question: How does battlefield selection work at the start of the game?
answer:
Ruling: Battlefield selection depends on the number of players and match format. In Best of 1 (Bo1), players select battlefields at random. In Best of 3 (Bo3), each player selects which battlefield to use each match (cannot repeat battlefields in subsequent matches of the same round).

Sequence:

In 1v1 Bo1: Both players select a battlefield at random, and both are used

In 1v1 Bo3: Each player selects which battlefield to use each match

In multiplayer (2v2 or 4 players): Apply Bo1 ruleset (random selection), but the first player removes their battlefield from the game, resulting in 3 battlefields in play

Selected battlefields are placed face up on the battlefield zones before drawing 4 cards

Nuances:

In 4-player games, only 3 battlefields are used, so the first player does not provide a battlefield

The same rule applies to 2v2 format

question: Can Vi cycle her entire discard pile (e.g., 20 cards) to give her +20 might from her ability?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can cycle your entire discard pile to give Vi that much might (e.g., +20 might from 20 cards in discard pile).

Nuances:

The ability is not at Reaction speed, so you must use it before entering a showdown

The ability can only be used on your turn

question: When a defender is removed from a battlefront during combat using Portal Rescue and replayed at base, does the attacker (Darius with Cleave) keep their combat bonus?
answer:
Ruling: The attacker (Darius) keeps the Cleave bonus and survives the Riptide Shark's 6 damage. Combat/showdown continues until both players pass focus in order, not when units are removed.

Sequence:

Portal Rescue removes Riptide Shark from battlefront and replays it at base

Riptide Shark's on-play effect deals 6 damage to Darius

Darius survives because he still has the Cleave bonus (still considered an attacker)

Showdown then resolves and Darius conquers

Nuances:

Showdowns never end automatically, even if every unit is gone

Showdowns only end when both players pass focus in order

As long as effects are being resolved, the showdown continues

question: Can activated abilities on cards be used during an opponent's turn, and what timing restrictions apply?
answer:
Ruling: Activated abilities follow the same timing logic as spells. Abilities with "Reaction" or "Action" speed tags can be used during any appropriate timing window on any player's turn. Abilities with no speed tag can only be used on your own turn outside of combat.

Sequence:

Check if the activated ability has a speed tag (Reaction or Action)

If it has Reaction, it can be used during any reaction timing window on any turn

If it has Action, it can be used during any action timing window (like during a showdown) on any turn

If it has no speed tag, it can only be used on your own turn outside of combat

Nuances:

Different abilities may have different speed tags, so not all abilities on different cards can be used at the same timing

Action speed abilities like Malzahar can be used during showdowns on the opponent's turn when you have priority

question: Do units and gear go on the chain and can they be reacted to when played?
answer:
Ruling: Units and gear enter the chain but skip Execute and Pass after Finalizing, immediately Resolving, so opponents cannot react to them.

Sequence:

Unit/gear is played and enters the chain

It Finalizes

It skips Execute and Pass steps

It immediately Resolves

Nuances:

This applies anytime a unit or gear is played from anywhere at any time

This includes units with hidden being played from hidden as a reaction

Main Deck cards must be recycled randomly (not in an order of your choice)

question: When ganking, if you move your only unit out of a battlefield, can you play a new unit to that now-empty battlefield after the move?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play a unit to a battlefield after your ganking unit leaves it empty. When you no longer have any units at a battlefield, you lose control of it, and you can only play units to battlefields you control.

Sequence:

Your unit ganks and moves to another battlefield

The original battlefield becomes empty

You lose control of that battlefield

You cannot play units there anymore

Nuances:

Standard Move (like ganking) does not use the chain, so you cannot use reactions in response to play a unit

If you move with a spell (like Ride the Wind), you could play a unit with Reaction before the spell resolves, because spells create a chain

question: If a unit with Sett Legend ability is targeted by Charm, then dies to Hidden Blade and is saved by Sett (returning to base), does the Charm still resolve and pull the unit?
answer:
Ruling: The Charm will still resolve and pull Cithria from base to the battlefield. Since Cithria never hit a non-board zone (she went from battlefield to base via Sett's ability), she is still considered the same target and remains a legal target for Charm.

Nuances:

If a unit goes to a non-board zone (like the graveyard) and then returns, it becomes a different object and would no longer be a legal target for effects that targeted the original unit

Base is not a non-board zone, so moving to/from base does not change the unit's identity as a target

This interaction is specific to Sett Legend's ability; units that die and revive through other means (like Phoenix) would be treated as new units

question: When does Deathknell trigger in a combat showdown, specifically regarding whether units like Kog'Maw heal before Deathknell triggers and whether Undercover Agent can play Chompers to a contested battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: The rules do not currently provide sufficient clarity for this interaction. There is no consensus answer.

Nuances:

One interpretation suggests Deathknell triggers after cleanup, meaning units would heal before Deathknell effects resolve

For contested battlefields, if Deathknell triggers after cleanup, the contested status would be cleared and neither player would have control, preventing units from being played there

An alternative interpretation suggests Deathknell goes on the chain during cleanup but finalizes afterwards, potentially allowing Chompers to be played, followed by another cleanup and then control shift

Playing Chompers to a contested battlefield creates a problem where two players would have control simultaneously, which violates the rules

The current rules lack a definitive solution for these edge cases

question: When does Ravenbloom get +1 might when you play spells - immediately when you use the spell or after the spell resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Ravenbloom gets +1 might when your spells resolve, not when you initially use them.

Sequence:

You play a spell

The spell fully resolves

Ravenbloom's trigger goes on the Chain

Both players get priority before the trigger resolves

The trigger resolves and Ravenbloom gets +1 might

This repeats for each spell that resolves

Nuances:

A card is only considered "played" when it resolves, not when initially used

question: Does Yone's ability work with Skyfall (does Yone deal damage when holding with Skyfall equipped)?
answer:
Ruling: Yone's ability does not work with Skyfall because you cannot hold an open battlefield.

Nuances:

Skyfall changes the word "conquer" to "hold" in Yone's ability text

Yone's ability specifically requires conquering/holding an "open battlefield"

Since you cannot hold an open battlefield, the modified ability cannot trigger

question: When Anivia attacks into a defending Ahri, does Ahri's ability trigger before she dies from Anivia's 3 damage?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ahri's ability triggers and resolves before she dies from Anivia's damage.

Sequence:

Attack triggers activate first

Defend triggers activate last

Triggers resolve in reverse order (defend triggers resolve first)

Ahri uses her -2 Might ability

Ahri then dies to Anivia's damage

question: Can a hidden Zhonya be revealed as a reaction to save a unit that is being moved or discarded from a battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, hidden Zhonya can be revealed as a reaction to save units being moved or discarded. Hidden cards have Reaction speed, allowing them to react to any action, and when a gear at a battlefield is revealed it returns to base.

Sequence:

Opponent takes an action that would move or discard your unit (e.g., Charm, Flight or Fight)

You can react by revealing the hidden Zhonya

Zhonya returns to your base

The unit is saved from being moved/discarded

Nuances:

This works even if the unit has already been moved to a different battlefield before you react

A hidden Zhonya at one battlefield (BF1) can be revealed during a showdown at a different battlefield (BF2) to save a unit at BF2

question: Does Blast of Power target a unit on cast or resolution?
answer:
Ruling: Blast of Power targets a unit on cast.

Nuances:

Even though the card doesn't explicitly say "target," any time a unit is mentioned in card text it counts as a target (with some exceptions listed in the core rules)

In Riftbound, "Play" equals "Resolution" which differs from some other card games

question: Do units heal after a combat showdown if one unit is moved away (e.g., via Flash) before combat damage is dealt?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, units heal after combat as long as a combat was started, even if combat damage is skipped or a unit is moved away before damage is dealt.

Sequence:

Combat must be initiated (unit moves to occupied battlefield)

Even if a unit is moved to base during the showdown (e.g., via Flash)

After the showdown closes and after the combat damage step

In the combat resolution step, all units heal

Nuances:

If combat wasn't started (unit moves to unoccupied battlefield for non-combat showdown), units will not heal

Only combat heals units

All units in play heal all damage after combat ends, regardless of which battlefield the combat occurred on or how the damage was dealt

question: With the Patch Rules for Hidden, do hidden cards now target other battlefields?
answer:
Ruling: No, hidden cards that have a targeting choice must choose from that battlefield when played from hidden.

Nuances:

This ruling is confirmed in the FAQ

question: Does Thousand-Tailed Watcher's -3 might effect persist if units are later buffed, or is it a one-time reduction?
answer:
