Two timing notes: the Reaction resolves first (LIFO), so the unit is not yet Empowered while you're responding — an [Empowered][>] dependent ability isn't active yet. And if your reaction removes the unit from the board, the Empower does nothing when it resolves.

question: I play Rampage with the additional cost, to get my unit +2, but opponent cast Gust on the enemy unit I targeted. Does my spell still resolve and I get the +2 on my unit?
answer:
Yes — Rampage still resolves and your friendly unit still gets the +2 this turn.

The +2 instruction only needs your friendly unit, which is still a legal target; the additional cost was already paid, so that part executes normally (Rule 359.3.e.5/e.8). The damage exchange, however, does nothing: the enemy unit is back in its owner's hand, so it can't deal damage to your unit and your unit can't deal damage to it — that part of the instruction is ignored.

question: When can my opponent play Flash in response to Brynhir Thundersong being played?
answer:
Ruling: Your opponent can play Flash after all other triggered abilities have resolved, while Brynhir's "When you play me" lockdown trigger is still on the chain. Brynhir enters play immediately as a unit (it does not linger on the chain), but its lockdown trigger goes on the chain as a separate Pending Item that can be responded to.

Sequence:

Brynhir is played and enters play immediately upon finalization

Brynhir's "When you play me" trigger goes on the chain

If opponent responds with Tideturner from Hidden, it also enters play immediately

Tideturner's "When you play me" trigger goes on the chain above Brynhir's trigger

Tideturner's trigger resolves, swapping with Hwei

Hwei's "When I move" trigger goes on the chain and resolves

Chain now has only Brynhir's trigger remaining; priority passes and opponent can play Flash as a reaction

Flash resolves, then Brynhir's lockdown trigger resolves

Nuances:

Units enter play immediately upon finalization and do not linger on the chain like spells do

The lockdown effect only applies after Brynhir's "When you play me" trigger resolves, not when Brynhir enters play

question: If a unit is being targeted by alpha strike and would die, but then you reveal a temporal breach saving the unit that would have died to alpha strike, do you get to re-choose who alpha strike is targeting?
answer:
No — you don't get to re-choose Alpha Strike's targets.

Temporal Breach banishes the unit, and Banishment is a non-board zone (Rule 56.1). Per the Flash/Repulse ruling, when a target moves to a non-board zone the targeting relationship is severed — Alpha Strike stops targeting that unit, and when Temporal Breach replays it, it's a brand-new game object (Rule 124) that Alpha Strike never chose. It won't take the damage.

At resolution, Alpha Strike just deals its Might in damage split among the remaining original targets. You re-decide the damage split at that moment (Rule 355.14.e), but you can't pick new units that weren't chosen at finalization (Rule 355.15). If the saved unit was the only target, the damage instruction does nothing — no new targets are selected.

question: If Kennen is played from hidden, I can stun units where I want, right?
answer:
No. Kennen's "When you play me... stun a unit" is a play effect, and CR 811.1.d.3 requires play effects of hidden cards to target only units at the battlefield where Kennen was hidden. So if you play him from Hidden, your stun target must be at that same battlefield.

The exception: if Kennen later attacks, that trigger is a regular triggered ability (not a play effect), so it can stun a unit at any location. (FAQ #11770)

question: If I have a Kaisa at a bf with a Back Off hidden, on the next turn my opponent plays a spell to increase the might of the Jayce in the base. Can I react now with Back Off on the Jayce in base?
answer:
No. A hidden Back Off can only choose a target at the battlefield where it was hidden — Jayce is in base, so he isn't a legal target (CR 811.1.d.2).

Timing isn't the problem: since Back Off was hidden on a previous turn, it gained [Reaction] and you can play it in response to your opponent's spell. But when played from Hidden, its "Stun a unit" target must be chosen from among options at that same battlefield, and Back Off has no targeting text that would free it from that restriction. If you want to hit a Jayce in base, you'd have to play Back Off normally from hand instead.

question: If I play Shadowcloaked Lurker with Last Rites, is it reduced by 2 energy?
answer: Yes — but only for the copies that stay in the trash. The Lurker you're playing has already left the trash before its cost is determined, so it can't count itself (FAQ #8430). Each remaining Shadowblade Lurker in your trash still gives [2] off, so with one other copy in trash the cost drops from 5 to 3; with two others, to 1. This works the same whether you play it from hand or from trash via Last Rites (Rule 366.2).

question: Can I still create a sand soldier token using my Azir Legend even though the text says "played" a gear, if I play a gear and my opponent banishes it with Ravenbloom Prefect?
answer:
Yes. The gear was fully played and resolved — Ravenbloom Prefect's "When an opponent plays a gear" trigger only fires after the act of playing has completed (CR 420.4.a), and then it banishes the gear from the board. Banishing it afterwards doesn't retroactively undo that it was played.

Azir's condition ("Use only if you've played an Equipment this turn") is a non-triggered check that looks back at whether an Equipment was finalized this turn (CR 420.4.b) — and once satisfied, it stays satisfied regardless of where that gear ended up. The only thing that would stop it from counting is the play itself being countered (e.g., Defy). Just remember to activate Azir when the chain is fully resolved and the game state is Open again.

question: If I have a unit on a battlefield that states "At the start of your beginning phase, Draw 1," and a unit with the ability that states "When I hold Draw 1," what is the sequence the abilities resolve at the start of turn in relation to gaining a point?
answer:
The "start of Beginning Phase" draw resolves first — before you gain the point. The "when I hold" draw resolves after the point is gained.

Sequence: the Beginning Phase's Beginning Step ("at the start of Beginning Phase" effects, Rule 315.2.a) comes before its Scoring Step, where you Hold and score the point (Rule 315.2.b). So your start-of-phase draw fully resolves, then you gain the Hold point, then the "when I hold" trigger is placed on the Chain and resolves (Rule 383.4.d, FAQ #7628).

Also note: if both draw triggers came from the same event they'd be ordered by their controllers — but these aren't simultaneous, so the fixed step order applies regardless of card choice.

question: If I have only one unit, and my opponent bellows breath. If I flash to the base does my unit still die?
answer:
Yes — your unit still takes the damage and dies (if it has 1 Might).

Bellows Breath targets the units themselves, not their location. The "same location" is a targeting restriction checked when the spell is cast — and with a single target, that condition is always satisfied. Flash moving the unit to base doesn't undo the target; the spell tracks it to the base, which is a valid location, and deals the 1 damage on resolution. (If the unit has 2+ Might it survives with 1 damage marked.)

question: Can you use Akali rouge assasin during an open battlefield and not conquering?
answer:
Yes. Rogue Assassin's [Action] ability can be activated during the open (non‑combat) showdown at the contested battlefield, and moving your unit back to base prevents the Conquer.

When your unit enters an open battlefield, it applies Contested and a Non‑Combat Showdown opens — you, as the player who applied Contested, gain Focus, and in Showdown Open state you may activate abilities with [Action]. Your unit there counts as "a friendly unit in a showdown," so it's a legal target. Once the ability resolves and the unit is at your base, a Cleanup runs, no units remain at the battlefield, control is never established, and Contested is removed — so no Conquer occurs (Rule 348.2, per FAQ #11800). One condition: the ability only works if it's your turn, which it will be since you made the move.

question: Does Master Yi's Legend ability remain applied to the defending unit post combat?
answer:
No — the +2 falls off the moment combat ends.

Wuju Bladesman, Starter's ability is a continuous passive ("While a friendly unit defends alone, it gets +2 might"), not a one-time buff or a lasting trigger. It's rechecked constantly, so the instant the unit stops defending — which happens at the end of the Showdown when Attacker/Defender designations are removed — the condition fails and the bonus is removed. There's nothing that "sticks" after combat, and the same applies mid-combat if a second unit joins the battlefield (FAQ #10141, #3935).

question: If I have Baron out and someone tries to Switcheroo one of my units, after the Switcheroo does my unit get the new might plus the +2 from Baron?
answer:
Yes — your unit keeps Baron's +2 after the swap, but it's already baked into the swapped number, so you don't get it a second time.

Baron's "+2 to other friendly units" is a passive ability, so it keeps applying after Switcheroo resolves (passives don't snapshot). Switcheroo swaps the units' current Might — which already includes Baron's +2 — and applies a fixed +/- modifier for the turn to achieve those totals. So if your unit was at 5 (3 base + Baron's 2) and the enemy's was at 4, your unit becomes 4, which is the enemy's pre-swap Might with Baron's bonus still active (3 + 2 − 1).

One nuance: the swap modifier is fixed for the turn, so if Baron leaves play later, your unit would lose the +2 and drop accordingly (FAQ #2144, #645).

question: If I play Heedless Resurrection on my Baron, and resurrect Soul Gorger, can I play back the same Baron with the onplay from Soul Gorger?
answer:
Yes — this works. The FAQ #9523 restriction only stops Heedless from resurrecting the very unit it killed, because targets are locked in before costs are paid. Here Heedless targets Soulgorger, so that's fine.

Sequence: kill Baron as Heedless's cost (Baron → trash) → Heedless resolves and plays Soulgorger → Soulgorger's "when you play me" trigger goes on the chain and resolves after Baron is already in the trash, so Baron is a legal choice. You still pay Baron's 3 Power cost (Soulgorger only ignores Energy). Baron Pit is already on the board from the first Baron, so Baron's "as you play me" clause won't re-add or re-route him — he enters at the battlefield you control (or Base) that you choose.

question: There's a board of Hwei on player 1 side and an Ashe on player 2 side. Player 2 activates Cull the Weak. Player 1 responds with Flash. Does player 1 get Hwei movement trigger?
answer:
Yes — Flash counts as a move, so Hwei's "When I move" trigger fires and resolves before Cull the Weak.

Chain order matters here: Flash is on top of Cull the Weak, so Flash resolves first and moves Hwei from his battlefield to base — a Move per CR 442. That move generates Hwei's trigger as a new Pending item on top of the chain, so he draws 1, discards 1, and gets his type-based bonus before Cull the Weak ever resolves. Then Cull the Weak has each player kill one of their units — Player 1 can choose Hwei or a different unit, and Player 2 must kill one of theirs (Ashe doesn't interact with this at all). The move trigger doesn't require Hwei to survive; it just needs him to actually move.

question: If I Baited Hook a unit and Soraka keeps it from dying, do I still get to grab a unit off of the Baited Hook?
answer: No. Because Soraka's replacement effect means the unit is never actually killed, Baited Hook has no "killed unit" to reference — so you look at the top 5 cards but can't play any of them, and you recycle all 5 (RiftJudge FAQ #10387; Rule 359.3.e.12). Your original unit stays in base (exhausted and recalled), so you keep it but get no unit off the hook.

question: If the enemy unit is left with 2 might, can I play the Glist and tap to kill?
answer:
No — not by itself. The List gives the unit −2 Might, which just drops a 2-Might unit to 0 Might. A unit at 0 Might doesn't automatically die; it only dies in cleanup if it has damage marked on it (Rule 142.4.b — lethal damage is non-zero damage ≥ Might, so a 0-Might unit needs at least 1 damage marked).

So: if the enemy unit has no damage on it, it survives at 0 Might until end of turn. If it already has any damage marked (even 1), then yes — reducing it to 0 makes that damage lethal and it dies in the next cleanup.

Two extra notes: you must have named that unit's tag when The List was played, or it's not a legal target; and the −2 lasts "this turn," so the unit returns to 2 Might afterward if it survived.

question: If I play Star Crossed from my trash with Fizz, but my opponent defies it, will my Kennen Legend still get empowered?
answer:
No — Kennen's legend will not empower.

Heart of the Tempest's "When you play a card from anywhere other than your hand, empower me" is a triggered ability that fires only when the act of playing the card is completed by its resolution (CR 420.4.a). If Defy counters your Star-Crossed, the card never resolves, so per CR 420.4.a.1 it isn't considered "played" for triggers — so no empower (same principle as FAQ #8491 / #8710 for "when you play" triggers).

Two side notes: the Star-Crossed is still recycled to the bottom of your deck (Fizz's replacement effect overrides the normal trash-on-counter rule), and if the spell had resolved, the legend would have empowered. Non-triggered effects like Legion would still care about it being Finalized — but Heart of the Tempest's trigger does not.

question: Is empower considered an activated ability?
answer:
Yes. Empower is explicitly an Activated Ability keyword (Rule 827.1) — functionally short for "[Cost]: Empower this. Play only if not Empowered" (Rule 827.1.c.1).

So it follows the full activated ability process: you declare it in your Main Phase during an Open State, it goes on the Chain as a Pending item creating a Closed State, and opponents can respond with Reaction cards/abilities before it resolves (Rule 377.3).

One caveat: the Empowered status itself can also be granted by other effects (e.g., "Empower a unit"), which isn't an activated ability — only the keyword is (CR 442, FAQ #11809).

question: How does Unyielding Spirit interact with Glowstone triggered ability?
answer:
Yes — Unyielding Spirit prevents the 5 damage from Glowstone's end-of-turn trigger. Glowstone itself still dies.

Glowstone's trigger ("At the end of your turn, kill this and deal 5 to all units you control") deals damage directly from the ability — the ability is the source of that damage (CR 418.6.b.2). That's "ability damage," so the global prevention from Unyielding Spirit ("Prevent all spell and ability damage this turn") stops it, even if Unyielding Spirit is played in reaction to the trigger.

This is different from fight effects like Challenge, where the units deal the damage and Unyielding Spirit does nothing. The "kill this" instruction is not damage, so Glowstone is still killed by its own trigger.

question: Regarding Zed Legend, can I freely banish cards on my own to empower without needing another card with a banish effect, similar to how destructive can Recycle to gain +1 Might?
answer:
No — you can't banish "for free" to empower Zed. Banishing is a Limited Action: you may only banish cards when a game effect directs you to (CR 428.4). There's no standalone "banish" cost or action like Vi's Recycle cost, and Master of Shadows itself doesn't have one — its activated ability is "Disempower me, [T]: Discard 1, then draw 1," and discarding is not banishing (CR 428.2.b), so it won't trigger the empower.

To empower, you need an actual card effect that banishes a card you own — e.g., a Shadow Clone's attack trigger ("When I attack, you may banish a unit from your trash"), Death Mark's Flow, or other banish effects. Unlike Vi, whose ability lets you pay Recycle as a cost, there's no equivalent self-serve banish here.

question: In a Showdown, I cast a Reaction spell targeting an enemy unit. Since Ezreal, Prodigal Explorer has the REACTION tag, can I chain Ezreal's ability if the targeting condition is met? Can I also chain Vi, Destructive's ability on top of them?
answer:
Yes for Ezreal, no for Vi.

Prodigal Explorer (Ezreal's Legend): Yes — its ability has the [Reaction] tag, so it can be activated during the Closed State while your spell is on the chain. The "chosen twice this turn" condition still gates it: your Reaction spell targeting an enemy unit counts as one of those choices (targeting = choosing), so you need one other qualifying spell/unit-ability choose earlier this turn. Pay the exhaust cost and it resolves on top of your spell (LIFO).

Vi, Destructive: No — her ability ("Recycle 1 from your trash: Give me +1 might this turn") has no [Reaction] or [Action] tag. Plain activated abilities can only be used during your Main Phase in an Open State, not during Showdowns (Rules 145.2, 381), so she can't be chained onto the open chain — or activated anywhere in that Showdown.

question: Do "when I attack" triggers create a chain, such as yellow Ambessa's champion empowered ability?
answer:
Yes. "When I attack" is a Triggered Ability, and all triggered abilities use the Chain (Rule 383.3, 383.4.e).

For empowered Ambessa, Respected and Feared, here's the sequence: the moment she gains the Attacker designation, her empowered "When I attack" ability goes on the Chain as a pending item and the game enters a Closed State (FAQ #11742). While the Chain has items, only Reaction-speed plays are allowed — so your opponent can't interrupt with Action-speed spells. Opponent "when I defend" triggers go on top of yours and resolve first, then reactions can be added in priority order, and finally her trigger resolves (killing an enemy unit there with less Might than her current Might, which includes her Assault 2 bonus while attacking).

Note the two keywords don't merge: Assault is a passive that applies immediately and never uses the Chain (FAQ #5840), while her "When I attack" kill is a trigger that does.

question: If my enemy Bellows Breath my Rengar at a battlefield, does using Flash to change the location of Rengar cancel out Bellows Breath?
answer:
No — Flash does not cancel Bellows Breath.

Bellows Breath targets the units themselves, not the location they're at. "Same location" is a targeting restriction checked when the spell is cast, not on resolution. When Rengar moves to base via Flash, the spell tracks him there, and base is a valid location — so he still takes the 1 damage (FAQ #12002).

One nuance: if Bellows Breath also targeted other units that stayed at the battlefield, the controller picks one location among where the original targets now are and deals damage only to targets there — so Rengar could avoid damage only if the controller picks the battlefield instead. If Rengar is the sole target, he always satisfies "same location" with himself and gets hit no matter where he goes.

question: Can I play Cannon Barrage on an enemy trying to conquer an open Battlefield?
answer:
Yes, you can play Cannon Barrage — but it won't do anything to the conquering unit.

Moving a unit to an open battlefield creates a Non-Combat Showdown (no opposing unit present), and during that showdown you're in an Open State where Reaction cards like Cannon Barrage are legal to play. However, Cannon Barrage only deals damage to "enemy units in combat," and units are only "in combat" once a Combat Showdown begins at a battlefield with opposing units (CR 344.1, 466). In a Non-Combat Showdown there is no Combat, so the moving unit isn't in combat and takes no damage.

So: legal to cast, but it whiffs — the unit will still establish control and conquer when the showdown closes unless you remove it another way (e.g., a spell that deals damage to units at a battlefield, not just those in combat).

question: When a seal is given temporary, can you tap it in response to the temporary trigger and keep the power during your turn?
answer:
You can tap it in response — but the power won't survive to your Main Phase, so you can't keep it.

Seal abilities have Reaction (exhaust: [Reaction] — Add power), so they're legally timed during the Closed State while the Temporary trigger sits on the chain in your Beginning Phase. You tap, the power finalizes immediately, and then the trigger resolves and kills the seal. So yes, you get the 1 power — but your Rune Pool empties at the start of your Main Phase (Rule 316.3), and the Beginning Phase comes before Channel and Draw. The power is wiped long before you'd have anything to spend it on.

The only exception: if some effect during the Beginning/Channel/Draw phases itself has a power cost, you could use it there. Otherwise the tap is wasted — the seal dies either way.

question: Question about Swain Visionary, I play unit, then I conquer and get point, then I play gear and spell, will I plus 1 point?
answer:
No. Swain's "if you've played a non-token unit, a non-token gear, and a spell this turn" is part of his trigger condition, checked at the moment he conquers — so the gear and spell must already be played when the conquer happens. Playing them afterward doesn't satisfy it, and the trigger never fires (Rule 383.2.a.1).

Note that "played" means the cards were finalized (CR 420.4.b), and a card like Patched Porobot can count as both the unit and the gear (FAQ #11866). To get the point, play the gear and spell before the conquer — e.g., during the Showdown if legal timing allows — not after.

question: If I cannot play additional cost to play something like sacrifice, my card go to hand again?
answer:
Yes — if you can't pay the additional cost, the play is cancelled and Sacrifice returns to your hand.

When you start playing a card it moves from hand to the Chain, but you have to pay all costs in step 4 of the play process (killing a friendly Mighty unit here, Rule 357.2). If you can't or won't pay it, the legality check fails and "the actions taken in this process are undone and the action is cancelled" (Rule 358.5) — so the card goes back to hand, no costs are paid, and nothing from the card happens.

Note: Sacrifice's cost is mandatory — if you have no friendly Mighty unit to kill, you simply cannot play it at all. You also can't pay partway and get a partial effect; it's all-or-nothing.

question: If I have resonating strike hidden in a battlefield that I control with 2 units, then another combat showdown starts at the other battlefield I also control. Can I reveal hidden strike and bring a unit from there to the other battlefield where the combat showdown is happening?
answer:
No. When you play Resonating Strike from hidden, the destination battlefield must be the battlefield where the card was hidden — you can't use it to move a unit to the other battlefield where the showdown is happening.

The card's "choose a battlefield you control" choice can be satisfied at the battlefield it was hidden on (it's a battlefield you control), so it must be chosen there (CR 811.1.d.2). The "unit at a different location" choice can't be fulfilled at that battlefield, so that choice is free — but the destination is locked. In practice, revealing it moves a unit from another battlefield (or your base) to the hidden battlefield, not the reverse.

You can still reveal and play it during the showdown at the other battlefield — hidden cards are playable whenever you have priority — it just can't target across battlefields (FAQ #5820, CR 811.1.d.2).

question: Can I use action spell cards on opponent such as Wages of Pain/Bellow's Breath even though I have no units (it's a non-combat showdown right)?
answer:
Yes. A Non-Combat Showdown still counts as a Showdown with an Open State, and you can play Action spells during it even with zero units on board.

The opponent's move to an empty battlefield you don't control applies Contested and stages a Non-Combat Showdown (Rule 344.2). In any Showdown, each player in turn — regardless of whether they have units there — gets Focus and may play Action/Reaction spells (Rules 345, 347; keyword Action per Rule 806.1.b). The mover gets Focus first, then it passes to you, so you'll get your window.

As for the cards: Wages of Pain targets "a unit at a battlefield," and Bellows Breath targets "up to three units at the same location" — the opponent's moved unit is a perfectly legal target. Your lack of units doesn't matter for either spell. Just keep in mind each spell closes the chain once played, so the opponent can only respond with Reactions (FAQ #7200, #2682).

question: If I have Applied Researchers empower and play Shock blast is it free?
answer:
It depends on Shock Blast's printed cost — you pay its cost minus 3 (Shock Blast's own −2 plus Applied Researchers' −1), to a minimum of 0. So it's free if the printed cost is 3 or less; if it costs more, you pay the difference.

Two notes: Applied Researchers' "to a minimum of [1]" only constrains her own discount — Shock Blast's −2 can still take the cost to 0 (apply her discount first for the best result, Rule 356.4.d–e). And once she's Empowered, she satisfies "if you control something empowered" for Shock Blast's own condition. She also knocks 1 [A] off the Power cost. One caveat: "Shock Blast" isn't in my card database, so this assumes the −2 condition text you quoted (FAQ #11897).

question: If my unit dies in Showdown during opponent's turn, can I return it if I hold Altar of Blood?
answer:
Yes — if your unit is at Altar of Blood and it would die during combat (including lethal combat damage during the Combat Cleanup), you can pay [A][A][A] to heal it, exhaust it, and recall it to your base instead. This works on your opponent's turn; you just need the power available in your rune pool.

Two things to note:

You don't need to Hold/control Altar of Blood — the replacement applies to any unit at that battlefield, so it works even if your opponent controls it and your unit is attacking there.

It only replaces deaths "during combat." A kill during a Non-Combat Showdown (conquering an empty battlefield) wouldn't be covered. If multiple units die at once, the turn player decides first whether to pay, then the other player in turn order (Rule 373.1; FAQ #11503).

question: I have Astral Heron on the battlefield. My opponent pushes my battlefield and I react, playing Retreat on my Heron. Does my next card gain the discount?
answer:
No. Heron's "if I'm at a battlefield" is part of its trigger condition, and that condition is checked after your first card of the turn fully resolves — by which point Retreat has already recalled Heron to hand, so the ability never triggers.

The trigger condition is evaluated only after the inciting event is fully processed (Rule 383.2.c). Since Retreat resolves and returns Heron to your hand before the condition check happens, Heron is no longer at a battlefield and the conditional fails. The discount only applies if Heron is still at a battlefield when the first-card trigger is evaluated (FAQ #11610). You'll need to get Heron back to a battlefield and play a first card that doesn't remove it to get the discount.

question: If I play Abandon in response to a card being played from discard through the flow mechanic, does it go back to trash or does it become banished?
answer:
It becomes banished — it will not go to the trash, and it will not even go back to hand despite Abandon's text.

Abandon's "return to hand instead of trash" and Flow's "banish it instead" are both replacement effects modifying the same event (the spell leaving the chain), so the spell's owner picks the order (Rule 372) — but either order ends in banishment. If Abandon applies first, the spell would go to hand, but that still counts as "leaving the chain," so Flow's delayed replacement kicks in and swaps the destination to banishment. FAQ #11690 confirms a countered Flow spell is banished, since Flow's effect covers any departure from the chain except the spell's own execution (Rule 829.1.b.1).

question: For best of 1, when can you sideboard?
answer:
By default, you can't sideboard at all in a standard Best-of-1 — sideboarding is only allowed between games of a match (Rule 403.4), and Rule 403.5 forbids using sideboard cards in the first game, which is the only game in a BO1.

The one exception: the head judge may opt into the altered BO1 setup process, which adds a single sideboard opportunity before game 1 begins (TR 406.1.h.5). Unless the event announced that change, your main deck stays locked for the match.

question: Does Volibear channel a rune exhausted when playing a Mighty card or also when he makes a card Mighty?
answer:
No — Volibear only triggers when you play a unit that is already Mighty at the moment it's played.

Relentless Storm reads "When you play a Mighty unit, you may exhaust me to channel 1 rune exhausted." The Mighty check happens in the trigger condition at the time of play — the unit must have 5+ Might when it resolves and enters play. Making a card Mighty afterward (via a buff, a "When Played" self-buff like Sett, or any later effect) is too late; the trigger window has already passed. Volibear himself doesn't even make cards Mighty — he only channels runes.

A card that enters already Mighty — from a static/passive effect (e.g., Trifarian War Camp) or printed 5+ Might — does trigger him, and the rune does enter exhausted. (Rule 706; FAQ #4060/#1160.)

question: Can Mirror Image be discarded using Decree of Strength?
answer:
Yes — Mirror Image can be chosen by Decree of Strength, but it isn't discarded; it's recycled.

Decree of Strength lets you pick a Mind ([C]) card from your opponent's revealed hand. Mirror Image is a Mind–Order spell, so it qualifies. However, the card doesn't go to the trash — Recycle puts it on the bottom of its owner's Main Deck (CR 417.1.a), whereas Discard is strictly hand → trash (CR 423.1). So the effect works, just with a different destination than "discard."

question: If my opponent has 2 gear in base and plays his Porobot, does he count as the 3rd gear to draw 1, or will there already be 3 gear?
answer:
No. Porobot needs 3 other gear — he doesn't count himself.

His ability reads "if you control 3 or more other gear, draw 1." With only 2 gears already on your Base, playing him gives you 3 gear total, but only 2 other gear — the condition fails and you draw nothing. You'd need a 3rd gear already in play before playing him (so he'd be the 4th).

question: If a Champion conquers a location with no monsters, would it be considered dealing excess damage in respect to something like the effect of "Vi, Piltover Enforcer"?
answer:
No. Conquering a battlefield with no enemy units doesn't assign any damage, so there's no excess damage for Piltover Enforcer.

Excess damage only exists as a concept during the Combat Damage Step — it's the damage you assign to an enemy unit beyond the lethal amount needed to kill it (CR 467.2.c.3–4). That step only happens when both attackers and defenders are present (CR 467.1). Moving to a monster-free location is a Non-Combat Showdown: there's no combat, no damage assignment, and no combat cleanup.

So when your Champion conquers an empty battlefield, Piltover Enforcer's "if you assigned 3 or more excess damage" condition is simply not met — you haven't assigned damage to anything at all. (CR 467.1, 462.2.c)

question: If you move a unit to a combat showdown and have Mask of Foresight, can Akali Rogue Assassin move a unit from combat and then when moved back in that unit trigger Mask of Foresight a second time?
answer:
Yes — in this exact line, Mask of Foresight can trigger a second time, because the unit left the combat entirely and its re-entry starts a new Combat Showdown.

How it works:

Your unit moves in alone → gains Attacker designation → Mask triggers (+1 Might).

Akali, Rogue Assassin's ability moves that unit to base. With no friendly unit left, the Showdown ceases to be staged — that combat is over (no Combat Cleanup since damage was never dealt).

If Akali is Empowered, the unit is readied. It then Standard Moves back to the battlefield → Contested applies again, enemy units are there → a new Combat is staged → a new Showdown begins.

The unit gains Attacker designation "for the first time" in this new combat, and if it's alone again, Mask triggers again.

Mask's trigger is limited to once per unit per combat (FAQ #5044, #5554), but a new combat resets that eligibility — even in the same turn.

Critical caveat: this only works if the first combat actually ends. If other friendly units remain at that battlefield, the Showdown continues, and a unit that leaves and re-enters during the same combat will not re-trigger Mask. Also, the re-entry move needs a ready unit (Empowered Akali readies it) or another effect like Ride the Wind, since you can't Standard Move during a Showdown.

question: If my opponent attacks and puts a 'When I attack' trigger on the chain, when I reveal Mischievous Marai from Hidden as a Reaction, does it stack directly on top of the opponent's existing chain or start a new separate chain?
answer:
Yes — it stacks directly on top of the existing chain. Riftbound allows only one Chain at a time, and any card or ability played while a Chain exists is placed on that same Chain (Rule 330.1–330.2).

Mischievous Marai's Hidden status grants her Reaction, so she's legally playable in the Closed State during your opponent's attack-trigger chain. She's added as a new Pending Item on top — she does not create a new chain — and resolves before the opponent's "When I attack" trigger (LIFO).

One extra wrinkle: once Marai finalizes and enters play at the battlefield where she was hidden, her "When you play me to a battlefield, deal 2 to an enemy unit here" also triggers and goes on that same chain, on top of everything else. Reactions played mid-chain always join the existing chain (FAQ #2952).

question: If my opponent plays Ride the Wind, can I chain a Temporal Breach on a Fizz at the battlefield to play a Hard Bargain from my trash, or would Fizz's play effect be on a separate chain?
answer:
Yes — it all happens on the same chain. Fizz's play effect doesn't start a new chain; it's added as a pending item on the existing chain, and you can use it to play Hard Bargain to counter Ride the Wind.

Here's the sequence: Ride the Wind finalizes → you react with Temporal Breach (Hidden) on top of it → Temporal Breach resolves, banishing Fizz and playing him back to the same battlefield → Fizz's "When you play me" trigger fires during that resolution and is added as a pending item on top of Temporal Breach (CR 402.2 — the chain keeps going). Once Temporal Breach finishes, Fizz's ability finalizes, you choose Hard Bargain (energy 2 ≤ 3) from your trash, and it resolves by playing Hard Bargain onto the same chain — where Ride the Wind is still sitting below it.

Hard Bargain then resolves first (LIFO), targeting Ride the Wind. Your opponent can pay [2] to save it, otherwise it's countered. The chain only ends when everything on it clears, so Ride the Wind can't sneak through in between (Rule 330). One note: when Fizz's ability plays Hard Bargain, it ignores the energy cost but not the Power cost — Hard Bargain has none, so it's free.

question: Does Dazzling Aurora enter the field first before the When You Play Me effect of Soul Gorger resolves? Basically, does Prefect exile Aurora?
answer:
Yes — Aurora enters the field before Soulgorger's "When you play me" effect resolves, so Prefect cannot exile her.

Chain items finalize in the order they were appended, and a Gear resolves immediately upon finalizing (Rule 337.1.b, 337.2). So the order is: Soulgorger enters → Aurora resolves and enters as a Gear → then Soulgorger's WYPM trigger resolves and plays Ravenbloom Prefect from the trash. When Aurora was played, Prefect was still in the trash, and its "When an opponent plays a gear" ability is only active while Prefect is on the board — so it never triggers on this Aurora. Prefect enters after Aurora is already in play, and its trigger doesn't retroactively fire.

question: If my opponent attacks and puts a "When I attack" trigger on the chain, when I reveal Mischievous Marai from Hidden as a Reaction, it has "when you play...", does it stack directly on top of the opponent's existing chain or start a new separate chain?
answer:
Same chain — it stacks directly on top. There's only ever one Chain at a time (Rule 330.1), and anything played or triggered while a Chain exists is added to that Chain as the top item.

Here's how it plays out: your opponent's attack trigger is already on the Chain. You play Marai from Hidden as a Reaction — it's placed on that same existing Chain (Rule 330.2). Since Marai is a permanent, it resolves immediately (you can't react to permanents being played), enters play, and then its "when you play me" effect is put on the Chain as a new Pending Item on top of the attack trigger. Both the attack trigger and Marai's 2-damage effect will resolve from that one Chain, LIFO — so her damage resolves first.

The "new chain" situation you may have seen (FAQ #6244, Tideturner) only applies when the Chain is empty — a fresh play creates a fresh Chain. With an existing Chain in progress, everything joins it.

question: Does Diana Lunari trigger resolve if she gets gusted to hand in response?
answer:
Yes. Once Diana's "When a showdown begins here" trigger is on the chain, Gust only removes her — it doesn't counter her ability, and triggered abilities resolve independently of their source (FAQ #10222; CR 393).

Gust has [Reaction], so your opponent can play it in response to the trigger, but when her ability resolves you can still pay [1], [Predict], reveal, and draw a spell if revealed — her card text doesn't require her to still be in play.

question: When I play Rebuttal, do I have to decide to pay 1 more power to take control of the spell, or will I wait until it resolves?
answer:
You decide when Rebuttal resolves, not when you play it.

When you finalize Rebuttal, you only choose the target spell. The "You may pay [A]" isn't an additional cost of playing Rebuttal — it's a cost within an instruction, paid on resolution (CR 204.3.a). So you play Rebuttal for its printed [1][P], and only when it resolves do you choose whether to pay [A]: pay it and you take control and may make new choices, or decline and it counters the spell.

One catch: the target must still be on the chain when Rebuttal resolves. If something else removes or counters it first, Rebuttal fizzles and you never get the chance to pay — you just keep your runes.

question: When I play Sacrifice to kill my Glasc Mixologist to play Vanguard Captain - will it enable its Legion to play 2 recruit tokens?
answer:
Yes — Sacrifice enables Vanguard Captain's Legion, so you get the two 1[M] Recruit tokens.

Legion checks whether a different card has been finalized by you this turn (Rule 812.1.c), and Sacrifice was finalized when you played it — before Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell even resolves. So when the Deathknell plays Vanguard Captain from your trash, Legion is already active and its "When you play me" makes both Recruit tokens at the location Vanguard Captain entered. It doesn't matter that Sacrifice is still resolving on the chain; even a countered card would satisfy Legion (CR 420.4.b).

question: I play Temporal Breach to a unit at a battlefield a hidden card. If they don't react it now, will the hidden card get discarded or can they play it later after the unit is played again and will they score this turn? This is my turn.
answer:
No — the hidden card stays, and the Breach replay doesn't score.

Your control of that battlefield is never lost during the sequence. While Temporal Breach is on the chain (Closed State), no loss-of-control check happens, and after it resolves your unit is pending on the chain being played back — a pending unit prevents the cleanup from stripping your control (187.4.c, 2026-04-29 FAQ clarification). Since you never lose control, the hidden card is not trashed, and there's no window where it gets discarded. FAQ #11796 confirms this exact line.

The hidden card can be played later as normal — just remember it can't be played the same turn it was hidden (811.1.b); if you hid it on a previous turn, it's available whenever you have priority to play it.

Scoring: replaying the unit does not trigger a Conquer — you never lost and regained control, so no Contested status, no Showdown, no score from the Breach itself. If you already scored that battlefield this turn (e.g., via Hold at your Scoring Step), the once-per-battlefield-per-turn limit means you get nothing more (CR 472). If you haven't scored it yet this turn, you can still Hold it normally at your Scoring Step.

question: How does Switcheroo work with Orrn Forge God with a Sterakos and GA equipped and 7 gears in total against a tentacle token?
answer:
Ornn ends at the Tentacle's Might (1), and the Tentacle ends at Ornn's full current Might — Switcheroo counts every bonus, including Ornn's +1 per friendly gear and each gear's own Might bonus (CR 434).

Math: Ornn = 4 base + 7 (his passive, one per friendly gear) + 3 (Sterak's Gage) + 1 (Guardian Angel) + whatever the other 5 gears grant. If the other 5 grant nothing extra, that's 15. Tentacle token = 1. Switcheroo applies a fixed +14 to the Tentacle and −14 to Ornn, so Ornn = 1 and the Tentacle = 15 for the rest of the turn.

The gear stays attached to Ornn — only the Might values are adjusted. If any gear is killed or removed later that turn, Ornn's Might drops below 1 (treated as 0, CR 143.2.c), since the swap modifier stays fixed. Guardian Angel and Sterak's keep working normally on him.

question: If I play Rumble, if opponent asks me how many might I have on a battlefield, do I have to tell him with or without apply of shield?
answer:
You must give them the unit's current Might — which, outside of combat, is without Shield. Shield is "While I am a defender, I have +X Might" (Rule 814.1.c), so it only adds to Might when the unit actually has the Defender designation. A unit sitting on a battlefield isn't a defender, so its current Might is its printed Might plus any active modifiers (buffs, Assault if attacking, etc.).

Two layers here:

Current Might is public information — you must answer honestly and accurately (TR 502.4.e). Answering with Shield added while the unit isn't defending would be misrepresenting public information.

What Shield would add if the unit became a defender is derived information — you're not required to compute or volunteer that future consequence (Rule 502.5.c; Rule 502.2.b). So you can answer "4 Might" and leave it at that.

If combat is already staged and the unit is actually a defender, then Shield is included in its current Might, and that's the number you report.

question: If I use Stupefy on an opponent's unit that has 2 might while I control an empowered Mel, Newly Awakened, does the opponent's unit get reduced to 1 might or 0 might?
answer:
The unit ends at 1 Might, not 0.

Empowered Mel's ability modifies spells you control that "give −[S]" — so Stupefy's −1 becomes −2 Might. But the "to a minimum of 1 might" clause is part of Stupefy's own effect, so the floor still applies: 2 Might − 2 clamps to 1. This is the same snapshotting principle as CR 479.4.b — the limitation is applied when the reduction is generated, capping it at −1 for the turn. (If Mel weren't empowered, Stupefy alone would also leave it at 1.)

question: Can you use a quick draw gear after both passing focus and before assigning combat damage?
answer:
No. Once both players pass focus in sequence, the Showdown closes and combat proceeds directly to the damage step — there is no priority window to play anything, including a Quick-Draw gear at Reaction speed.

Quick-Draw only grants Reaction timing (Rule 819); it doesn't create a new window where none exists. Since both players passed on an empty chain, no player has Focus or Priority when the Showdown closes, so the gear can't be played before damage assignment (Rules 347.2.a, 348.1; FAQ #6389, #7747).

If your opponent plays anything on the chain before passing, focus returns to you and you'd get your reaction window then — but once both pass, the window is gone.

question: Emperor's Divide can be used to pull back units from multiple battlefields or just one?
answer: No — only one battlefield. Emperor's Divide reads "any number of friendly units at a battlefield" (singular), so you pick a single battlefield and move any number of your units from that one location to base. It can't grab units from multiple battlefields (FAQ #10641). Units moved keep their current Ready/Exhausted state when they arrive.

question: Does Vi, Destructive ability I can use it as often as I want?
answer:
Yes — Vi, Destructive's ability can be used as many times per turn as you can pay for it, since nothing on the card limits the number of activations.

Each activation costs 1 card recycled from your trash, so the only limit is how many cards you have in trash (CR 417.3). Activate once, let it resolve, then do it again — each activation resolves individually and gives +1 Might this turn.

One restriction: this is an activated ability, so it can only be used on your turn, in an Open State (empty chain, no showdown), and your opponent gets a chance to respond between each activation (Rule 381; FAQ #8013). You can't use it at action/reaction speed or during a showdown.

question: Can Frigid Jewel trigger more than once per turn, for example drawing 6 cards?
answer:
No — Frigid Jewel triggers at most once per turn.

Its condition is "when you draw your second card each turn" — there's only one second card per turn. If you draw 6 cards, the ability fires on the 2nd draw and that's it; the 3rd–6th draws don't satisfy the condition. Even if you draw multiple cards at once (e.g., "draw 3"), you pick which one counts as the second and the ability triggers only once (Rule 383.1.b). It resets each turn, so a new turn's second draw can trigger it again.

Per FAQ 10414, the only thing that matters is which draw is the second one that turn — everything after is irrelevant.

question: If I play Kennen from Hidden, can I stun a unit in a different location?
answer:
No. Kennen's "When you play me... stun a unit" is a play effect, and Hidden restricts play-effect targets to units at the battlefield where Kennen was hidden (CR 811.1.d.3) — so the stun target must be at that same battlefield.

The exception: if Kennen later attacks (played normally, not from Hidden), that trigger is a regular triggered ability, so it can stun a unit at any location. (RiftJudge FAQ #11770)

question: If Blue Nasus and another unit trade on a Showdown, does the Blue Nasus trigger and channel 1 Rune Exhausted?
answer:
No — Nasus's ability does not trigger.

Nasus, Guardian of Knowledge's trigger is "once each turn, when an enemy unit here dies." When he and the enemy unit both take lethal damage, they're killed together in the same combat cleanup step (CR 323.4). Since Nasus leaves the board at the exact same instant the enemy unit dies, he can't evaluate his own trigger condition — Rule 383.2.c.2 says a triggered ability fails if its source leaves the zone it's active from at the same time the condition is met (same as the Viktor, Leader example). He has to be alive when the enemy dies. (FAQ #11803)

question: If my opponent plays Fizz to use Hidden Blade targeting my Kayle, can I play Disposable Orders to remove the Hidden Blade from trash before Fizz uses it?
answer:
Yes. You can respond to Fizz's "When you play me" trigger with Disposal Order and recycle the targeted Hidden Blade — once it leaves the trash, Fizz's ability has no valid target and its instruction to play the spell is ignored (Rule 359.3.e.7; FAQ #10771).

Timing detail: Fizz's target is declared when his trigger is put on the Chain, so you'll know Hidden Blade is the target before you respond. Since Disposal Order is a Reaction, you may play it while the state is Closed. If you recycle Hidden Blade, it goes to the bottom of your opponent's deck and never gets played — Kayle won't be killed, and no draw 2 for your opponent.

question: When Lightning Rush looks at the top 3 cards and I see Undertitan, does that add 2 energy?
answer:
No. Lightning Rush says "Look at the top 3 cards," and looking is not revealing — Undertitan's energy ability only fires when an effect explicitly uses the word "reveal" (RiftJudge FAQ #4282/#251).

Same as Hook and Baited Hook: you can choose and draw the Undertitan, but you get no [2] Energy from it. Only effects that literally say "reveal" (like Rift Herald's move trigger) will set it off.

question: If I have a Stellacorn and Zhonya's Hidden on one battlefield, and I have Irelia and a Tideturner Hidden on another, if an opponent starts a showdown on the first battlefield, can I Ride the Wind my Irelia into the other battlefield while activating Tideturner to move my Stellacorn while keeping my Zhonya's Hidden?
answer:
Yes — the whole line is legal, assuming Stellacorn and Irelia are actually in play (not hidden).

During the showdown at BF A, Ride the Wind is an Action, so it's playable in the Showdown Open State — it moves Irelia from B to A and readies her (joining the ongoing showdown is fine; the "no moving into combat" restriction only covers combat you're not in). Then you can play Tideturner from hidden at B — it enters at B, and its "when you play me" trigger may target Stellacorn at A because Tideturner is the explicit exception to Hidden's same-battlefield targeting (CR 811.1.d.3). Resolution: Tideturner → A, Stellacorn → B, and Stellacorn's "when I move, draw 1" fires. Zhonya's stays facedown the whole time — nothing forces it to flip.

Two catches:

You can't have two hidden cards on one battlefield. Only one facedown card can be hidden per battlefield (Rule 811.1.b), so "Stellacorn and Zhonya's hidden at A" (and "Irelia and Tideturner hidden at B") is an illegal setup. Stellacorn and Irelia must be in play — Tideturner can't swap with a facedown card that isn't a unit yet.

Sequencing: each play opens its own chain, so you need two windows — either two Focus turns in the Showdown Open State, or play Tideturner as a Reaction while something is on the chain. And if you end the showdown with no units at A, you lose control and the hidden Zhonya's goes to trash — you keep it only while you still hold A.

question: Does Divine Judgment recycle trash and banish cards?
answer:
No — Divine Judgment only touches the card types it names: units, gear, and runes on the board, plus cards in hand. Cards in the trash or in banishment are not among the "rest" and stay exactly where they are.

The same logic is why hidden cards are unaffected: they aren't units, gear, runes, or hand cards, so they're neither chosen nor recycled (FAQ 7410).

question: Can you just exhaust Irelia without moving her?
answer:
No — you can't just exhaust Irelia without moving her.

Exhausting is a Limited Action that only happens as a cost for an action/ability or when a card effect tells you to (CR 415.3). The Standard Move is the only generic exhaust you have, and there "exhaust" is the cost while actually moving is the effect — per CR 415.4, the cost can only be paid if the action can be completed, so you can't declare a move and skip it. There's no free "exhaust this unit" action, and note it wouldn't help anyway: Irelia, Fervent triggers on being chosen or readied, not on being exhausted.

question: Does Red Akali deal marked damage when combined with Akali's Champion ability?
answer:
Yes — when the Akali legend (Rogue Assassin) moves Akali, Deadly Weapon out of a showdown, her "When I move" trigger fires and deals real damage: 1 (or 2 if she's Empowered) to a unit at the battlefield she moved from. That damage is marked on the unit as damage counters and counts as damage marked by you (CR 142, 418.1.b).

Two quick caveats:

The damage amount depends on Akali, Deadly Weapon's Empowered status, not the legend's. Empowered legend just lets the moved unit ready.

The trigger resolves after the move completes, before any cleanup/heal window — so the damage stays marked and can finish off an already-damaged unit (FAQ #11755).

question: Does Shuriken Flip cause the unit to exhaust?
answer:
No — Shuriken Flip moves the unit without exhausting it.

Exhaustion is only the cost for a unit's Standard Move (Rule 144.2). Moving via a spell effect is not a Standard Move, and Shuriken Flip's text doesn't instruct you to exhaust the unit, so it keeps its current ready/exhausted state (see also FAQ #3678 for the same principle). The moved unit will, however, enter exhausted if it's a fresh unit being played — but that's unrelated to the spell.

question: If I move to an enemy battlefield with Twilight Reveler and use Akali Champion ability to bring it back, is the card still considered an attacker?
answer:
No — once Twilight Reveler is moved back to base, it is no longer an attacker.

Twilight Reveler gained the Attacker designation when combat opened at the enemy battlefield (CR 466.2.c.3), but the designation is tied to that combat. When Akali's ability moves it to base, it no longer occupies the battlefield where combat is ongoing, and the designation is removed during the ensuing cleanup — a unit is only "in combat" if it occupies that battlefield and has a combat designation (2026-03-30 rules clarification). Same principle as FAQ #1920: leaving the combat battlefield drops the combat designation.

One nuance: Twilight Reveler's "When I attack" trigger has already fired the moment it gained the designation, and it will still resolve normally even though the unit is now at base — triggered abilities are independent of the source's current state. If it was the only attacking unit, moving it out also unstages the combat at that battlefield.

question: Can I use Akali champion to trigger Mournfull Witnesses?
answer:
Yes. On your turn you can activate the Akali legend (Rogue Assassin) ability to move Mournful Witness out of an ongoing combat to your base, and that ends the combat — Mournful Witness's "when a combat that I was in ends" trigger fires and it becomes Empowered.

Key points:

The trigger is a historical check (FAQ #11725): as long as Mournful Witness had already gained an Attacker or Defender designation in that combat, moving it to Base doesn't erase that it was in the combat. When the combat is unstaged during the Cleanup after the move (FAQ #11755), the trigger fires.

It must be an actual Combat Showdown (opposing units present). If Mournful Witness is just in a Non-Combat Showdown over an empty battlefield, there's no combat to end, so no trigger.

The Akali legend ability needs "it's your turn" and targets "a friendly unit in a showdown" — so Mournful Witness (or any friendly combatant whose departure ends the fight) works. If other friendly units remain at that battlefield, the combat doesn't end yet; the trigger will fire when the combat finally does end.

question: If I counter a spell with Defile and my opponent counters my Defile with Abandoned and sends it to my hand, can I let Abandoned resolve and recast my Defile on the original target?
answer:
Yes — assuming you mean Defy (there's no card named "Defile"), you can let Abandon resolve and then recast Defy on the original spell.

The chain resolves one item at a time (LIFO), not all at once. After Abandon resolves and returns your Defy to your hand, a priority window opens before the original spell resolves (Rule 340.1; FAQ #9457). Since Defy is a [Reaction] spell, you may play it during that window to target the original spell again, which is still on the chain.

One caveat: the new Defy must still have a legal target — the original spell must still be on the chain and meet Defy's restriction (printed cost of 4 or less energy and no more than 1 power). If it still qualifies, your recast Defy resolves and counters it.

question: If I play Draven Glorious Executioner, do I win a combat and draw a card if an enemy unit is pushed back by the ability of Overzealous Fan?
answer:
No. When Overzealous Fan kills itself to push your attacking unit back to Base, both players end up with zero units at the battlefield, so the combat result is "No Result" — not a win for you — and Glorious Executioner's "When you win a combat, draw 1" does not trigger.

Per CR 468.3.d, if neither player has units present during the Determine Combat Result step, the result is No Result, and the battlefield becomes Uncontrolled (CR 468.5.b). Since you didn't win the combat, no card is drawn.

question: Can I use Whirlwind or King's Edict to target Baron?
answer:
Yes — both can hit Baron Nashor.

Neither spell targets or "chooses" units itself. Whirlwind and King's Edict both instruct players to make choices during resolution, and per Rule 355.10.e those player-made choices are not targeting. Since Baron's protection only blocks being chosen by enemy spells and abilities (not by players resolving them), he's a legal choice for both (FAQ #10445, #509, #8959). In a 1v1, King's Edict means your opponent simply must pick Baron and he gets killed.

question: If combat is resolving, I have a 5 might unit, and the enemy has a 7 might unit and a 4 might unit, can I assign my damage to the 7 might unit or do I have to assign lethal damage to the 4 might unit?
answer:
Yes — you can put all 5 damage on the 7 Might unit. Nothing forces you to kill the 4 Might unit first.

The lethal-damage rule (465.2.c.3) only prevents overkilling: you must fill one unit to lethal before moving to another, and can't assign more than lethal to a unit while others remain. It never requires you to kill every possible target. So 5 damage on the 7 Might unit is fine — it just survives with 5 marked.

What you can't do is split 2 and 3, or dump all 5 onto the 4 Might unit (that would overkill it while the 7 Might unit takes nothing).

question: Does Mel and Ambessa Legends trigger on the same chain you empower a unit? For example, I empower a unit, it goes on the stack, and then Mel Legend triggers, that goes on the stack and will resolve first before the unit's empower trigger?
answer:
No — it's the opposite order. The unit's Empower resolves first; Mel (Soul's Reflection) and Ambessa (Matriarch of War) only trigger after that, on a fresh chain.

"Empower this" is the effect of the activated ability — it happens when the Empower resolves, not when you activate it (Rule 827.2, FAQ #11993). The legends' "When you empower something else" condition is evaluated only after that inciting event is processed (Rule 383.2.c), so they can't join the chain on top of the Empower. The unit becomes Empowered, then both legend triggers fire simultaneously and go on the new chain — you choose their order (Rule 383.3.d), and they resolve one at a time.

One edge case: if a reaction removes the unit before the Empower resolves, the Empower does nothing — no empower event occurs, and neither legend triggers. Also note "something else" means empowering the legend itself doesn't trigger that legend's own ability, though the other legend would still trigger.

question: I have tapped legend LeBlanc and then conquer Hall of Legend battlefield, can I trigger Hall of Legend first to ready my legend and then use her ability?
answer:
No — if LeBlanc is already exhausted when you conquer Hall of Legends, her Deceiver trigger never enters the Chain at all.

"Exhaust me" is a cost paid to finalize the trigger (Rule 383.3.b), and an already-exhausted Legend can't be exhausted again to pay a cost (CR 415.1.b, 415.4). So Hall of Legends' "ready your legend" trigger is the only one that fires — it readies her after the fact, but the conquer trigger window for Deceiver has already passed. This is the same interaction as Rek'Sai (FAQ #11259).

If LeBlanc is ready when you conquer, both triggers fire simultaneously and you can order them freely — e.g., Hall of Legends resolves first, then Deceiver exhausts her and plays the Reflection.

question: When Bottled Constellation triggers and I have Patched Porobot on my board, is it possible that the Patched Porobot counts as 2 of these 3 needed to kill to trigger the Bottled Constellation?
answer:
No. Patched Porobot counts as one of the three kills, not two.

Bottled Constellation requires you to kill 3 game objects that are friendly units and/or gear. Patched Porobot is a single game object with both card types (Rule 178), so it's a valid choice for the kill — but it still satisfies only one of the three kills. This is a quantity check (3 objects), unlike Swain's existence check where one dual-type card could satisfy two separate yes/no conditions.

So killing Porobot leaves you needing 2 more friendly units and/or gear to pay the cost. Note "other" also means you can't count Bottled Constellation itself.

question: For rebuttal, to take control of it, do I pay the power on resolution or to put it on the chain?
answer:
On resolution — not when you put it on the chain.

You play Rebuttal for its printed [1][P]. The "You may pay [A]" is a cost within an instruction paid when Rebuttal resolves, not an additional cost of playing it (FAQ #12038). When it resolves you choose: pay [A] and take control (making new choices), or decline and counter the spell.

One catch: the target spell must still be on the chain when Rebuttal resolves — if it's countered or removed first, Rebuttal fizzles and you keep your runes.

question: For Ravenbloom Conservatory, opponent moves into that open bf. I play Ride the Wind to move my unit into Ravenbloom where he is attacking. Do I get the "when you defend" trigger?
answer:
No — you don't get the trigger. The battlefield has no Controller during the Showdown, so "you" in "When you defend here" refers to no one, and the ability stays dormant.

Control is only established at the end of a Showdown (Rule 348.2.a). Since Ravenbloom Conservatory was open (uncontrolled) when your opponent moved in, it remains uncontrolled while Contested — even after your Ride the Wind brings a unit in as the Defender. "You" in a battlefield's ability refers to its Controller (Rule 190.6.d), and with no Controller, the "when you defend here" condition can't be met by either player. This is the exact interaction covered by FAQ #8647, just with the roles flipped.

question: When my opponent plays Promising Future and reveals dazzling aurora, can I reveal thermobeam to destroy it, or will it resolve in such order that aurora will be played after thermobeam resolves?
answer:
Yes — a Thermo Beam played through Promising Future will kill Dazzling Aurora, but Aurora still enters play first. There is no response window to a permanent being played: gears and units finalize immediately and leave the chain (Rule 359.2), so you can't destroy it "before it's played."

Here's the order: "starting with the next player," you play first. Thermo Beam goes on the chain first but, as a spell, lingers as a finalized item while Aurora (a permanent) finalizes and enters play — then Thermo Beam resolves and kills all gear, Aurora included (Rule 359.3.b). Timing isn't an obstacle either: cards played as part of an effect like Promising Future ignore normal Action/Reaction timing restrictions (RiftJudge FAQ #4658). If you instead meant playing Thermo Beam from hand in response — that isn't possible: it's Action speed and permanents don't linger on the chain for reactions.

question: Can Rebuttal counter or take control of Starfall?
answer:
Yes — Rebuttal can target Falling Star (there's no card named "Starfall" in the database; if you mean the Fury spell Falling Star, it has Energy cost 2, which is within Rebuttal's "no more than [4]" limit).

When Rebuttal resolves, you choose then: pay [A] to take control of Falling Star and make new choices for it (you can retarget either or both "Deal 3" instances, including onto the opponent's own units), or decline and simply counter it. You don't have to commit to the [A] when you play Rebuttal — it's a cost paid on resolution (FAQ 12038).

One catch: Falling Star must still be on the chain when Rebuttal resolves — if it's already been countered or removed, Rebuttal fizzles and you keep your runes.

question: Gangplank Naval, if I use Starcrossed, can they use their ability? Will they get +3 and do they need to pull back to hand? Or can they stay at the same battlefield? It says "or put to hand," so you don't need to, right?
answer:
Yes — if Gangplank is already Empowered, he stays on the board and gets +3 Shield this turn instead of being bounced.

His Empowered ability is a mandatory replacement effect: if a spell that chooses him would return him to hand, that doesn't happen — he gets +3 [S] (Shield 3, i.e., +3 Might while defending) for the turn instead (Rule 814, FAQ #11914). Star-Crossed does choose him (choosing = targeting), so the replacement applies automatically. The Gangplank player doesn't activate anything — it just happens, and there's no choice to "use" it or decline it.

To be clear: Star-Crossed has no "or put to hand" option — it always returns both chosen units to hand. It's Gangplank's ability that swaps the bounce for the +3, so he stays right where he is. The other unit Star-Crossed chose still returns to hand as normal. One caveat: if he's not Empowered yet (or if Star-Crossed resolves before an Empower on the chain does), he bounces like any other unit.

question: Does Ki Barrier stack with each other?
answer:
Yes — two Ki Barriers stack, giving the unit a combined 14 damage prevented this turn.

Each Ki Barrier creates its own separate Prevent pool (Prevent 7) tracked on the unit (CR 438.1.b.1). When damage would be dealt, both replacement effects apply in the order you choose (Rule 372), so the first pool absorbs up to 7 damage and the second absorbs whatever remains, up to another 7. CR 438.5.a also confirms the game considers "the Prevent Value of all Prevent Actions on a Unit" together when calculating lethal damage. Unused prevent value from the second copy carries over normally if the first is fully spent.

question: Can I destroy a non Chaos Gear with decree of unity?
answer: No — Decree of Unity can only kill a Chaos gear. Its text reads "Kill an enemy Chaos ([C]) unit or gear," so a non-Chaos gear (e.g., a Calm or Order gear) doesn't meet the targeting requirement and can't be chosen (Rule 355.6). Chaos gear, on the other hand, is a perfectly legal target — Gear are Killable per Rule 148.1.a.4.

question: If I have Rengar Trophy Hunter with a buff (7 might) does he die when targeted by Singularity followed by a Stupify?
answer:
Yes — Rengar dies.

With the buff he's at 7 Might. Singularity marks 6 damage on him (6 < 7, so he survives that alone), but when Stupefy resolves afterward it reduces his Might to 6 while the 6 damage is still marked. Lethal damage is checked whenever a chain item resolves: 6 damage ≥ 6 Might, so he's killed (FAQ #4751). The order doesn't matter — even if Stupefy resolves first, Singularity's 6 damage still makes the kill. If Stupefy never resolves, he'd survive at 7 Might with 6 damage marked.

question: If a move into an open battlefield with Irresistible Faefolk and use her ability to pull in Fiora Peerless, does she get the bonus from her ability?
answer:
Yes, Fiora, Peerless gets her bonus.

When Faefolk moves to the open battlefield, you applied Contested and are the attacker (FAQ #11891, CR 461.2.b.1). Faefolk's trigger resolves, pulling Fiora in, and she gains the Defender designation when the Combat Showdown begins. At that exact moment the battlefield holds only Faefolk and Fiora — one on one — so her trigger fires and doubles her Might (3 → 6) for that combat. Fiora's "one on one" condition is checked only at the moment she's designated (FAQ #1102, #11502), and here it's satisfied.

question: Can I attach Spinning Axe to my unit after my unit dies even though it's not my turn?
answer:
No — you can't re-attach Spinning Axe on a turn that isn't yours.

[Equip] is an activated ability, and activated abilities can only be used on your own turn, in an Open State (chain empty, no Showdown) — Spinning Axe's Equip doesn't have Reaction, so it doesn't get special timing. Also note the Axe doesn't return to your Base immediately when the unit dies: it detaches and stays at the battlefield until the next Cleanup Recalls it. So on your turn, once the chain is empty and the Axe is at your Base (after that Cleanup), you can pay its [A] Equip cost to attach it to another unit you control.

Rule 381 (activated abilities on your turn, Open State only) and CR 459.1 (unattached gear recalled next Cleanup).

question: About Temporal Breach, when I banish a friendly unit, must I play it immediately or can I wait to play it anytime?
answer:
No — the play-back is immediate, part of Temporal Breach's resolution. You can't bank the banished unit and play it at a later time.

Temporal Breach reads "Banish a unit, then its owner plays it to the same location, ignoring its cost." The "then" instruction executes right after the banish during that same resolution — the unit goes straight from Banishment to pending on the Chain and is finalized to the same location (entering exhausted, unless you pay Accelerate). There's no point where the unit sits in your Banishment waiting for you to choose to play it later.

The only way the play-back doesn't happen is if the instruction is impossible — e.g., the location can't accept units (Rockfall Path), the unit is a token (it ceases to exist in Banishment), or a mandatory additional cost can't be paid. In those cases the instruction is negated and the unit stays banished (Rule 359.3.e.6); you still don't get to play it later.

question: If I control an empowered blue mel, can my opponent rebuttal a spell of mine?
answer:
Yes — your opponent can Rebuttal your spell even with an Empowered Mel, Newly Awakened on your side.

Mel's protection ("Your spells and abilities can't be countered") only stops the counter part of Rebuttal — it doesn't make your spell unchoosable, and Rebuttal's targeting only checks Energy cost (≤[4]). So Rebuttal is legal.

The key is what happens on resolution: Rebuttal's controller chooses whether to pay [A]. If they pay, they take control of your spell and may make new choices for it — that's a control change, not a counter, so Mel does nothing to stop it. If they decline to pay, the "counter it" instruction is simply ignored ("can't beats can," Rule 54) and your spell resolves normally.

So Empowered Mel saves you from the fallback counter, but not from having the spell stolen.

question: If I play Timewarp, do I get a point for holding on my extra turn?
answer:
Yes — your Time Warp extra turn is a full turn, so you go through your Beginning Phase and score holding points for each battlefield you control that you haven't already scored this turn (Core 735, 315.2.b.2).

Key point: the extra turn is a new turn, so the "once per battlefield per turn" scoring limit resets (Core 470). Your opponent, whose turn got pushed back, gets nothing — holding only happens during the holder's own Beginning Phase (FAQ #8241). One caveat: you still need to control the battlefield on that extra turn's Beginning Phase to hold it.

question: Can I use spells without the keyword Action and Reaction during my opponent's turn?
answer:
No. Spells without Action or Reaction can only be played during your own turn, in an open state with nothing on the chain — never on your opponent's turn.

To play a spell while it's not your turn, it must have Reaction (lets it be played in a closed state on any player's turn, e.g., responding to a chain) or Action (lets it be played during a Showdown on any player's turn). A spell with no timing keyword has neither permission (Rule 155; Rule 806.1.b; Rule 813.1.c.1).

question: Can I play spells with flow keywords like Perfect Execution during my opponent's turn?
answer:
No — Flow doesn't change when you can play a spell, only where from (your trash instead of your hand).

Perfect Execution has no Action or Reaction keyword, only Flow, so it's a "base speed" spell (Rule 155): it can only be played during an Open State on your turn outside a Showdown. Rule 829.1.b.2 is explicit that playing for the Flow cost doesn't alter timing permissions.

So on your opponent's turn you can't play it — not even during a Showdown, since that requires the Action keyword. For contrast, a spell like Defy (which has Reaction) can be played from your trash via Flow on your opponent's turn, but only in response to a Chain item or during a Showdown.

question: Does Akali Deadly Weapons move trigger create a window for me to play actions before the showdown?
answer:
No — Akali's "When I move" trigger doesn't create an Action window before the showdown; only Reactions can be played while her trigger is on the chain.

Here's the sequence: the move completes, a Cleanup runs, and Akali's trigger is placed on the Chain — that's a Closed State. While a chain exists, only Reaction cards/abilities are playable; Action spells require an Open State (FAQ #2235, FAQ #9306). Once her trigger chain empties, another Cleanup runs and the Showdown/Combat is staged immediately — there's no Open State in between.

Your first chance to play an Action comes after the Showdown is open and you have Focus. Since Akali's controller applied Contested, they get Focus first (Rule 345) — if you're the defender, you act once they pass or their chain empties, which is already inside the showdown, not before it.

question: Do units heal after a non-combat showdown and what is a non-combat showdown?
answer:
No — units do not heal after a non-combat showdown.

A non-combat showdown is a showdown opened at a Contested battlefield where units controlled by different players are not present (Rule 344.2) — e.g., you move a unit into a battlefield you don't control and there are no enemy units there. If units of opposing players are present, the showdown opens as a combat showdown instead (Rule 344.1).

Healing only happens in two places: during Combat Cleanup (which occurs only after a combat showdown, CR 463) and at the end of each player's turn. Since a non-combat showdown has no Combat Cleanup, it heals nothing — even units that were at Base or other battlefields stay damaged until end of turn (FAQ #11781, #9726).

question: On my Hwei ability, can I draw a Porobot and float 2 energy before discarding a Porobot to get two free energy?
answer:
Yes — with the right timing. You can't interrupt Hwei's ability mid-resolution, but you can float before it resolves.

Here's the line that works:

Hwei moves → his "When I move" trigger goes on the Chain (Closed State) and you have priority.

In response to the trigger, exhaust 2 ready runes to float 2 energy (runes can be exhausted whenever you have priority — FAQ #2353).

Hwei's ability then resolves as one uninterrupted effect: draw 1, discard 1 (you pick the Porobot you just drew — CR 423.1.a), and since Patched Porobot is a Gear, you ready up to 2 runes — including the ones you just exhausted.

Net result: 2 floating energy and those runes ready again. What you can't do is draw the Porobot, exhaust runes, then discard mid-resolution — once Hwei's effect starts resolving it completes in full (CR 340.1, 402.2); you'd only be able to add resources mid-resolution if the effect made you pay a cost (Rule 357.1.a), which it doesn't.

One correction: the energy isn't conjured out of thin air — you're exhausting your own runes and Hwei refunds their readiness. Your pool keeps the 2 energy until end of turn (or the draw phase if this happens early), so spend it before then. Also note Porobot is Unit and Gear, so it also satisfies the Unit branch (+3 Shield) under the natural reading of the type check.

question: I have two units in base, and my opponent has two units in base. My opponent casts Star Crossed targeting one of my units and one of theirs. I cast Rebuttal, and take control of Star Crossed. Can I reselect only the "enemy unit" portion of Star Crossed to target my opponent's other unit? If so, do one or two units return to their hand?
answer:
Yes — you can end up with the opponent's other unit targeted, and two units total go to hand (one yours, one theirs).

When you take control of Star-Crossed via Rebuttal, "friendly" and "enemy" are re-evaluated from your perspective. Your originally-targeted unit is still a legal "friendly unit" for you, so you may re-pick it and choose your opponent's other unit as the "enemy unit." Rule 753 requires you to remake all of a finalized spell's choices, though, even if you make the same choice that was previously made — you can't remake just one.

You cannot choose only an enemy unit, though: Star-Crossed's "a friendly unit and an enemy unit" is mandatory, so the friendly slot must stay filled (one of your units). On resolution, both chosen units return to their owners' hands — your unit to your hand, and the opponent's other unit to theirs. That's 2 units returned (one per player), not 1.

question: I have two units in base, and my opponent has two units in base. My opponent casts Star Crossed targeting one of my units and one of theirs. I cast Rebuttal and take control of Star Crossed. Can I essentially bounce two of their units back by only reselecting, switching the target on my friend unit to their other unit?
answer:
No — when you gain control of Star-Crossed, "friendly" and "enemy" re-anchor to you as the new controller, so you still must choose one of your own units and one of your opponent's.

You may make new choices and can switch either target (e.g., bounce your other unit and your opponent's other unit), but both mandatory targets must be legal relative to the spell's current controller — that's you. One target has to be a unit you control (Rule 740.1), so you can never make both targets your opponent's units.

If you decline to retarget, the original targets stay and the spell just resolves normally: one of your units and one of theirs each return to their owner's hand — a trade, not a two-for-one.

question:
Looking at these two key rulings, I can see the distinction: a spell that fizzles due to invalid targets is still considered played because it completed the full play process, which means "when you play" triggers will fire. But a countered spell never finishes that process, so it doesn't count as played and won't trigger those effects. This means I should increment the cards played counter at the moment of play, before any resolution happens.
The regulations are clear, and they partially refute the obvious repair:

350.1 — "A card is played when it has finished this process in its entirety."
359.3.e.10 — a spell whose targets all become invalid "has no effect but is still considered played" — and the example is literally "When you play a spell, give me +1 [M]".

So: countered = never played, but target removed = played anyway
answer:
Your conclusion is correct — countered = never played, fizzled-by-invalid-targets = still played — but the timing model is not. Riftbound does not count a card as played when it hits the chain; per Rule 350.1, a card is only "Played when it has finished this process in its entirety," and for a spell that means actually resolving.
